people.name: Mariana Defranceschi
notes: Wife of Joannes Baptista (casa 36); recorded as "Mariana ejus uxor" in the

**⚠ THREE OF THE SIX CHILDREN OF THIS HOUSEHOLD NOW NAME A DIFFERENT MOTHER, AND NONE NAMES HER.** *The baptism register gives* **Catharina née Jablich of Buccari** *as the mother of* **Josephus Antonius (1785)**, **Catharina (1786)** *and* **Maria Rosalia (1789)**. *Catharina is also entered as the wife of Joannes Baptista standing godmother in* **1786** *and* **1787** — *five sightings across five years, four of them spelled* **Jablich** *and one* *Joblich*.

**Mariana is not deleted**, *because this archive records her from a source of its own — but she cannot be the wife of casa 36 between 1785 and 1789. **Either she precedes Catharina, or she follows her, or the reading that produced her needs re-examining.** The remaining three children of the household are left under her until their own entries are read.*

people.name: Maria Rosalia Defranceschi
notes: **Baptised 20 July 1789, house 36** — *«Maria Rosa=/lia Defrances=/chi ex Loco»*, by **a.R.D. Antonius Giacich ex abatia**; godmother **«Rosalia Baxa uxor Petri, ex Lindar»**, for whom she is named. **Died 30 September 1826 aged 37y 2m 10d**, which computes back to her baptism day exactly. *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069020 and M01069321.)*

**⚠ Her mother is CATHARINA JOBLICH, not Mariana.** *Corrected 30 September 2026 from the baptism's own parents' column. She is the woman entered three years earlier as* «**Cath. ejus uxor nata Jablich ex Buccari**» — *born a Jablich of **Bakar**.*

people.name: Catharina Defranceschi
notes: **Baptised 5 March 1786 at house 36**, by the chaplain *Joh: Mart[inus] Vinich*; midwife **Maria Chrismanich**; godparents *Joh: Miroli* and *Mariana his wife*, **Cives ex Gollogorica**. *(doc.)* Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, image **M01069016**, folio 4.

**⚠ Her mother is CATHARINA née JABLICH of Buccari, not Mariana.** *The entry reads* «**Catharina nata Jablich ex Bucari**». **She is the second child of this household whose mother the archive had wrong**, *after [Maria Rosalia](/gologorica-line/).*

people.name: Maria Antonia Defranceschi

people.name: Josephus Antonius Defranceschi
notes: **Baptised 6 January 1785 at house 36** — *«Josephi Anton Defranceschi ex Loco»*, entered as catholic, male and legitimate. **He had no dates at all in this archive**, being known only from a name index. *(doc.)* Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, image **M01069014**, folio 2, entry of **6 January 1785**.

**His mother is named: «Catharina nata JABLICH … BUCARI»** — *born a Jablich of* **Bakar**. *This is the **third** instance of her and the first in a baptism of her own child: she stands godmother in 1786 as* «Cath. ejus uxor nata Jablich ex Buccari», *and is named* «Catharina Joblich» *as the mother of [Maria Rosalia in 1789](/gologorica-line/).* **It corroborates the correction made to Maria Rosalia's mother on 30 September.**

**The godparents came from Pazin** — *«Antonius Couaz» and «Maria ejus uxor», both entered* **Cives Pisinenses**; *the midwife was* **Maria Chrismanich**. *A household that fetches its godparents from the county town is not a peasant household, which agrees with the* **Civilitas** *this family carries in the census.*

people.name: Joannes Baptista Defranceschi
notes: **Baptised 13 August 1787 at house 31** — *«Joh: Bapt: Defranceschi in Loco»*. Son of **Joannes Baptista** and **Theresia née Grach**. *He had no dates in this archive.* *(doc.)* Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, image **M01069018**, folio 6.

**The godfather is «Matth: ORTIS ex Novacco»** — *an Ortis of **Novaki**, seventy-two years before [Clotilda Ortis of Novaki house 2](/married-in/) married into this family in 1859. **The connection between these two houses and that village is far older than the marriage.*** The godmother is *Maria, widow of Matthaeus **Orlich**, of Pisino* — **so the same line of the same entry writes both «Ortis» and «Orlich»**, *which is why neither spelling is preferred on [the married-in page](/married-in/).*

people.name: Franciscus Antonius Defranceschi
notes: **Baptised 13 April 1785 at house 31** — *«Franciscus Antonius Defranceschi ex Loco»*, by **Defranceschi, plebanus**. Son of **Joannes Baptista** and **Theresia née Grach**. *He had no dates in this archive.* *(doc.)* Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, image **M01069015**, folio 3.

**His godfather is his mother's own kin, and a churchman: «Archipresbiter Grach» of Cherbune**; the godmother **Catharina Defranceschi**, *Cives ex Gollogorica*; the midwife **Maria Chrismanich**. *An archpriest in the Grach family is new to this archive.*

people.name: Matthea Defranceschi
notes: Wife of Leonardus (house 6). Maiden surname not captured.

**Attested as a godmother across twenty years of the baptism book** — *«Matthea Defranceschi uxor Leonardi» in* **1795**, **1805** *and between; «Matthia uxor Leon: Defranceschi* **filia Antonij**» *in* **1792**, *which gives her a father where this archive had none.* **⚠ Still no maiden surname**: *a «Matthia Couacich» stands beside Leonardus on one 1794 entry and may be her, but it is one reading and is not claimed.* *(doc for the patronymic.)*

**⚠ Her *Conditio Patrini* is not stable across the book.** *She is entered* **Rust.** *in* **1805** *and* **Civis** *in* **1810** *and* **1815**. *The column is one cell serving two godparents, so it may not be describing her at all.* **A claim that the register separates the two Defranceschi branches by class was published on 1 October and [withdrawn to a question](/corrections/) the same day.**

Death exact from the register, 6 Oct 2026: «1858 Septbris 8° · 6 · Mathaea Defranceschi, agla, munita s. sacramentis moribundorum, sepulta vero 9° hujus · 86 · hydropisis» (M01069278, p. 98). Was «ABT 1858».

people.name: Antonius Defranceschi
notes: **Son of Usualdus and Apollonia**, not of Leonardus — corrected 30 September 2026 from the 1826 status animarum, M01069328, which names him «Antonius Defranceschi filius Usualdi et Apoloniæ».

**Adopted by his paternal uncle Leonardus** (*patruus*) into house 6, which he later headed. He entered the household from the **parish of Lindar** on his marriage of 29 January 1840; his wife Francisca came **from the parish of Gallignana (Gračišće), house 5**, on the same day. *(doc.)*

people.name: Francisca Defranceschi
notes: Wife of Antonius (house 6). The register writes her **«Francisca uxor n. Defranceschi»** — ***n.* for *nata*, so she was born a Defranceschi** and this is a marriage inside the name. **Settled beyond doubt within the same book, on three constructions in one hand**: «Victoria uxor **n.** Calligarich» at M01069322, where the surname can be nothing else; and, decisively, «**Joanna eius uxor nata Defranceschi**» at M01069323, where the scribe ***writes the word out in full***. **(doc.)**

**She came from the parish of Gallignana (Gračišće), house 5**, on her marriage of 29 January 1840 — *«Ex Parochia Gallignana sub N.o 5»*, 1826 status animarum, M01069328. **This archive already holds the Gallignana status animarum for house 5** (DAPA ZM34K-217, M01072071, supplied 24 June 2021), so her own household is readable. *(doc.)*

people.name: Joannes Baptista Defranceschi
notes: Son of Antonius & Francisca (house 5).

**His baptism, found 5 October 2026** — *«Joannes Baptista n. **19 huj.**», baptised* **21 June 1842**, *house* **5**, *of* «Antonius Defranceschi» *and* «Francisca nata Defranceschi»; *godparents* «Antonius Sestan ac Joanna Ivich». *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069116, folio 103.)* **The pedigree's 19 June 1842 is confirmed to the day.**

people.name: Theresia Defranceschi
notes: Daughter of Antonius & Francisca (house 6 in 1826, house 5 by 1843).

**Her baptism, found 5 October 2026 — and it turns «about 1843» into a day.** *«9bris 15 [1843] · domus* **5** *·* **TERESIA** *nata* **14 hujus**», *of* «**Antonius Defranceschi**» *and* «**Francisca**»; *godparents* «Antonio Salamon et Maria soror», *entered* **cives**. ***Born 14 November 1843, baptised on the 15th.*** *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069118, folio 104.)*

**⚠ The godfather's surname reads «Salamon» and is not claimed as a Salomon connection** — *see [the house-2 section](/gologorica-line/) and [the worklist](/worklist/) for the test that would settle it.*

people.name: Rosa Defranceschi

**The pedigree had her as «Joanna, born 9 June 1848». The register names her ROSA.** *«Junii 8ᵃ · domus* **5** *·* **ROSA** *nata* **heri**», *of* «Antonius Defranceschi» *and* «Francisca nata Defranceschi»; *godparents* «Giovanni L— et **Adelina Defranceschi**», *entered* **cives**. ***Born 7 June 1848, baptised the 8th.*** *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069123, folio 109.)*
**And a later hand closed her life on the same line:** «† 10/12 99» — ***died 10 December 1899, aged fifty-one***, *where this archive had no death year at all.* [The correction](/corrections/).

people.name: Antonia Defranceschi
notes: Daughter of Antonius & Francisca (house 5).

**Born 23 December 1849, baptised on Christmas Eve** — *where the pedigree had* «about 1849». *«Antonia nata heri», 24 December 1849, house* **5**, *of* «Antonius Defranceschi» *and* «Francisca nata Defranceschi». *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069124, folio 110.)*

people.name: Franciscus Defranceschi
notes: Son of Antonius & Francisca (house 6).

**Born 27 December 1851, baptised the next day** — *where the pedigree had* «about 1850». *«Decbris 28ᵃ · domus* **6** *·* **FRANCISCUS** *natus* **heri**», *midwife* «Dominica Flegar». *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069126, folio 112.)* **Found in the strip at the foot of the page that [the day's crop had been discarding](/corrections/).**

people.name: Antonius Defranceschi
notes: Son of Antonius & Francisca (house 6).

**Born 3 February 1855, baptised the 5th** — *where the pedigree had* «about 1853». *«Antonius natus 3ᵃ hujus», house* **6**, *godparents* «Joannes Udovich et Sancta Sestan». *And in the margin,* **«† 17.II.1913»**. *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069130, folio 116.)*
**⚠ This archive may hold him twice** — *see [the roster note](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1853/) and [the worklist](/worklist/).*

notes: Head of house 7 in the 1826 status animarum (census page 14, img M01069332).
The death name-index calls him "Josephus junior" (father of Maximilianus,

**Born 4 March 1765** — *where this archive had «about 1763».* Married **3 February 1807**; died **12 December 1838**. **⚠ The register's own arithmetic does not quite close**: it gives his age at death as **74 years 9 months**, which would put the birth in **March 1764**, a year earlier than the birth column says. *The written birth is taken as the better figure and the tension is recorded rather than smoothed.* *(doc for the date; the age noted as inconsistent.)*

people.name: Lambertina Peschle
notes: Wife of Josephus junior (house 7); the 1826 census records her as "Lambertina

**Born 17 September 1786** — *the household book gives the day, where this archive had only «about 1786».* She is entered **«Lambertina uxor nata Peschle»** with **«Ex Volosca»** in the provenance column, and her death on **16 July 1863, aged 76 years 10 months**, which agrees with the date already held. *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069332.)*

**⚠ Her maiden name is written four ways in two books.** *«Peschle» in the 1826* status animarum; ***«Pesle»** twice in the baptism register (1821, 1822); and* «Peste» *once at page scale, which was a misreading of* «Pesle». **No form is preferred**; *the family's own [married-in page](/married-in/) uses* **Peschle** *because that is the form the archive has used longest, not because it is established.*

⭐ 6 Oct 2026 — DEATH YEAR CORRECTED 1857 → 1878 from the burial register: «1878 Decembris 22. · 7 · Josephus Defranceschi, possidens, munitus SS. et sepultus die 24. Dec. 1878 · 70 · Senectus» (M01069295, p. 132). Seventy on 22 Dec 1878 closes on the birth of 13 March 1808; at 1857 he would have been 49. people.name: Carolus Josephus Defranceschi
notes: Son of Dnus Josephus Defranceschi & Dna Lambertina (house 7); status Civilis.

**His own baptism entry, found 1 October 2026.** *«Die 19na 8bris 1809 ·* **CAROLUS JOSEPHUS DEFRANCESCHI** *natus die 17ma hujus, **vespere**» —* **born on the 17th of October in the evening, baptised on the 19th**, *at* **house 17**. *Parents* **«Dnus Josephus Defranceschi et Domna Lambertina ejusdem uxor»**; *godfather* **«Dnus Gioanni Curelich, Petinensis»** — *of* **Pićan**; *midwife Maria, widow of Antonius Crismanich Santelich.* *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069064, folio 51.)*

**And a later hand has written his death into the margin of his own baptism** — *a cross and* **«8/I 1893»** *above his name. **The archive's death date for him is confirmed by the register that recorded his birth.***

**✅ This retires a discrepancy.** *The 1826 census was read here as* **17 October** *on one page and* **19 October** *on another, and the difference was logged as unresolved. **Neither reading was wrong: one is the birth and the other the baptism.***

people.name: Maria Aloysia Defranceschi
notes: Daughter of Josephus & Lambertina (house 7). Her baptism is NOT in the

**Her baptism entry, found 1 October 2026 while closing the sampled gaps.** *«Die 17ma Augusti 1811 ·* **MARIA ALOYSIA DEFRANCESCHI** *nata die* **14ta** *hujus hora 8va mane» —* **born on 14 August 1811 at eight in the morning, baptised on the 17th**, *at house 17. Godfather* **«Joannes Ant. Torbulla, Parochus Paspergensis»** — *the parish priest of* **Paz**. *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069070, folio 57.)*

**⚠ AND THE REGISTERS DISAGREE ABOUT HER BIRTHDAY.** *The baptism register says she was born the* **14th**; *this archive and the 1826 census both say the* **16th**. *The baptism book is the primary record and was written three days after the event; the census was compiled fifteen years later. **The date is NOT changed here** — it is flagged, because a two-day difference between two registers is a different thing from the birth/baptism gap that explained her brothers, and it deserves its own look.*
*Her second name* **Aloysia** *is new to this archive, which carried her as* «Maria» *alone.*

people.name: Franciscus Xaverius Joseph Defranceschi
notes: Son of Dnus Josephus Defranceschi & Dna Lambertina (house 7); status Civilis,

**His baptism entry, found 1 October 2026.** *«Die 25ta Februarii 1816 ·* **FRANCISCUS XAVERIUS JOSEPH DEFRANCESCHI** *natus die* **19na** *hujus mensis» —* **born on the 19th, baptised on the 25th**, *at* **house 17**, *of* **«Dnus Josephus Defranceschi et Dna Lambertina ejusdem uxor»**. *One godparent is entered* **Nobilis**, *«da Lindaro» — of Lindar.* *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069078.)*
**A later hand has written «† 4 Januarii 1893» above his name** — *confirming in the baptism register the death date this archive already held.*

**✅ This retires the discrepancy logged on 30 September.** *The 1826 census gave* **25 February** *where this archive held* **19 February**, *and the difference was left open. **Both are right: the 19th is the birth and the 25th the baptism.***

people.name: Clementina Maria Defranceschi
notes: Daughter of Dnus Josephus Defranceschi & Dna Lambertina nata Pesle; status

**Her baptism confirms the date this archive already held.** *«6 8bris 1822 ·* **CLEMENTINA MARIA** *nata die* **3 8bris** *hora 10 pomeridiana», house* **17**, *of* «Dnus Joseph Defranceschi» *and* «Dna Lambertina ejus uxor **nata PESLE**». **Born 3 October 1822 at ten at night, baptised on the 6th.** *(doc — Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, M01069089.)*

**Her godmother came from Silesia.** *«**Amalia PESCHLE ex SILESIA**» stands with* «Pietro Ant. Defranceschi», *both* **Cives Gollogoricenses**. *A Peschle out of **Silesia** at an Istrian font is the furthest this archive has traced [her mother's family](/married-in/).*

**⚠ She had an elder sister of the same name.** *A* **Clementina** *was baptised to the same parents on* **28 January 1821** *(M01069086, house 104) and appears in no later record of the household. **The name was reused**, which is what families did when a child died — and it explains why the 1826 census date sat between the two.*

⭐ 6 Oct 2026 — DEATH YEAR CORRECTED 1840 → 1870 from the burial register, which this archive had itself named as the thing needed: «1870 Martii 10ma · 7 · Clementina Defranceschi, possidens, munita SS Sacram. et sepulta 11. Martii · 47 · Phthisis» (M01069286, p. 114). Forty-seven on 10 March 1870 closes exactly on the birth of 3 October 1822. The family tree's 1870 was right; this archive's 1840 was wrong. See /corrections/.

people.name: Maximilianus Antonius Josephus Defranceschi
notes: Son of Dnus Josephus Defranceschi & Dna Lambertina (house 17); status Civilis. Born 8 January 1828, baptised the 9th.

**His baptism entry, found 5 October 2026.** *«9 Januarii 1828 ·* **MAXIMILIANUS ANTONIUS DEFRANCESCHI** *natus* **heri media nocte**» — ***born the previous day at midnight, so 8 January, and baptised on the 9th***, *at house 17, of* **«Dnus Josephus Defranceschi et Domna Lambertina ejusdem uxor nata Pesle»**. *(doc — Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, M01069098, folio 85.)*
**The archive's 9 January is the BAPTISM**, *the same pattern that explained [Carlo and Franciscus Xaverius](/gologorica-line/). **His birth is 8 January 1828.***

**His godfather was a dean.** *«Joannes Ant. Tesak, **Canonicus … et Decanus**», with «Teresa Giacich»; the conditio column reads* **Mercator Pisinensis** — *a merchant of Pazin, though the column serves both godparents and cannot be assigned to one.*

**⚠ And the register's margin disagrees with this archive about his death.** *A later hand has written* **«† 6/8 910»** *above his name — read at seven times magnification. In Austrian and Croatian usage that is* **6 August 1910**; *this archive carries* **6 October 1910**. **Not changed** — *one marginal note does not move a date the archive holds from elsewhere, but the better-placed source now disagrees and that has to be visible.*

**⚠ This pedigree carried 9 January as his BIRTH until 5 October 2026**, *when an audit found that the archive had [published the correction](/gologorica-line/) and never moved the tree.* **9 January is the baptism; the register says «natus heri media nocte».**

people.name: Henricus Jacobus Defranceschi
notes: Son of Dnus Josephus Defranceschi & Dna Lambertina nata Pesle (house 7 of the 1826 status animarum). Confirmed Oct 1844.

**His baptism was found 5 October 2026.** *«Die 28va Martii [1830] ·* **ENRICHUS JACOBUS DEFRANCESCHI** *natus* **11ma Martii hora 5ta Mane**» — ***born 11 March 1830 at five in the morning and baptised on the 28th***, *by* **Franciscus Brussich, parochus**. *Godparents* «Giacomo Giacich» *and* «Jos.a Teresa Giacich»; *midwife* «Marianna uxor Stanislai Rabar». *(doc — Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, M01069102, folio 89.)* **The date this archive already held is confirmed to the hour — verification, not discovery.**

**The register spells him ENRICHUS, without the H**, *and so does the 1826* status animarum. *This archive carries* «Henricus Jacobus» *off the family tree; the id* `henricus-jacobus-defranceschi-1830` *is* **minted and frozen** *and is not moved for a spelling.*

**⭐ His entry is where the archive noticed that this book counts houses twice.** *The* Domus *cell is written, struck through and replaced with* **104**. *It is not a note about his family: from 1830 the register routinely carries two house numbers per entry, and by 1831 every entry on a page does.* *See* [the 1830 section](/gologorica-line/) *and* [worklist 171](/worklist/).
**Seventeen days from birth to font** — *where his brother Maximilianus was baptised the day after he was born. The longest gap this family shows.*

people.name: Aloysius Defranceschi
notes: **Born at VOLOSCA, not in Poland.** *The 1826* status animarum *enters him* **«Aloysius … filius natus Volosca»** — *read at five times magnification, where the word is unambiguous.* **This archive had him as «natus Polonia», born in Poland**, and built a note on it. *(doc.)* Gologorica *Status Animarum* 1826, house 7 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, image **M01069408**.

*It is also the obvious thing: his mother* **Lambertina née Peschle was «Ex Volosca»**, entered so two lines above him. **She went home to be delivered.** *[Volosca's registers have never been opened by this archive](/worklist/), though it has held the waypoints all along.*

**⚠ The register gives his birth as 4 May 1832; this archive carries 8 May.** *Not changed — one page-scale reading of a digit does not move a date, and the baptism register that would settle it is on the same reel.*

people.name: Clotilda Orlis

**Her parents and her village, from the 1826 household book:** she is entered **«Clotilda uxor Ortis, filia Joannis ac Franciscæ»** — *daughter of Joannes and Francisca* — and the provenance column gives her coming **«Ex Parochia Novacis sub N.º 2»**, **out of Novaki, house 2**. *Her birth (12 October 1834) and the marriage (10 October 1859) were already held from the 1894 census and are confirmed here.* **⚠ The surname is written *Ortis* on this page**, *against the* **Orlis** *this archive carries from the 1894 book. chronicle.heading: The village, as its priest saw it — 1892 to 1918
chronicle.lead: Ljudevit Žváček was parish priest of Gologorica from 1892 to 1923 and kept a chronicle. He was a Czech from Moravia, recruited because the bishop of Trieste and Koper had advertised in a Prague newspaper in 1885 for young Czechs willing to serve in Istria, where priests were short. He was a Pan-Slav. He arrived in a village dominated by an Italian-national gentry family of the same surname as this archive's, and he wrote down what he saw. Stipan Trogrlić published his chronicle in the Vjesnik istarskog arhiva; it is open access, and it is the closest thing that exists to a description of the family's own village from inside.

split.heading: Grajani and poljani
split.text: The village called itself in two halves. The «grajani» — townspeople, those inside the old walls — and the «poljani», or «campagnoli», the people of the surrounding hamlets, whom the townspeople named with a certain contempt. The line was social before it was national. Then it became national.
split.quote: Građani, iako etnički Hrvati, pod utjecajem moćne furlansko-karnijske obitelji De Franceschi, koja se naselila u Gologoricu još u 17. st., postaju politički Talijani.
split.en: The townspeople, though ethnically Croats, become politically Italians under the influence of the powerful Friulian-Carnian family De Franceschi, which settled at Gologorica back in the seventeenth century. They voted for the Italian Liberal Party — and went on speaking Croatian to one another. The poljani, conscious of being Croats, voted for the Croatian Party, and the quarrel between the two became part of the village's ordinary week.

carnia.heading: A third witness for Carnia — and this one is not the family's own
carnia.text: «Furlansko-karnijske obitelji De Franceschi, koja se naselila u Gologoricu još u 17. st.» — the Friulian-Carnian family De Franceschi, settled at Gologorica in the seventeenth century. That is Croatian scholarship, following Miroslav Bertoša, stating the origin as established fact and dating it a century earlier than Carlo did.
carnia.why: This archive has held the Carnia claim at arm's length because it rested on one document — the headmen's list of 1679 — and on Carlo's private testimony about his own family. There are now three independent things: the 1679 list; Kobler's record that Valentino Defranceschi came from Carnia and was made a citizen of Fiume in 1739; and a modern Croatian historian describing the Gologorica family flatly as Friulian-Carnian, settled in the seventeenth century. None of them joins this line to that one. But the road itself is no longer in doubt.

priest.heading: How he came to be there at all

rows.w: Pravdoslav Filiplić of Lindar was appointed administrator of the parish, and an agitation started at once against his being confirmed. It was led by the sitting mayor, Antun Ivić, and the reason Ivić gave was Filiplić's close and friendly relations with the family of Francesco De Franceschi, the former mayor. Filiplić had the backing of most heads of households. The bishop moved him «stanta pede» — that instant — to Grdoselo.

rows.t: A Slav priest, foisted on them
rows.w: Žváček was appointed instead. Now it was the Italians and the Italianised townspeople who bristled: they took badly to having a Slav priest, a Czech out of Moravia, put over them.

Žváček complained to the district authority at Pazin about one Leonardo De Franceschi, who had repeatedly disrupted the singing in Croatian in the parish church — conducted by the village schoolmaster, Josip Monas. He asked the authority to protect Monas, because De Franceschi had once threatened to kill him.

weaver.heading: And the one tradesman in the town was a weaver called Leonardo De Franceschi
weaver.text: Žváček's survey of the trades is short. «U gradu osim nekoliko samoukih zidara i postolara te jednog izučenog tkalca, Leonarda De Franceschija, podrijetlom Krnjela, drugih zanatlija nema.» — In the town, apart from a few self-taught masons and cobblers and one trained weaver, Leonardo De Franceschi, of Krnjeli origin, there are no other craftsmen.
weaver.why: Three things meet in that sentence and this archive did not put them there. The Carnia argument is that the family came down into Istria as weavers — the cramars of the Ovaro parishes, out in autumn and home in spring. The one De Franceschi household reconstructed at Mione has as its head in the nineteenth century a «tessitore contadino», a peasant weaver. And here, at Gologorica, in the family's own village, the single trained weaver in the place is a De Franceschi — named Leonardo, which is the name Carlo gives to his own great-great-great-grandfather.
weaver.caution: It is a convergence, not a proof of descent. Leonardo is a common enough name in this family that it means little on its own, and Žváček's Leonardo came to Gologorica from Krnjeli. But one leg of it has since stopped being an assumption: Giorgio Ferigo, quoting the 1679 headmen's return in full, states that the men in it are tessitori — weavers — and that in Istria «dire cargnel equivaleva a dire tessitore», to say Carnian was to say weaver. The trade is now in the source, not only in the pattern. See the Carnia page.

occupation.heading: 20 December 1918
occupation.text: A company of a hundred and fifty-four Italian soldiers came into Gologorica with three officers — the Compania mitraglieri Fiat — on eight carts drawn by sixteen mules, two to a cart. Tenente Giacomo Sechio was billeted in the house of Giulio De Franceschi; sottotenente Antonio Defassio in the house of Luigi De Franceschi; tenente Emilio Galizzi in the guest room of the parish house.
occupation.then: The military command asked Žváček to tell the congregation that after the ten-thirty mass the soldiers would raise the Italian flag on the church tower. After mass, with all three bells rung in celebration, the tricolour went up. The soldiers formed up on the square in full kit, and a schoolmaster from Trieste, Josip Celentich, addressed them from the low wall, celebrating «great mother Italy, who after such long slavery has taken her daughter Istria under her protection».
occupation.close: «Narod je šuteći odslušao govor. Neki su u znak prosvjeda stisnuli šake. Kad je govornik završio i uzviknuo: Eviva Italia! — nitko mu nije odgovorio osim vojnika.» The people heard the speech out in silence. Some clenched their fists. When the speaker finished and shouted «Long live Italy!», nobody answered him but the soldiers.

life.heading: What a day was worth
rows: 60–70 novčića a day in summer, 50 in winter
1 florin 20 in summer, 1 florin in winter
half of the above, whatever the trade
life.note: Gologorica had been a fortress and had two town gates. The one at the entrance still stands; the other, on the south side beside the parish house, had long been pulled down — and the priest still stopped at the place where it had been when carrying the viaticum to the sick, as did the funeral processions coming up from Gologorički Dol on their way to the cemetery.

chronicle.source: Stipan Trogrlić, «Gologorica u Kronici Župe (1892.–1918.) prema zapisima župnika Ljudevita Žvačeka», Vjesnik istarskog arhiva 32. Open access on Hrčak, with Croatian, English and Italian summaries.

argument.heading: Both sides of the Istrian quarrel used this village as their first exhibit
argument.lead: This archive has been reading the Italian press of Istria and has heard, so far, only the Italian side. «Naša Sloga» — Our Concord, the Croatian paper of Istria, printed at Trieste and then Pula from 1870 — is the other side, and its whole run is in the Austrian National Library's newspaper archive. Searching it for this family turned up something better than a mention of a De Franceschi. It turned up the two sides using the same page of the same book, and the same three place-names, to prove opposite things. One of the three is Gologorica.

carlo.heading: What Carlo wrote, in 1879
carlo.quote: …mentre sino al 1000 tutti i nomi dei luoghi che si trovano indicati nei diplomi, sono italiani, cento anni più tardi incomincia a comparirne taluno di slavi, come nel 1102 si trova Golgoriza, e Cernogradus e Bellegradus, in mezzo a molti altri luoghi citati tutti di nome italiano. Dal che si deve inferire che appena dal 1000 al 1100 incominciarono quei parziali trasporti nell'Istria interna di slavi…
carlo.en: …whereas up to the year 1000 all the place-names that appear in the diplomas are Italian, a hundred years later some Slavic ones begin to appear — as in 1102 one finds Golgoriza, and Cernogradus and Bellegradus, among many other places all cited under Italian names. From which it must be inferred that only between 1000 and 1100 did those partial transplantings of Slavs into inner Istria begin…
carlo.why: Carlo's argument is that the Slavic names are late and that the Slavs were brought in, in stages, to repopulate country emptied by war and plague. The document he is reading is the donation of 1102, by which Count Ulric (Voldarico) and his wife Adelaide gave their Istrian possessions to the church of Aquileia. He describes it himself on page 143. And the first Slavic name in his list is the name of the village he was born in.

sloga.heading: What the Croatian paper did with it, thirty years later
sloga.quote: Za velikih seoba narodâ nastanili su se Hrvati sigurno i u labinskom kraju, oko Raše, u Buzeštini i Pazinštini. Neka Vam dokaze dadu sami Talijani: mjesta Gologorica, Cernogradus i Bellegradus spominju se u listini od 1102 (v. De Franceschi str. 351.) Da tamo nije bilo Hrvata već davna prije u velikom broju, ne bi ta mjesta mogla imati u 11. stoljeću onako liepih hrvatskih imena.
sloga.en: At the time of the great migrations of peoples the Croats certainly settled in the Labin district too, around the Raša, in the Buzet and the Pazin country. Let the Italians themselves furnish you the proofs: the places Gologorica, Cernogradus and Bellegradus are named in a charter of 1102 (see De Franceschi, p. 351). Had there not been Croats there long before, and in great numbers, those places could not have borne such fine Croatian names in the eleventh century.
sloga.why: The citation is exact. Naša Sloga has gone to page 351 of Carlo De Franceschi's own book, taken his three names and his charter, and reversed the inference: for Carlo the Slavic names mark the arrival, for Naša Sloga they mark a presence that must already have been long and large. «Neka Vam dokaze dadu sami Talijani» — let the Italians themselves give you the proofs — is aimed at the Italian side, and the Italian it names is this family's own historian.
sloga.then: The paragraph ends with the complaint that gives the village its two names: the Italians «su u novije vrieme odlučili, da potalijanče sva imena» — have lately decided to Italianise all the names. Gologorica is the bare hill in Croatian; Moncalvo is the same thing in Italian. Which of them a man wrote told you where he stood — though on which came first, see the section below, where a third party disagrees with both of them.

argument.why: Why this belongs in a family archive and not only in a history of Istria. The village these people came from was, for two generations, a piece of public evidence — quoted in print, in two languages, by people arguing about who Istria belonged to. Carlo De Franceschi led the Italian side and is buried in the village. His Croatian neighbours read his book and turned it round. The family's «Gologorica» and «Moncalvo» are not two spellings of a place; they are two positions, and the records of this family use both.
argument.sourcing: Naša Sloga of 25 March 1909 was located through ANNO's search endpoint and its pages fetched from the library's IIIF image service; the passage was enlarged on the page image and read against the type, not taken from the OCR. Carlo's page 351 was read in the Internet Archive's scan of the 1879 first edition, which this archive has in full text.

third.heading: A third voice, from Kraków, that neither side had
third.where: Mieczysław Małecki, «Przegląd słowiańskich gwar Istrji», Polska Akademja Umiejętności, Kraków 1930, p. 130
third.quote: …w 1102 r. pojawia się nazwa Cernogradus i Bellogradus w miejsce dawniejszych Nigrignanum i Albinianum; w tym też mniej więcej czasie spotykamy po raz pierwszy nazwę Gologorica zamiast dawniejszej Moncalvo.
third.en: …in 1102 the names Cernogradus and Bellogradus appear in place of the earlier Nigrignanum and Albinianum; and at about the same time we meet for the first time the name Gologorica in place of the earlier Moncalvo.
third.why: A Polish Slavist with nothing at stake in Istria, working forty years after the quarrel, takes the same charter and the same three names — and on the philology he sides with Carlo. The Slavic names replace older Romance ones; they do not underlie them. Moncalvo is the older name of this village and Gologorica the newer, which is the reverse of the order this archive assumed and stated a few paragraphs above, and the correction belongs here rather than quietly in the earlier text.
third.but: But Małecki does not give the Italian side its conclusion either. He dates Slav settlement in Istria to Duke John and the assembly on the Rižana in 804 — well before 1102 — and argues the colonies grew steadily afterwards, helped by the plagues of 954–8, 1010, 1073, 1080 and above all 1098, which thinned the native population until «ludność romańska cofnęła się w obręb murów miejskich, ludność słowiańska stała się jedynym panem wsi» — the Romance population drew back inside the town walls, and the Slavic population became the sole master of the countryside. So: Carlo was right that the name is late, Naša Sloga was right that the people were not, and the village where this family lived for three hundred years was the exhibit for both.

correction.heading: And the correction has itself been corrected
correction.text: Within the same day's work, a second source contradicts Małecki on which name came first — and the weight is against him. The «Atti» of Rovigno, volume 3 of 1972, warns that Istrian and Italian historiography has been running two villages together: Gologorica (Italian Gologorizza) in the Pisino district, which is this family's, and Golaš (Italian Moncalvo) near Valle, which is not. For the family's village it says flatly: «Nei documenti del periodo veneto non viene citato il termine Moncalvo, per indicare Gologorizza, perché è sorto probabilmente appena nel XIX secolo» — in the documents of the Venetian period the term Moncalvo is not used for Gologorizza, because it probably arose only in the nineteenth century. Its evidence is a man of this surname: in 1795 Pietro De Franceschi of Gollogorizza, marrying at Valle, gives only the Croatian name, «perché il nome italiano Moncalvo sembra non esistesse ancora».
correction.then: Camillo De Franceschi — Carlo's son, and the historian of the County of Pisino — is quoted in the same footnote calling Gologorizza «una delle prime località abitate dell'Istria che abbiano avuto nome slavo», one of the first inhabited places in Istria to have borne a Slavic name. So the family's own second historian, and the Rovigno scholarship, both make Gologorica the old name and Moncalvo a nineteenth-century Italian coinage. Małecki, writing in Kraków without the Venetian registers, appears to have carried the Nigrignanum-to-Cernogradus pattern across to a village it does not fit. This archive published his version this morning and is correcting it here rather than deleting it, because the disagreement is itself the point: three scholars, three readings, and the family's village in the middle of all of them.

bishop.heading: Whose village it was, from the Vatican side
bishop.lead: Every bishop of Pićan from 1589 had to send Rome a sworn report on the state of his diocese. Ivan Grah published the whole series in 1980 from the Vatican archive, and the paper is free on the Internet Archive. Carlo De Franceschi had already told this archive that the bishops of Pedena styled themselves «Dominus Gollaegoritiae, Scopliaci et Tupliaci». The reports say what that meant on the ground — in the century before the Defranceschi came down from Carnia, and through the century they spent here as the bishop's people.

rows.lab: When the bishop got it
rows.text: Bishop Antun Zara (1601–1621), reporting to Rome in 1606 and 1614, says he holds temporal power over the villages of Škopljak and Tupljak «a od nedavna i nad župom Gologoricom» — and lately also over the parish of Gologorica. That dates the lordship. The benefice itself had been founded in 1444 and fell to the bishops when its last holder died; by Zara's time it had become secular lordship as well, and it was still the bishop's under Maria Theresa, when the last bishop, Aldrago de Piccardi (1766–1785), writes that he obtained the Gologorica benefice from the empress herself and is «gospodar Gologorice, Škopljaka i Tupljaka».

rows.lab: What the bishop's tenants were worth
rows.text: The bishop's people were koloni — colonus tenants, held to the land. Zara reports that his koloni at Škopljak suffer beatings, break-ins, robbery and imprisonment at the hands of the inhabitants of Gračišće and of Bernardin Barbo, captain of the County of Pazin, and that being a friend and counsellor of the archduke has not helped him stop it. At Tupljak it was worse. Under Bishop Zaharija (1550–1562), who could not find sixty florins of provincial tax, the authorities carried off fifteen colonus families with their movable goods and sold them to the Lupoglav lessee Kristofor Gušić, who resold them to one Tuzler, who left them by will to his wife. A clerk of the Congregation wrote in the margin «Commendatur Nuntio». The case was never resolved.

rows.lab: How poor the see was
rows.text: The canons and parish priests swore in 1656 and again in 1661 that the whole revenue of the diocese did not exceed 150 Venetian scudi: thirty went to Carniola in tax, fifteen to the roof, fifty to the keeper of the bishop's palace, ten to the chancellor, fifteen to the four little churches of Pićan. Thirty scudi were left, and on that the bishops lived at Pićan for one, two or three months a year — some for a fortnight, some for eight days. They swore that within human memory no bishop had ever actually resided in the diocese. The cathedral chapter, which had once had twenty canons, had four.

rows.lab: Two priests of Gologorica, named
rows.text: The 1656 and 1661 statements are signed by the diocesan clergy in person, with their ages: Petar Gašprotić, vicar general, 75; Ivan Težak, canon, 61; Juraj Hlaj, parish priest of Gračišće, 78; Juraj Glogovac of Lindar, 56; and «Juraj Kukurin, župnik gologorički, star 52 godine» — George Kukurin, parish priest of Gologorica, aged fifty-two, so born about 1604. The report was carried to Rome by Petar Šestan of Novaki, travelling with «Zec Mihovila, gologoričkog kapelana» — Mihovil Zec, chaplain of Gologorica. Two men who served the family's church before the family got there.

rows.lab: And what language the village prayed in
rows.text: Zara found that in every parish except Pićan and Gračišće the liturgy was Glagolitic — Church Slavonic in the round Croatian letters. He put a stop to it: «Sacerdotes omnes quasi, Petinensibus exceptis, Illyrico Idiomate Sacrum in meo primo adventu celebrabant, iam fere omnes Latino» — at my first coming almost all the priests celebrated in the Illyrian tongue; now nearly all in Latin. He would ordain nobody who could not manage the grammar, and sent his older seminarians to Ljubljana and Graz. Almost all his priests spoke Croatian, Italian and German. Grah adds that the Glagolitic outlived the diocese: the last Glagolitic priest died at Grimalda in 1849.

bishop.why: Read this next to the Carnia evidence and it stops being background. A family of Friulian-Carnian carpenters and weavers settles at Gologorica in the seventeenth century, in a parish whose lord is a bishop too poor to live in his own diocese, among tenants who could be seized and sold for sixty florins of unpaid tax, in a church that had been singing in Glagolitic within living memory. By 1739 a Valentino Defranceschi come from Carnia was made a citizen of Fiume; by 1819 the family was marrying Salomons at Gračišće; by 1848 one of them sat in the parliament at Vienna. That is the distance travelled, and this is the floor it started from.
bishop.source: Ivan Grah, «Izvještaji pićanskih biskupa Svetoj Stolici (1589–1780)», Croatica Christiana Periodica IV (1980), no. 6 — read in full from the copy at the Internet Archive, September 2026. The De Franceschi named in its footnotes are Carlo and his son Camillo, cited as authorities; no member of this family appears in the text.

dialect.heading: What the village actually sounded like, recorded in 1930
dialect.lead: The same Kraków monograph is a dialect atlas, and both of this family's parishes are survey points in it. Małecki went round Istria with a notebook and wrote down what people said. Gologorica is point I, 3; Gračišće is point I, 2, a — different groups, five kilometres apart.

rows.lab: Gologorica belongs to the Čepić dialect
rows.text: Not to the central Istrian group its neighbours belong to. Małecki puts it in a north-western wedge running out from the Čepić lake — with Gradinje, Cerovlje, Novaki and Zarečje — which is «odciętego przez wioski rumuńskie od swego centrum», cut off from its own centre by the Romanian villages: Nova Vas, Šušnjevica, Brdo and Grobnik, the Istro-Romanian settlements. The village's speech came from the other side of a Vlach-speaking barrier and was then worked on from all sides by the central dialects.

rows.lab: Words written down at Gologorica
rows.text: «ne znamo, mala, bárka, jedán» · «trukińu» for maize, «susêd», «na pütu», «dotaju» · «stiéna, ceno» for cheap, «tiesto, drién, pedestiét, piet» · «jabuka, vuk, puna, vuna, dužni» · «venac, pisak» for sand, «ždribac, sirak» · «nevêste, žene, kozé». That is a page of the family's own village speaking, taken down by a stranger who wanted nothing from it but its vowels.

rows.lab: And words written down at Gračišće
rows.text: «besêda, dretva, léto, koleno, člověk» · «kral', pole, l'udi, vol'a» · «klenémo, zet, žetva» · «soka, srieda» · «gnizlo». A different set of reflexes, and Małecki assigns it a different code. The two parishes this line runs through — one where the family married, one where it lived — were, to a dialectologist, two dialects.

dialect.why: This is not decoration. It is the only record this archive has of how the people in it spoke. The registers give their Latin names and the newspapers give the Italian argument about them; Małecki gives eleven words of the Croatian they used at home in the village where the family had lived since the seventeenth century, in the decade before the last of them left.
dialect.source: Mieczysław Małecki, «Przegląd słowiańskich gwar Istrji» (with six maps), Prace Komisji Językowej nr 17, Polska Akademja Umiejętności, Kraków 1930 — read from the Toruń university library copy at the Internet Archive, September 2026. The index entries are «Gologorica (Moncalvo di Pisino I 3)» pp. 27, 49, 60, 68–9, 72, 130 and «Gračišće (Gallignana I 2a)» pp. 6, 18, 51, 60–3, 65–6, 131.

bandnight.heading: The band, the stones, and the grave they tried to refuse
bandnight.lead: Six issues of «Il giovine Pensiero» of Pola, found by pairing the family's own fused spelling with the village's Italian name, carry one continuous story out of Gologorica between 1893 and 1895. It is told entirely from the Italian side and should be read that way; it is also the only close-up this archive has of the village in the years just after Carlo's death, and a Defranceschi house and a Defranceschi witness are both in it.

rows.t: Somebody tried to stop the burial
rows.w: Twice in 1894 the paper refers back to it as a known thing. In July: «il rappresentante comunale di Moncalvo, certo Ivić, è quello stesso che negò la sepoltura alla salma del nostro illustre storico Carlo De Franceschi» — the communal representative of Moncalvo, one Ivić, is the same man who refused burial to the body of our illustrious historian Carlo De Franceschi. In August: «colui che già un tempo volle negare la sepoltura alla salma dell'illustre storico istriano Carlo Defranceschi». This archive already had the line about him resting in the humble cemetery of Moncalvo. It did not have the fact that his getting there was contested.

rows.t: The village invited Pisino to a party
rows.w: «Invitati gentilmente dall'intera popolazione di questo villaggio, la banda dei dilettanti e molti cittadini di Pisino vennero domenica scorsa alle 4 pom. qui, nel luogo natio dell'illustre storico istriano Carlo Defranceschi» — invited by the entire population of this village, the amateur band and many citizens of Pisino came last Sunday at four in the afternoon, here, to the birthplace of the illustrious Istrian historian Carlo Defranceschi. The whole village went out to the entrance to meet them, and the women and girls had brought a great vase of flowers in the visitors' honour.

rows.t: Two stones from the bell tower
rows.w: Five men from Dol, an hour off, wanted to start something; the village's own people talked them down. Then a large stone landed on the musicians' table and smashed the flower vase, and a second crushed a trumpet. Nobody was found, but «le parve che le pietre fossero state scagliate dal campanile» — it seemed to them the stones had been thrown from the bell tower.

The band formed up to leave and came back at a run: stones were falling at the village exit from every side. Children were got to safety and a second attempt made, and «ci vedemmo assaliti da una decina di contadini, che da una parte con sassate dall'altra colle daghe sguainate ci si slanciarono contro» — about ten peasants came at them, stones on one side and drawn blades on the other. Fifteen wounded, twelve from Pisino and three from the village, two of them seriously. «Una vera carneficina.» One assailant was disarmed of a large flick-knife.

rows.t: And one of the wounded was carried into a Defranceschi house
rows.w: The party went back to Pisino «ad eccezione dei due colpiti gravemente, che rimasero uno nella casa della famiglia Peschle e altro in quella Defranceschi» — except the two badly hurt, who stayed, one in the house of the Peschle family and the other in the Defranceschi house. Four gendarmes came out from Pisino the same night with the district doctor, Dr de Beden.

rows.t: The village turned on its delegate
rows.w: The paper reports that against Ivić, «causa la sua intemperanza, le sue villane e rozze maniere, il suo interessato odio contro l'elemento italiano si ribellò quasi tutta la popolazione di quel paesello, la quale volle destituito dal posto di delegato comunale» — almost the whole population of that little place rebelled and wanted him removed from the post of communal delegate.

rows.t: A Defranceschi in the witness box
rows.w: «Il giovine Pensiero» of 15 June 1895 prints the trial, plainly of the same affair — the band, the departure, the stones. Among the witnesses: «Entra Vittorio Defranceschi fu Francesco, Gollogorizza d'anni 23.» Vittorio Defranceschi, son of the late Francesco, of Gologorica, aged twenty-three. He is named in other men's evidence too — one witness says «Vittorio Defranceschi mi diede un calcio», Vittorio Defranceschi gave me a kick; another says the Defranceschi came out of the inn and dragged him off to drink with them. The shouts the court was trying to pin down were «crepa i taliani, bastonemoli» and «živio», and the advocate Dr Trinajstić addressed the bench in Croatian.

bandnight.person: Vittorio Defranceschi, son of a Francesco already dead, aged twenty-three in June 1895, living at Gologorica. Born about 1872. That is a person, with a father, a place and a date, and he was not in this archive before Friday.
bandnight.caution: Read the framing with care. «Il giovine Pensiero» was an Italian-national paper reporting an Italian-national grievance, and everything above is its account: it is the side that calls the priest furious and the delegate brutal. But it also says two things that cut against the simple picture. The invitation came from «l'intera popolazione di questo villaggio», and the paper is at pains to record that of the attackers «nessuno nativo di Moncalvo» — not one was a native of Moncalvo. By its own telling this was not an Italian family against a Croatian village. It was a village welcoming a band, and men from Dol an hour away coming in to break it up.
bandnight.source: «Il giovine Pensiero», Pola: 26 July 1894, 16 August 1894, 15 June 1895 (pp. 3–4), with further mentions on 21 December 1894, 15 March 1895, 3 October 1896 and 10 April 1897. Found in ANNO by pairing the fused spelling «Defranceschi» with «Gallignana», downloaded through the library's IIIF image service, located by OCR; the two passages quoted at length above — the refused burial and Vittorio's entry — were enlarged on the page image and read against the type.

bembo.heading: A marriage at Valle, 22 January 1795
bembo.lead: Found in the «Atti» of the Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno, volume 3 of 1972, in a study of the parish registers of Valle (Bale) on the west coast — a hundred kilometres from Gologorica, and the last place this archive would have thought to look. The author quotes the entry whole.
bembo.quote: Adi 22 Genaro 1795. Essendo stati dispensati delle trine solite publicazioni da Monsig.r Ves.uo di Parenzo come da Lett.e de dì etc., io D. Angelo Can.co Mitton Piou.o di questa Collegiata Diocesi di Parenzo hò interrogato il Sig.r Piero De Franceschi da Gollogorizza, e la Sig.ra Anna figlia del N. Sig.r Tommaso Bembo, et avuto il loro mutuo consenso per parole de p.nti l'hò congiunto in Mat.nio alla presenza di molti, e specialm.te del sig.r Pietro Basan da Lindar, e di d.no Damian Fiori Testj.
bembo.en: 22 January 1795. The three usual publications of banns having been dispensed with by the Lord Bishop of Parenzo as per his letter of etc., I, Don Angelo, canon Mitton, parish priest of this Collegiate church of the diocese of Parenzo, questioned Signor Piero De Franceschi of Gollogorizza and Signora Anna, daughter of the noble Signor Tommaso Bembo, and having their mutual consent in words of the present tense, joined them in matrimony in the presence of many, and especially of Signor Pietro Basan of Lindar and of Damian Fiori, witnesses.

rows.lab: Who he married
rows.text: Anna, daughter of «N. Sig.r Tommaso Bembo» — Nobil Signor. Bembo is a Venetian patrician name, and there were Bembo at Valle. A De Franceschi of the bishop of Pedena's village marrying into that, in 1795, is a step this archive had no evidence of.

rows.lab: He is a signore
rows.text: «il Sig.r Piero De Franceschi» — not a plain name in the register but a title, and the same title the parish priest gives the bride's noble father a line later. It sits with what the Gologorica registers already show: a Dominus Josephus Defranceschi standing godparent through the 1760s and 1770s, and a Defranceschi signing as parish priest in the 1780s.

rows.lab: The banns were dispensed
rows.text: All three publications set aside by letter from the bishop of Parenzo. That happens for haste, for distance, or for people whose business the bishop takes an interest in. Piero was marrying a hundred kilometres from home, in another diocese, which alone would explain a good deal of it.

rows.lab: And he brought a neighbour
rows.text: The named witness is «il sig.r Pietro Basan da Lindar». Lindar is the next parish along from Gologorica, inside the same small diocese of Pedena. He travelled to the far coast with a man from home.

rows.lab: And thirty-one years later, Gologorica's own book says the same thing
rows.text:
**Until 30 September 2026 this marriage was known here from one printed study of another parish's registers, a hundred kilometres away.** *The Gologorica* status animarum *of 1826 now carries the couple in the parish's own hand: **«Petrus Defranceschi»**, condition ***civilitas***, born **17 April 1768**, married **21 January 1795**; **«Anna Mater nata Bembo»**, born **5 July 1779**; and their son **«Hermenegildus Filius»**, born **4 October 1803**, who is new to this archive.* **The Valle register says 22 January and Gologorica says the 21st** — *one day, between a marriage register and a household census copying it out three decades later. **The Valle date stands**, being the primary entry. The year, the names and the man's own village all agree.*

**And a brace in the margin against the wife and the son reads** ***«In partibus Venetias … habitant»*** — **they live in the Venetian parts.** *The Bembo bride did not simply move inland. **The household was split across the border**, with Anna and Hermenegildus on the Venetian side — which is the first evidence this archive has of what happened after that wedding.* *(doc — ZM34K-214, M01069326.)*

bembo.caution: No link to the direct line is established, and none should be assumed. This archive's generation 1 is a Giovanni Defranceschi who moved from Gologorica to Gračišće; Piero is a different given name, and the article calls him a member of «una conosciuta famiglia di Gologorizza», a well-known family of the village, which is a household, not a proof of descent. What the entry does is put a dated, quoted, archivally-located Gologorica De Franceschi into the 1790s — the generation before the one this archive's line starts with — with a title, a wife of patrician family and a witness from the next parish.
bembo.friuli: And one line in the article's own voice, worth more than the entry: the family is described, in passing and as established fact, as «una conosciuta famiglia di Gologorizza (emigrata dal Friuli verso il 1700)» — a well-known family of Gologorizza, emigrated from Friuli about 1700. That is a fourth independent witness to the Carnian arrival, after the 1679 headmen's list, Kobler's note on Valentino, and Bertoša and Trogrlić.
bembo.source: «Atti del Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno», vol. 3 (1972), in the study of the registers of the castle of Valle. The entry itself is in the Historijski arhiv Pazin, «Libro de' Matrimoni del Castello di Valle 1737–1815». Read from the copy at the Internet Archive, September 2026. The register itself has not been seen.

palazzetto.heading: There is a coat of arms on the front of the house
palazzetto.lead: Radmila Matejčić's survey of Baroque architecture in Istria, in the «Atti» of Rovigno for 1979, comes to the Habsburg county and describes what happened there in the eighteenth century. Her sentence about who was building is the sentence this archive has been trying to prove for a year. Her next sentence is a thing nobody here knew existed.
palazzetto.quote: Appena a decorrere dal XVIII secolo la nobiltà impiegatizia reclutata per lo più da Fiume e dalla Liburnia, quindi gli artigiani sopraggiunti dalla Carnia e dal Friuli, nello spirito dei tempi, cominciano ad erigere nei sobborghi di Pisino le proprie abitazioni. […] A Moncalvo di Pisino la famiglia Defranceschi innalza il proprio palazzetto con portico ad arcate e blasone sulla facciata, il che testimonia la penetrazione barocca nell'interno dell'Istria.
palazzetto.en: Only from the eighteenth century do the office-holding gentry, recruited mostly from Fiume and Liburnia, and then the artisans arrived from Carnia and Friuli, begin in the spirit of the times to raise houses of their own in the outskirts of Pisino. […] At Moncalvo di Pisino the Defranceschi family raises its own little palace, with an arcaded portico and a coat of arms on the façade, which testifies to the penetration of the Baroque into the interior of Istria.

rows.lab: An architectural historian puts them in the right migration
rows.text: «gli artigiani sopraggiunti dalla Carnia e dal Friuli» — the artisans arrived from Carnia and Friuli. Matejčić is not writing about this family; she is explaining who was building in the Pisino country in the eighteenth century, and the Defranceschi are her example of it. That is a fifth witness to the Carnian crossing, from a discipline that has no stake in the question.

rows.lab: A palazzetto with an arcaded portico
rows.text: Not a house. «il proprio palazzetto con portico ad arcate» — their own small palace with an arcaded loggia, in the modest but harmonious Zopf manner she describes going up around Pisino castle in the same decades. Carlo told Kobler that his great-great-grandfather Giambattista del fu Leonardo built the Gologorica house in 1711; the style Matejčić describes belongs to the later part of the century. Either the house was rebuilt or enlarged, or Carlo's 1711 is the older core of it.

rows.lab: And a blasone on the façade
rows.text: «blasone sulla facciata» — a coat of arms on the front. This archive has an arms page and a problem on it: Carlo describes his family's arms in a private letter to Kobler — a Greek cross crossed above by two arrows, a pomegranate below, a plumed helm over the shield — and the description matches nothing in any armorial consulted here. There is, on the front of the family's own house at Gologorica, a carved shield. Whether it is that one is a question a photograph would answer.

palazzetto.todo: Three things to ask for at Gologorica, and they are the same errand: a photograph of the front of the Defranceschi palazzetto, a photograph of the shield on it, and whether the Croatian conservation service has it on the register of protected buildings. The village has fewer than a hundred people and one road.

parroco.heading: And a Defranceschi was running the parish in 1788
parroco.text: This archive knew that the parish priest of Gologorica in the 1780s was one of the family, because he signs the register «Ego Joannes Mathias Franceschi Parochus». The Spiritual Visitation of the diocese of Pedena of 1788, edited by David Di Paoli Paulovich in the «Atti» for 2012, names him from the other side and gives the date: «A Gollogorizza, mentr'è parroco Mattia Defranceschi (relazione del 7.4.1788)».
parroco.quote: …insegna alla gioventù e agl'adulti in ogni giorno festivo doppo mezzo dì la Dottrina Christiana e doppo di questa si recitano le Litanie di tutti i Santi colle orazioni prescritte e cinque pater, Ave infine e successivamente dà la benedizione col Ciborio; nella mattina poi della festa si dice la Messa verso le 11 ore con l'Esposizione del S.mo, spiega il Vangelo, e dà la benedizione terminata la Messa.
parroco.en: …he teaches the young and the grown, every feast day after midday, the Christian Doctrine, and after it are recited the Litanies of All Saints with the prescribed prayers and five Our Fathers and a Hail Mary at the end, and thereafter he gives the blessing with the ciborium; and on the morning of the feast Mass is said towards eleven o'clock with the Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament, he explains the Gospel, and gives the blessing when the Mass is over.
parroco.why: A Sunday at Gologorica on 7 April 1788, hour by hour, run by a man of this family. He is one of only two Defranceschi this archive can put in the village in the eighteenth century by name — the other is the Dominus Josephus who stands godparent through the 1760s and 1770s — and until now he was a signature. Now he has a working week.

palazzetto.source_palazzo: Radmila Matejčić, on Baroque architecture in Istria, Atti del Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno vol. X (1979), p. 244; David Di Paoli Paulovich, «Pedena. Aspetti storici, rituali e musicali», Atti vol. XLII (2012), pp. 161–242, quoting the Visita Spirituale alla Diocesi di Pedena of 1788. Both read from the Internet Archive copies, September 2026.

casa31.heading: Casa 31, and a birthday that matches to the day
casa31.lead: The two Gologorica microfilms have been in the family's own files for years and were worked through in an earlier round of this project. They were opened again this week to check a single date, and the page turned out to say three things it had not been credited with.

rows.lab: The wife of casa 31 is Theresia, not Marianna
rows.text: The register names her four times and always the same way: «Theresia Defranceschi nata Grach». She is the mother at the baptism of Franciscus Antonius on 13 April 1785 and at the baptism of Joannes Baptista on 13 August 1787, and she stands twice as a godmother in the same book. This archive had her as Marianna, carried forward from a first pass over the film. Theresia is what the page says, in a clear hand, in four places. Corrected here and in the people records.

rows.lab: And her family provided an archpriest
rows.text: At the 1785 baptism the godfather is the «Archipresbyter Grach[ich] Cherbunensis» — the archpriest of Krbune, the next parish over, and of her own surname. The other godparent is a Catharina Defranceschi. The status column for the whole household reads «Cives»: townspeople, not rustics.

rows.lab: The 1785 baptism was dated 1788
rows.text: Folio 3 of the book is headed 1785; the earlier reading had it as 1788. The consequence is that Franciscus Antonius was born three years before this archive thought.

rows.lab: And folio 6 is headed with the wrong year by the priest himself
rows.text: The page carrying the 13 August baptism is headed «1782», in a hand that writes its 7s plainly enough elsewhere. It cannot be 1782: its entries run from 13 April to 7 October, folio 5 before it is headed 1786, and folio 7 after it opens on 16 October 1787 and closes with the record of the spiritual visitation of Gologorica on 8 April 1788. The year is 1787 and the heading is the parish priest's slip. It is worth saying out loud, because a heading is the first thing a reader trusts.

join.heading: What the date does
join.text: «Idem — 13 August — 31 — Joh: Bapt: Defranceschi ex Loco — Joh. Bapt. — Theresia nata Grach — Math. Ortiz ex Novacco, Maria vidua Math. Orlich, Pisinenses — Cives — Civ. — Maria Chrismanich.» A Joannes Baptista Defranceschi baptised at Gologorica, house 31, on 13 August 1787, son of Joannes Baptista and Theresia née Grach.
join.then: The Status Animarum of Gallignana, house 5 — which this archive already holds, and which is the evidence for generation 2 of the direct line — gives its head as «Joan. Bapt. Defranceschi», agricola, born 13 August 1787. Same name, same day, same month, same year, in two parishes eight kilometres apart, in a district where the surname occurs in three households.
join.why: If they are the same man, and the archive's reading is that they are, then generation 2 of this line was born at Gologorica in the casa-31 «detti Leonardi» house and moved to Gračišće — which is exactly the move the family's own chart has always claimed for generation 1, and which no register page has shown until now. It would give the line two more named ancestors: Joannes Baptista of casa 31 and his wife Theresia née Grach, and behind him the Leonardus whose name the branch carries.
join.against: Set against it, honestly. The Gologorica entry gives a baptism and the Gračišće entry a birth, so a same-day baptism is being assumed — usual in this register, but assumed. The Gologorica household is entered «Cives» and the Gračišće man is an «agricola»: a townsman's son who took land, or two different men. And two boys of one name born in one small district on one day is unlikely, not impossible. This is recorded as inferred, not documented, and it stays inferred until the Gračišće marriage of 1819 or a death entry names his father.

casa31.source_casa31: Državni arhiv u Pazinu, microfilm ZM34K-214, Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880: folio 3 (M01069015), folio 6 (M01069018) and folio 7 (M01069019), read from the family's own copies of the film in September 2026. The Gallignana Status Animarum, house 5, is DAPA ZM34K 217, M01072071, supplied by the archive on 24 June 2021.

house.heading: The house at Gologorica, and the shield on it
house.lead: This archive published, this morning, an architectural historian's sentence from 1979 — «A Moncalvo di Pisino la famiglia Defranceschi innalza il proprio palazzetto con portico ad arcate e blasone sulla facciata» — and wrote underneath it that somebody should go and photograph that shield, and that it had just gone from a guess to a target. The photographs came the same day.

rows.lab: It is standing, and it is a palazzetto
rows.text: A long white block of two and three storeys under a tiled roof carried on projecting wooden brackets, with a tall Istrian chimney of dressed stone. At the near end, exactly as Matejčić describes it, an arcaded loggia: two round arches on stone columns, a stone balustrade, and a flight of stone steps up to it from the lane. Palms and a chestnut in front of it, a dry-stone wall, and a motorbike parked under the balcony. It is a lived-in house on a village street.

rows.lab: And the builder cut his name into the front of it
rows.text: Set into the wall, a plain framed tablet in Roman capitals: «[A]N.O DOMINI [17…] / GIO: BATISTA / DE FRANCESCHI / FECCE FARE PER SE / ET HEREDI SVOI» — in the year of Our Lord, Gio. Batista De Franceschi had this made for himself and his heirs. The year is worn and this archive will not put a figure on it from these photographs. The name is not worn at all.

rows.lab: Between the tablet and the arms, a Madonna
rows.text: An aedicule with scrolled volutes and a moulded cornice, framing a marble relief: a haloed woman, seated or half-kneeling, her arms flung wide, drapery falling around her. It is a devotional panel set into a private house, of the kind a family put up when it had money and meant to be seen to have it.

arms.heading: And at the top of the façade, the coat of arms
arms.text: An oval cartouche in high relief, with curling mantling to either side and, above it, a helm with a crest and plumes. On the oval shield: in the upper part a cross, crossed diagonally by two straight objects; beneath them a horizontal band; and in the lower part a round fruit. Around the rim of the oval, cut in small capitals, a circular legend — the letters «…A DE FRANCESCHI FIERI…» are legible on the left of it and further letters on the right that this archive will not guess at from a photograph taken from below.
arms.carlo: Now set that beside what Carlo De Franceschi wrote privately to Giovanni Kobler in about 1873, which this archive has had on its arms page for a year and could not match to anything: «Abbiamo arma: nella parte superiore dello scudo una croce greca attraversata da due frecce, nell'inferiore un pomo granato; sopra lo scudo un elmo piumato.» We have arms: in the upper part of the shield a Greek cross crossed by two arrows, in the lower a pomegranate; above the shield a plumed helm.
arms.verdict: A cross crossed by two arrows. A pomegranate below. A plumed helm above the shield. That is what Carlo said his family bore, in a private letter to a friend, with nothing to gain by it. It is what is carved on the front of the house. This archive spent a long time noting that his description matched no entry in any armorial it could find, and treating that as a difficulty. It was not a difficulty. It was the point. He was not copying a catalogue. He was describing the stone he had grown up looking at.

house.plaque: Read in full now, from a frontal photograph, and the archive's earlier partial reading was wrong in one word. The tablet says:  «IN QVESTA CASA AVITA / NACQVE E MORÌ / CARLO DE FRANCESCHI / PATRIOTTA FERVENTE / ARCHEOLOGO E STORICO / AGLI STVDI DELLA SVA ISTRIA / OPEROSO / · MDCCCIX — MDCCCXCIII ·»  In this ancestral house were born and died Carlo De Franceschi, fervent patriot, archaeologist and historian, industrious in the study of his Istria. 1809–1893.  Three things it gives that the archive did not have. «Casa avita» — the ancestral house, not merely the house: whoever cut this knew the building was older than the man. «Nacque e morì» — he was born in it and he died in it, which the press notices of 1893 implied and this states. And MDCCCIX again, a third independent witness for 1809 against the obituary that printed 1810. The archive had guessed «patriota istriano» from an oblique photograph; the stone says «patriotta fervente», with two t's.
closes: Matejčić described it in 1979 from the outside and this archive took her word for it. It is there, with the arcaded portico she names.

Carlo told Kobler that his great-great-grandfather «Giambattista del fu Leonardo» built the house in 1711. The tablet on the wall says Gio. Batista De Franceschi had it made for himself and his heirs. The name on the stone is the name in the letter.
Carlo's private blazon — cross, two arrows, pomegranate, plumed helm — is on the façade. The description and the carving agree.

The house at Seget near Umag and the tomb at Umag both carry a lion rampant with a star under a coronet. The house at Gologorica carries a cross, two arrows and a pomegranate. Two families of one surname in one province, and they never used each other's arms.
house.todo: What is still wanted, and it is small: the year on the builder's tablet, the circular legend around the cartouche, and the full text of the Carlo plaque. All three are shallow carving in flat light. A straight-on photograph in low raking sun, early or late, would give all of it.
house.source_house: Photographed by the family at Gologorica, 2026: the house from the lane and from the field wall, the loggia end, the builder's tablet, the memorial tablet, the Madonna relief, and the arms in close-up. Carlo's blazon is from «Lettere di Carlo De Franceschi a Giovanni Kobler», printed 1928.
house.legend: And the circular legend round the cartouche is partly recovered. Two readers working independently from different photographs, each unwrapping the ellipse and re-reading it arc by arc, agree on two words and on the direction: it runs clockwise, letter-tops outward, beginning at the lower left and ending at the lower right, with the top of the oval eroded away. What survives: «… [a name ending in ‑A] · DE · FRANCESCHI · FIERI · […lost across the top…] PERMISIT …»  That is Latin, not Italian, and it is the ordinary donor's formula — fieri … permisit, allowed this to be made. So the two tablets on this façade are in two languages: the builder's, in Italian, says GIO: BATISTA DE FRANCESCHI FECCE FARE PER SE ET HEREDI SVOI — had it made for himself and his heirs. The arms above it say the same thing in Latin. The name in the legend ends in ‑A, which is what a Battista would end in, but the nine or ten letters before it are worn past reading and the archive is not going to supply them.
house.number: The house is number 22. A blue-and-white enamel plate on the wall between the loggia arches, and the archive has wanted a street address for it since the day it learned the house was still standing.

year.heading: And the year is on the stone: ANNO DOMNI 1711
year.text: This archive has been asking for the year on the builder's tablet since the day it learned the house was standing, and it has now been photographed close and read. The tablet, in a recessed panel under a moulded cornice, reads:  «ANNO · DOMNI · 1711 / GION · BATISTA / DE · FRANCESCHI / FECCE · FARE · PE[R] · SE / ET · HEREDI · SVOI»  In the year of the Lord 1711, Gion Batista de Franceschi had it made for himself and his heirs.
year.why: 1711 is the year Carlo De Franceschi gave Giovanni Kobler, privately, in a letter of about 1873: that his great-great-grandfather Giambattista del fu Leonardo built the Gologorica house in 1711. For a hundred and fifty years that has been family tradition reported at second hand in a printed correspondence. It is cut in the wall of the house.
year.careful: Said carefully, because a reading that confirms what you hoped for is the one to distrust. Four numerals are clean and unarguable — 1, 7, 1, 1 — each with the same serifed top and foot, sitting in one band. To the right of the last there is a further mark: a horizontal stroke meeting a vertical. One reader took it for the open-form 4 of an old hand and put 1714 at about one chance in three. Enlarged, that vertical runs the full depth of the panel, well above and below the digits' band, and meets the panel's inner border; the horizontal sits lower than the tops of the numerals. It reads to this archive as the border and a crack rather than a fifth digit, and 1711 is the reading published. It is one minute's work with a torch held at a low angle to settle it outright, and it is on the return list.
year.gion: One correction while the tablet is in focus. This site has been printing the name as «GIO: BATISTA», an abbreviation. It is not abbreviated. The stone reads GION · BATISTA — with an N, unambiguous at magnification, and with the interpuncts that separate every word on the panel. Gion for Giovanni is the Venetian-dialect form. The man who built the house in 1711 signed himself on it in the vernacular of the coast, not in Tuscan and not in Latin — and then set the arms above with a Latin legend. Both are on the same wall.

fabricated.heading: A warning, kept here on purpose: the day an image model rewrote this stone
fabricated.lead: In September 2026 this archive began commissioning constructed illustrations from written briefs. One of them was asked, in good faith, to «enhance» the family's own photographs of the builder's tablet. What came back was not an enhancement. Image models do not enhance; they regenerate. It is being recorded here, in full, because it is the most instructive thing that has happened to this project all year.

rows.lab: What the stone says
rows.text: Photographed close, in the wall, and read letter by letter: «ANNO · DOMNI · 1711 / GION · BATISTA / DE · FRANCESCHI / FECCE · FARE · PE[R] · SE / ET · HEREDI · SVOI». Italian. Arabic numerals. Five lines. And 1711 is the year Carlo De Franceschi gave Giovanni Kobler privately in about 1873 — that his great-great-grandfather Giambattista del fu Leonardo built the house in 1711. Two independent witnesses, a hundred and sixty years apart, agreeing on a year and a name.

rows.lab: What the model produced
rows.text: A photorealistic marble tablet in a wall, in convincing raking light, with five lines of clean Roman capitals: «ANNO · DOMINI · MDCLXV / GLORIA · DEO · OMNIPOTENTI / DE · FRANCESCHI / PATERNO · ET · MATERNO / NOMINE · DEX · VOTO». Latin. Roman numerals. Five lines. It kept the shape of the real thing and replaced every word in it.

rows.lab: Why that is worse than a bad drawing
rows.text: MDCLXV is 1665. Not 1711. A single plausible-looking image, circulated once, would put a rival date on the founding stone of this family and set it against the only two witnesses there are. It would not look like an error; it would look like a better photograph. And the Latin is not even sound — «DEX VOTO» is not a phrase; it is a machine's approximation of «ex voto».

rows.lab: So it is not on this site, and it is not going to be
rows.text: The file is kept in this project's source library under a filename that says what it is: WITHHELD, FABRICATED, contradicts the verified 1711 reading, not a photograph, do not circulate. It is kept rather than deleted because the next person to try this — including a future version of this archive — should be able to see exactly how convincing the failure looked.

rows.lab: And the rule it produced
rows.text: No image model is ever asked to render an inscription, a coat of arms, a signature, a document or any other carrying of text on this site. Where a real carved stone appears in a constructed illustration, its panel is left blank and the words are set in the caption underneath, where they can be footnoted. The drawn view of the house published above this section has an empty tablet for exactly that reason.

fabricated.source_fab: The verified reading is from the family's own close photographs of the tablet at Gologorica, 2026, checked against Carlo De Franceschi's letter to Giovanni Kobler printed in «Fiume» (1928). The fabricated version is a Gemini image generated September 2026 and archived unpublished.

carlograve.heading: «L'illustre storiografo riposa nell'umile cimitero» — and here it is
carlograve.lead: «Il giovine Pensiero» of 25 January 1893 gave this archive a line it had been looking for without knowing it: the illustrious historian rests in the humble cemetery of his own village. The family has now walked into that cemetery. The grave is not humble. It is the largest thing in it.
carlograve.what: A stone screen wall with a cross on top and, set into it, three panels. In the middle, framed by fluted pilasters under a cornice, a slab of rose-veined marble. To either side, a grey pedimented tablet, and in the peak of each pediment a carved shield under a five-pointed coronet. In front, a broad flat slab with iron lifting rings — the vault beneath. Over the centre panel, cut in relief, a circle: a serpent with its tail in its mouth. And a few metres off, its own stone cross with a marble plate.

centre.q: CARLO de FRANCESCHI / STORIOGRAFO DELL'ISTRIA / STRENVO ASSERTORE / DELL'ITALIANITÀ DELLA SVA TERRA / MDCCCIX — MDCCCXCIII
centre.en: Carlo de Franceschi, historiographer of Istria, strenuous asserter of the Italianness of his land. 1809–1893.
centre.why: MDCCCIX. The two Istrian papers that buried him in January 1893 both gave 17 October and one of them gave 1810; the archive published that discrepancy and left it open. The stone his family cut says 1809, which is what the reference works say. And the epitaph makes no attempt to soften what he was for: «strenuo assertore dell'italianità della sua terra» is a political sentence, chosen by his own people, and it is the same sentence this archive spent the morning documenting from Daniela Simon's monograph and from Naša Sloga.

left: This archive's research log has carried, as an open question, «Carlo's own marriage — which would give his wife's name, still missing from this archive». It is on the tablet. Maria Micheli, born at Pisino in 1828, died at Parenzo in 1880, thirteen years before her husband.
Virginia, daughter of the late Carlo
