And this answers a second open question. The Poreč burial register holds a Virginia, daughter of a Carlo De Franceschi, buried in August 1876 aged eighteen, and the archive could not prove she was his. Born 1858, dead 1876: eighteen. She was.
Pietro, son of the late Carlo, magistrate
Born at Rovigno in the year his father was still an assessor there, died at Moncalvo aged thirty. A magistrate, like his father before 1854.
right: Faustina, daughter of the late Carlo
Giulio, son of the late Carlo, academic painter

«PITTORE ACCADEMICO». Carlo's son was a painter, trained in an academy, and he came home to the village to die at eighty-six — nine years after his brother Camillo published their father's memoirs, and two years before the war reached Istria.
Silvia de Franceschi, daughter of the late Francesco, wife of Camillo
Camillo the historian married a De Franceschi — a woman of the same surname, daughter of a Francesco, born in this village. The family married back into itself.
carlograve.armella: And the separate cross, a few metres away, with its own marble plate: «ARMELLA de FRANCESCHI / MORTA A 48 ANNI / IL 6 MAGGIO 1920 / EBBE QUI LAGRIMATA SEPOLTURA / IL MARITO GIULIO». Armella de Franceschi, dead at forty-eight on 6 May 1920, was given here a tearful burial; her husband Giulio placed the stone. Giulio is the painter on the tablet behind her, who outlived her by twenty-two years.
carlograve.arms: And now the thing that matters most for this archive. In the pediment of each of the two tablets, and again cut into the stone urn standing on the slab, is the same shield: under a five-pointed coronet, a cross with two arrows crossing it diagonally behind, a horizontal band beneath them, and under the band a pomegranate. That is Carlo's blazon exactly as he described it to Kobler about 1873 — «nella parte superiore dello scudo una croce greca attraversata da due frecce, nell'inferiore un pomo granato». It is on his house, and it is on his grave, three times over. The archive spent a year treating his description as unverifiable because it matched no commercial armorial. It matches the stone.
carlograve.todo: Two things left in the frame that are not this family's: a broken marble slab propped against the enclosure wall, in Slovene — «FLEGAR FRANJO ✱ 2.3.1872 ✝ 19.10.1940 … LAHKA IN BILA ZEMLJA», may the earth be light on them — and the modern graves of the Rabar, Sinčić and Krošnjak alongside. The village bell tower stands over all of it.
carlograve.source_grave: Photographed by the family at the Gologorica cemetery, 2026: the monument entire and from the side, the three panels, both pediment shields in close-up, the ouroboros roundel, the carved urn, and the Armella cross. All transcriptions above are from those photographs.

first1661.heading: 1661 — the first time the name is written in this village
first1661.lead: The Zagreb librarians' 2022 article on the family's book collection contains, in one clause of one sentence, the earliest dated fact this archive has about the family at Gologorica. It is not presented as a discovery. It is stated the way you state something everybody in the local literature knows.
first1661.quote: Obitelj De Franceschi doselila se u Istru, točnije Gologoricu kraj Pazina, iz Karnije (Furlanija) sredinom 17. stoljeća u jednom od migracijskih valova… Prezime se prvi put spominje 1661. godine u knjizi krštenih župe Gologorice. U lozi je bilo članova iz različitih društvenih slojeva, zanimanja i dužnosti (ratari, trgovci, tkalci, pravnici, župani, notari, liječnici, odvjetnici i dr.)
first1661.en: The De Franceschi family moved into Istria, more precisely to Gologorica near Pazin, from Carnia (Friuli) in the middle of the seventeenth century in one of the migration waves. The surname is first mentioned in 1661 in the baptismal register of the parish of Gologorica. The line contained members of various social strata, occupations and offices — farmers, merchants, weavers, jurists, headmen, notaries, physicians, advocates and others.

rows.lab: What that gives this archive
rows.text: A year and a book. Not a tradition, not a nineteenth-century recollection, not a review's round number — the baptismal register of the parish of Gologorica, 1661. That register exists, it is in the state archive at Pazin, and this project has already learned how to read that hand and that Latin. It is now the single most specific unopened target the archive has, and it is of exactly the kind it has just spent a fortnight proving it can do.

rows.lab: And it fixes the tension on the other pages
rows.text: Four accounts have given four dates for the crossing: the sixteenth century, 1610, the mid-seventeenth century, about 1700. 1661 is a document, and it sits inside the mid-seventeenth-century answer. It does not overturn the others — the Rijeka fond genuinely starts at 1610, and Hauptmann in 1945 reported an inventory from the beginning of the seventeenth century in the house itself. What 1661 gives is a floor under one of them.

rows.lab: «Ratari, trgovci, tkalci»
rows.text: Farmers, merchants and weavers, before the jurists and physicians. Weavers. The 1679 headmen's list from the Val di Gorto that this archive published is explicitly a list of «tessitori», and Brhan's study of the migration says the weavers came especially from the Quartiere di Socchieve. The trade runs the whole length of the road.

first1661.biotz: The same article also names the man this archive had only as «a Belgian from the diocese of Liège». He was Charles Antoine Biotz, and it was he «koji za svog ubirača poreza postavlja Gian Pietra De Franceschija, sina Gian Battiste, gologoričkog župana» — who appointed as his tax-collector Gian Pietro De Franceschi, son of Gian Battista, headman of Gologorica. Gologorica had been a benefice of the bishops of Pićan in the seventeenth century; it became Biotz's fief in the eighteenth; and after the abolition of feudalism in 1848 it became a commune.
first1661.hauptmann: And it prints in full the report Ferdinand Hauptmann made on the archives at Gola Gorica, dated Zagreb, 12 August 1945 — after the villa had been used as a militia billet and the district committee at Čepić had carried off four cartloads. He found the library «za istarska pitanja upravo uzorna», exemplary for Istrian questions, and he wrote: «Plemićka porodica De Franceschi boravi, prema nađenom materijalu, bar od početka XVII. stoljeća u Goloj Gorici… Sačuvan je inventar iz početka XVII. stoljeća, koji pruža lijep uvid u te prilike.» The noble De Franceschi family has lived, according to the material found, at least since the beginning of the seventeenth century at Gologorica; and an inventory from the beginning of the seventeenth century is preserved, which gives a fine insight into those circumstances. Among the rest he lists: the protocols of the Pićan bishop Aldrago Antonio de Piccardi; «Atti di nomine e investiture dai parocci della Contea di Pisino», 1728–1776; a complete population list of Rovinj 1650–1736; the urbarium of the castle of Momiano of 1584–5 in two volumes; a Glagolitic parish register of Hum from the mid-seventeenth century; and parchments and papal bulls from 1201 onwards.

warning.lab: And a warning this archive must act on
warning.text: The same authors, describing the Rijeka fond, state plainly: «ustanovljeno je da je u kutijama došlo do spajanja fondova dviju obitelji De Franceschi koje zajedno nemaju ništa osim istarskog zavičaja i prezimena» — it was established that in the boxes the fonds of two De Franceschi families had been merged, families which have nothing in common but an Istrian homeland and a surname. And the state archive at Rijeka holds a separate fond titled «Obitelj de Franceschi iz Šegeta» — the De Franceschi family of Seget. This site publishes both a Gologorica line and a Seget line and has always been careful to keep them apart; the carvings say the same thing, since the Seget-Umag arms are a lion and a star and the Gologorica arms a cross, two arrows and a pomegranate. But any fact this archive has taken from a Rijeka box now has to be checked against which family that box belonged to. That is a real piece of housekeeping and it is going on the research log.

first1661.source_1661: Anita Marin, Martina Jurišić and Alena Matijaca, «Zbirka obitelji De Franceschi u Nacionalnoj i sveučilišnoj knjižnici u Zagrebu – prilog istraživanju», Libellarium 13/2 (2022), pp. 3–28, open access, doi 10.15291/libellarium.3708. Read September 2026 and held in this project's source library. The Hauptmann report is their Appendix 1, reproduced from Leideck 2015.

press.heading: The village in the Croatian press, which did not like them
press.lead: «Naša sloga» was the Croatian national paper of Istria, and Carlo De Franceschi was among the men it existed to oppose. That makes it a hostile witness, and hostile witnesses are useful: it had no reason to flatter this family and every reason to place it precisely. Seventy mentions of Gologorica across the digitised Croatian press, and four of them are about this house.

rows.lab: 27 February 1890 — the historian's son in the dock
rows.text: A trial at Pazin over petards. «Medju odsudjenimi nalazi se i jedan Istran talijanske narodnosti, sin naime talijanskoga povjesničara gospodina Karla de Franceschi-a posjednika iz Gologorice (po njegovu Moncalvo) obćine Pazin.» Among those condemned is an Istrian of Italian nationality, namely the son of the Italian historian Mr Karlo de Franceschi, landowner of Gologorica — in his usage Moncalvo — commune of Pazin. A seal reading «Circolo Garibaldi sezione Pisino» was produced at the hearing. That son is Camillo, and the Trieste society's own guide says he was sentenced to two years' hard imprisonment at Gradisca after an explosion at the unveiling of a monument in 1889. Here is the other side reporting it — and note how it fixes the father: landowner, of Gologorica, «po njegovu Moncalvo», in his usage Moncalvo. Even the name of the village was contested.

rows.lab: 22 July 1894 — a riot, and two villagers of the name
rows.text: «Gologorica pred sudom» — Gologorica before the court — ran in five instalments from 21 November 1895 to 2 January 1896. Two men of this surname appear in it, and not as gentry. 28 November 1895: «porinuli ga neki u konobu Antuna Defranceschi» — some of them shoved him into Antun Defranceschi's tavern. 5 December 1895: «za koju mu je kasnije Viktor Defranceschi rekao, da je Frane Rabar» — Viktor Defranceschi told him afterwards that it was Frane Rabar. Rabar is the surname on the stone standing next to the family monument in that cemetery today.

rows.lab: 5 September 1907 — the farm has a name
rows.text: A debate about a new road: «posto bijaše cesta istočno od Gologorice izmjerena, kojom bi se dolina Raše kod stancije Defranceschi (Zamporovica) jedino zavojima dotaklo» — since a road east of Gologorica had been surveyed, which would reach the Raša valley at the Defranceschi farmstead (Zamporovica) only by hairpins. The same page also spells it Zamperovica. A stancija is a farmstead, and this one has a place-name of its own. It is a thing to look for in the cadastre, and it is the family's land under a name this archive has never seen.

rows.lab: 26 May 1921 — and what the book had become
rows.text: A Čakavian dialogue in «Pučki prijatelj», two men arguing about the history of Lovran: «Neka zame storiju od De Franceschi, onega z Gologorice, pa će na str. 85. nać ovo ča sam ti ja rekal… Ča je oni De Franceschi pisal, to je za njih bilo od vavek sveto Pismo.» Let him take De Franceschi's history — the one from Gologorica — and on page 85 he'll find what I told him… What that De Franceschi wrote was for them always Holy Scripture. Written in dialect, twenty-eight years after his death, by people on the other side of the argument, and they are still checking him page by page.

press.source_press: «Naša sloga» (Trieste and Pula, 1870–1915) and «Pučki prijatelj» (Krk), from the digitised Croatian newspapers of the National and University Library, dnc.nsk.hr, searched September 2026. Every hit resolves to a stable page image and OCR text at DataServices/ImageView.aspx and TextView.aspx.

lives.heading: Eighty-eight people, and some of what happened to them
lives.lead: The Gologorica and Gračišće household books, read frame by frame, give something close to ninety distinct people of this surname between 1785 and 1945, in nine households. Most of them are a name and two dates. A few of them the priest wrote more about, and those entries are why parish books are worth reading rather than indexing.

rows.lab: 28 October 1898 — a soldier at Pola
rows.text: «Joannes, Aloysius», son of Leonardus of house 8, born 4 November 1876. Against his death, aged twenty-one years eleven months and twenty-four days: «Miles Polae sclopeto se interfecit» — a soldier, at Pola, he killed himself with a gun. The household page says it in slightly different words, «ictus bolae sclopeti se interfecit», and the parish index repeats it. Two entries in two books, and neither of them looks away.

rows.lab: 13 August 1914 — Ersilia
rows.text: «Ersilia-Maria», of house 87, born 8 December 1878, died at thirty-five years eight months and five days, and the adnotatio reads «in nosocomio (amens)» — in hospital, of unsound mind. Nine days after the war began. That is the whole record of her.

rows.lab: 27 January 1922 — Leopoldus, at Trieste
rows.text: «Mortuus Tergesti in nosocomio.» Leopoldus Antonius, of house 8, born 29 January 1884, died in hospital at Trieste two days before his thirty-eighth birthday, leaving a wife and children whose page carries a faint pencil note about emigrating.

rows.lab: Four of one household in America
rows.text: Against four of the thirteen children of Antonius the mason, the priest wrote «degit Americae» — he lives in America. Nicephorus born 1890, Josephus born 1892, Albina born 1900, Joachim born 1907. One of those, Albina, this archive has already followed onto the Conte Rosso out of Genoa in August 1922. The other three are still to be found.

rows.lab: And the trades
rows.text: Across the nine households the conditio column runs: agricola, lapidarius, murator, sartor, civis, mercator, nauta, obstetrix — and, for Julius of house 9, «director scholae industrialis», director of the industrial school. A tailor born in 1785, a stonecutter, masons, a midwife, merchants, a sailor and a headmaster, in one surname in one village.

lives.method: One thing about how this was read, because it is the reason to trust it. Where the register gives an age at death in years, months and days, that arithmetic can be checked against the birth date — and on every page where both appear, it computes exactly. Antonius of house 7 at 63 years 2 months 14 days; Leonardus at 70 years 11 months 7 days; Aloysius of house 87 at 80 years 7 months 0 days; Armella at 48 years 5 months 29 days; Julius at 86 years and 21 days. That internal check settled several ambiguous digits and corrected four readings taken from the parish index, where the household page and the index disagreed. The household page won every time.
lives.source_lives: Državni arhiv u Pazinu, Status Animarum of Gologorica and Gračišće — houses 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 19, 24 and 87, the parish repertorium, and the seniority lists of 1899 and 1903. Photographed from the reading-room screens by the family, autumn 2026, and read image by image by two independent readers whose transcriptions were compared.

before1661.heading: Gologorica before the family: six weddings, a boundary quarrel, and no De Franceschi anywhere
before1661.lead: A document David sent had been read and filed under a placeholder name, which meant this archive had its contents and not its title. It is Robert Kurelić's doctoral thesis, «Eagle and Lion: Integration, Immigration, and Conflict on the Istrian Frontier in the Sixteenth Century» — two hundred and twenty-one pages on precisely the county and the border this family later crossed. It puts named people in Gologorica three-quarters of a century before the family appears there, and none of them is a De Franceschi.

rows.lab: The Boljun book, written in Glagolitic
rows.text: The parish of Boljun, eight kilometres north of Gologorica, kept its registers in Glagolitic script: marriages from 1576, baptisms from 1598, confirmations from 1588. The original is in the archive of the Croatian Academy at Zagreb, III c 4, and Dražen Vlahov published it in facsimile with a Latin transliteration. Kurelić went through it to ask a political question — whether Habsburg subjects avoided marrying Venetian ones — and in doing so printed the names.

rows.lab: Six Gologorica marriages, 1585–1608
rows.text: Klara Kovač and Anton Kaligarić, 1585. Grgora Matijašić and a Gašparić, 1590. Agata Ilijašić and Šimun Gašparić, 1603. Marina Sergović and Juraj Ančić, 1607. Ivana Križmanić and Ivan Gortan, 1608. Ivan Cinić and an Elena, 1608. Six households of Gologorica, named, dated, and all of them Slavic — Kovač, Kaligarić, Matijašić, Gašparić, Ilijašić, Sergović, Ančić, Križmanić, Gortan, Cinić.

rows.lab: And what is not there
rows.text: No De Franceschi. Not in the Gologorica marriages, not anywhere in two hundred and twenty-one pages about the sixteenth-century county of Pazin. That is a controlled negative and it is worth as much as a positive: the family's first recorded appearance at Moncalvo is 1661, Carlo told Kobler in 1876 that «si stabilirono in Istria intorno al 1700», and the village that Gian Battista married into in the 1660s was a Slavic village of Kovači and Gašparići that had been there all along.

rows.lab: The village itself is older than the family by two centuries
rows.text: Kurelić lists the boundary disputes of the county, and one of them is «Gologorica and Tremaun, 19 February 1472», with the captain of Pazin sitting as one of the commissioners. The original is in the Haus-, Hof- und Staatsarchiv in Vienna; Milko Kos published a Croatian translation in «Pet razvodov», pp. 189–202. That is the earliest document naming Gologorica that this archive has found — 189 years before the family arrives in it.

rows.lab: And a gift for the Svetvinčenat work
rows.text: In a footnote listing the oldest surviving parish registers of Istria, Kurelić gives Svetvinčenat baptisms from 1569 and marriages from 1581 — among the very oldest in the province, and all in the State Archive at Pazin. The Carnian household there was traced through a household book of 1734. The registers behind it run a hundred and sixty-five years further back than that.

before1661.source_k: Robert Kurelić, «Eagle and Lion: Integration, Immigration, and Conflict on the Istrian Frontier in the Sixteenth Century», doctoral dissertation, Central European University, Budapest — Table 1 and its map; the register footnotes at pp. 30 and 55; the boundary-dispute footnote at p. 55. Behind it: Dražen Vlahov, «Matična knjiga iz Boljuna», facsimile and transliteration of Arhiv HAZU III c 4. Held in this project's source library.

fromtree.heading: Five people out of the family's own tree that this archive had nothing on
fromtree.lead: David's live MyHeritage tree was read directly in September 2026 — 459 individuals of the surname. Most of it agreed with what is published here. These did not, because this site had never heard of them.

rows.lab: Antonius Franciscus Defranceschi — Gologorica to Dachau
rows.text: **Born at Gologorica on 31 January 1909. Died at Dachau on 7 August 1945.** The camp was liberated on 29 April 1945, so a death there in August is a death among the thousands who did not survive being freed — typhus was still killing the liberated well into the summer. He was thirty-six. Nothing else about him is in this archive, and finding out how a man from this village came to be in that camp is now a piece of work in its own right.

rows.lab: Giuseppe de Franceschi — Gračišće to New York
rows.text: **Born at Gračišće on 12 March 1892, died in New York City on 26 April 1940**, with six separate citations behind him in the tree. This site's Diaspora page has argued that the United States records held only one family it could trace back to Gračišće — Basilio and Dario, of Gallignana. Here is a second, and a much better documented one.

rows.lab: Bruno Defranceschi — born in the house, died in this decade
rows.text: **Born at Gologorica on 20 November 1942, died 15 January 2023.** This archive has published that the surname is down to about ten people in Croatia and that the last of the Gologorica line left. A man born in that village in the middle of the war lived until two years ago.

rows.lab: Anna Maria Francisca, Gologorica to Trieste
rows.text: Born at Gologorica 28 October 1860, married a Domazetovich, **died at Trieste on 22 June 1941**. One more of the quiet westward moves the archive keeps finding one at a time.

rows.lab: And the eighteenth-century household, with its dates
rows.text: The tree carries a run of Gologorica deaths this site has never had: **Francesco, died 13 September 1719. Gian Battista, born 1673, died 11 September 1743. Cattarina, died 28 September 1740. Gisanna, born 1684, died 20 April 1774. Antonius, born 1742, died 17 September 1802. Cattarina, born 1756, died 21 May 1792. Gian Battista, born 1753, died 23 January 1813.** Set beside the 1711 tablet and Carlo's «il vecchio stipite» dead in November 1686, that is most of a century of the house filled in.

fromtree.source_ft: David Defranceski's live MyHeritage tree, read 7 September 2026. Dates as the tree gives them; the citations behind them, where they exist, are FamilySearch record links entered by the family.

fieldplates.heading: The house and the ground, photographed
fieldplates.lead: The family went to Gologorica in 2026 and came back with a hundred and seventy-five frames. Until now this archive has quoted from them and never shown them. These eleven are the ones that carry evidence: the tablet the house was built under, the arms Carlo described in a private letter, the same arms cut twice in the cemetery a century apart, and the building Radmila Matejčić described in 1979 from the outside without ever naming who lived in it.
fieldplates.note: Living people are in many of the other frames and are left out of this archive, as everywhere else on the site. What is published here is stone.

kasteli2012.heading: An architectural survey of the village — and a hard date for the lease
kasteli2012.lead: Krešimir Regan and Branko Nadilo's series on the Istrian castles ran in «Građevinar» in 2012, and the instalment on the fortified places north of the Čepić field takes Gologorica apart building by building. It is a civil-engineering journal rather than a genealogy, which is why it is useful: it has no interest in the family and describes the house as a structure. It also gives the benefice a date this archive did not have.

rows.lab: The house, as an architect sees it
rows.text: «Na trgu je pokraj crkve velika kamena **palača obitelji De Franceschi**, dvokatna građevina s balkonom i **portalom iz 1711.**, ukrašena **grbom i natpisom te reljefom s prikazom Isusa**. Mnogi drže da je to **jedan od najljepših primjera skromne palače seoskih posjednika**, funkcionalna i jednostavna u svojim dimenzijama i ukrasima.» — On the square beside the church is the large stone palace of the De Franceschi family, a two-storey building with a balcony and a portal of 1711, ornamented with a coat of arms, an inscription, and **a relief showing Jesus**. Many hold it one of the finest examples of the modest palace of a rural landowner, functional and plain in its dimensions and its ornament.

rows.lab: Which settles something this site got wrong once
rows.text: When this archive first tried to have the house drawn, it said the relief panels above the door were invented by the image model, then corrected itself from the family's own photographs, which show an aedicule with scrolled volutes and a haloed figure. A published architectural survey now names it: **a relief of Christ.** The tablet, the arms and the figure are all real, all of 1711, and all still there.

rows.lab: The benefice, with dates and a list of holders
rows.text: This is the correction that matters. Gologorica changed hands until **1443**, when the **provost of Pazin, Andreas Schuel**, bought it and with other property founded a **benefice** — an endowment to maintain priests bound to say Mass three times a week in St Nicholas's at Pazin. The Emperor **Frederick III** then took the right of appointment. The holders were, to the eighteenth century, mostly **the captains of Pazin or the bishops of Pedena**; then the **Marquis de Prié**; then **Charles Antoine Biotz**; and «**naposljetku od 1772. obitelj De Franceschi koja je gologorički beneficij držala u zakupu do ukidanja feudalnih odnosa 1848. godine**» — and finally, **from 1772, the De Franceschi family, who held the Gologorica benefice on lease until the abolition of feudal relations in 1848**.

rows.lab: How that sits with Carlo
rows.text: This site has carried the lease from Carlo's own letter to Kobler — the «affitto fermo» of the bishop of Pedena, renewed by every bishop, which is why the village is missing from the 1498 urbarium: «perchè ne era Dominus il vescovo di Pedena». The two accounts fit together rather than contradict. The bishops were among the earlier holders of an endowment founded in 1443; **the family took the lease of it in 1772 and kept it for seventy-six years**, through the suppression of the see of Pedena in 1788 and out the other side, until feudal tenure itself was abolished. Seventy-six years is a long time to be the man who collects, and it is the economic fact behind everything else on this page.

rows.lab: And the village they were collecting in
rows.text: The historic core sits on a narrow ridge running north to south. The walls were an elongated irregular quadrangle; only a small stretch survives with **the north gate**, the rest pulled down in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries or built into the fronts of the houses. **Deep ditches with drawbridges** defended the north and south ends and were gradually filled in and turned into gardens and vineyards. The walls are thought to be sixteenth-century, put up after Gologorica had been **taken and burned in 1463, 1508 and 1511**.

rows.lab: The churches
rows.text: The parish church of **Sts Peter and Paul** is a seventeenth-century single-nave baroque rebuilding of an older Gothic church, of which there survive a **Glagolitic inscription of the priest Juraj Kaligarić, 1595**, an **Imago pietatis relief of 1446**, and a fifteenth-century chalice. The bell tower was begun in late Gothic and finished in **1740** — twenty-four metres, three storeys, fine ashlar, biforate openings on the third. And above the north entrance, by the pond, the oldest building of all: the small **Romanesque church of the Blessed Virgin Mary**.

rows.lab: One more thing out of this village
rows.text: «Iz Gologorice potječe i plovan Mikula Gologorički, notar i pisac hrvatske glagoljaške verzije često spominjanoga **Istarskog razvoda iz 1325**.» — From Gologorica came the parish priest **Mikula Gologorički**, notary, and the writer of the **Croatian Glagolitic version of the Istrian Boundary Settlement of 1325** — the great delimitation between the patriarch of Aquileia, the count of Gorizia and Pazin, and Venice. One of the foundation documents of Croatian literacy was written by the priest of this parish, three hundred and fifty years before the family reached it.

kasteli2012.source_kasteli: Krešimir Regan and Branko Nadilo, «Istarski kašteli: utvrđeni gradovi i naselja sjeverno od Čepićkog polja», in «Građevinar» 64 (2012) 6, pp. 515–522. Supplied by the family as a scan, September 2026, and now in this project's library. Its own first citation is Camillo De Franceschi, «I castelli della Val…» — Carlo's son, cited by the engineers as the authority on the castles of his own valley.

orbanic2024.heading: The Gologorica parish archive exists, and a 2024 paper has been reading it
orbanic2024.lead: Elvis Orbanić's study of the weeping Madonna of Sveti Petar u Šumi, in «Acta Histriae» 32 (2024), works from the Paulines' chronicle of the miracles. Two of its pilgrims come from this county, and one of them is the parish priest of Gologorica. But the thing that matters most for this archive is buried in the source list at the back.

rows.lab: The source list
rows.text: «**ŽAG, MKK – Župni arhiv Gologorice, Matična knjiga krštenih (1691–1763)**» and «**ŽAG, MKU – Župni arhiv Gologorice, Matična knjiga umrlih (1646–1777)**». The **parish archive at Gologorica** — baptisms from 1691, deaths from **1646** — cited as a working source by a historian publishing in 2024. This site's Parish Books page says flatly that Gologorica has no film at all and that its registers are the great absence in every collection searched. **They are not lost. They are in the parish, they are being used, and their dates are now known.** Deaths from 1646 would reach a generation earlier than anything this archive holds for the village.

rows.lab: Petar Kruzila, priest of Gologorica
rows.text: On **2 October 1722** the archpriest **Petar Kruzila (Petrus Cruzilla)**, parish priest of Gologorica, walked the twenty-one kilometres to Sveti Petar u Šumi to discharge a vow. He had refused to believe the image wept. Then, riding, he came off his horse and **was struck deaf where he fell**, and kept his bed forty days; having made his vow to the Virgin he felt better at once, and «wished to tell everyone of his case and of his doubt». He stayed in the parish until he died there on **25 September 1731**, entered in the Gologorica death register as «Reverendissimus dominus Petrus Cruzilla, protonotarius apostolicus, archipresbyter et parochus Gologoriziae».

rows.lab: Which puts a face in the register
rows.text: He is the priest who was baptising at Gologorica in 1722 — the man whose hand wrote the entries for the household that had cut ANNO · DOMNI · 1711 over its door eleven years before. The paper cites him as the regular administrator of baptisms there in that year. Whoever of this family was born, married or buried at Gologorica between about 1720 and 1731 was written down by a deaf apostolic protonotary who had fallen off a horse for doubting a miracle.

rows.lab: And a footnote for the Fiume question
rows.text: The same paper, citing Camillo De Franceschi's «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino», notes that **Antonio Bartolomeo Bono, vice-captain and administrator of the County of Pazin in 1723–24, «porijeklom je bio iz riječke patricijske obitelji»** — was of a **Rijeka patrician family**, and had read law at Padua in 1705–6. The traffic between Fiume's patriciate and the County of Pazin's administration ran both ways, and that is the same channel Kobler's «venuto da Pisino» household went along in 1740.

rows.lab: How old the parish is
rows.text: «Župa Gologorica spominje se 1324., a vjerojatno je postojala i ranije» — the parish is mentioned in **1324** and probably existed earlier, within the diocese of Pedena. Which is a year before Mikula Gologorički, priest of this same parish, wrote the Croatian Glagolitic version of the Istrian Boundary Settlement of 1325.

orbanic2024.source_orb: Elvis Orbanić, in «Acta Histriae» 32 (2024) 1, on the votive record of the lacrimating image at Sveti Petar u Šumi — read in full, 8 September 2026, from a scan supplied by the family. Its Gologorica citations are to the parish archive there (ŽAG), baptisms 1691–1763 and deaths 1646–1777.

krizman1979.heading: Carlo, cited eleven times in 1979 — and a Roman road under the village
krizman1979.lead: Mate Križman's «Antička svjedočanstva o Istri» (1979), the first volume of the «Istra kroz stoljeća» series, is an anthology of every Greek and Latin writer who mentions Istria, with philological commentary. It is a classicist's book and it has nothing to do with genealogy. It cites **Carlo De Franceschi eleven times**, and it puts Gologorica in the Roman period.

rows.lab: Where Carlo stands in it
rows.text: In the index: «**FRANCESCHI C. de — 170, 189, 192, 193, 211, 263**», with «L'Istria, note storiche, Poreč 1879» cited at pages 10–11, 38ff, 45 and 67. Križman uses him for the topography of the Istrian war of 177 BC, for the siege engines at Nesactium, for the identification of Livy's lost towns, and for the question of whether the Pontic Histri and the Adriatic Histri are one people. He sits in the text beside **Kandler, Gnirs, Benussi, Zippel and Müller** — which is the canon. **Ninety-nine years after he published it, a professional classicist was still arguing with his book rather than around it.**

rows.lab: And where he was right
rows.text: «Najmanja je vjerojatnost da ćemo pogriješiti ako glede Mutile prihvatimo **Kandlerovo, De Franceschijevo i Gnirsovo mišljenje** koje na temelju sličnosti imena poistovjećuje **Mutilu s Medulinom**» — we are least likely to be wrong if, for Mutila, we accept Kandler's, De Franceschi's and Gnirs's view identifying it with **Medulin**; and for Faveria they propose **Mutvoran**. Two lost towns of Livy, placed by a man from Gologorica, still the best answer in 1979. **And Medulin is one of the towns in the southern-Istrian cluster this archive has just opened.**

rows.lab: The village in the Roman period
rows.text: Gnirs proposed that the ancient **Alùon** was a settlement of the Istrian interior, on the Veli potok **between Pićan and Gologorica**, at the place where the Roman inscriptions **CIL V 322, 323, 424 and 425** were found. Križman indexes Gologorica at page 98 for it. This archive's story starts in 1644 with a baptism register. There were people writing on stone in that valley sixteen centuries earlier, and the stones have numbers.

rows.lab: Where to read it
rows.text: The book is out of print and second-hand copies are scarce, but **the full text is online**, uploaded to both Scribd and idoc.pub. It was read there in September 2026. A proper library copy is still worth having, because the apparatus is the point of the book.

krizman1979.source_kriz: Mate Križman, «Antička svjedočanstva o Istri», Istra kroz stoljeća I/1, Pula–Rijeka 1979 — read in full text from the copy at idoc.pub, September 2026. Križman (1937–2015) taught classical philology at Zagreb.

cadastre1820.heading: Six households in 1820 — and one of them is «di Gallignana»
cadastre1820.lead: This archive has said, on this page and on three others, that **nothing yet joins the Gologorica house to the Gallignana line of farmers and stonecutters two villages away**. Both families believe the join exists; neither has the page. Dean Brhan, working the **Catasto franceschino of 1820** in the state archive at Trieste, prints a list that puts a name in the gap.

rows.lab: What the cadastre says
rows.text:
«**A Moncalvo di Pisino nel 1820 erano presenti 6 fuochi dei possidenti De Franceschi; Maria, Giuseppe, Giobatta (di Gallignana), Leonardo e Antonio. Erano la famiglia più influente dell'area in questione che comprendeva una decina di villaggi abitati compattamente da contadini croati.**»

At Moncalvo di Pisino in 1820 there were **six hearths of De Franceschi proprietors** — Maria, Giuseppe, **Giobatta (of Gallignana)**, Leonardo and Antonio. They were the most influential family in a district of some ten villages inhabited solidly by Croatian peasants.

rows.lab: Why that parenthesis matters
rows.text: Every other proprietor in the list is given by first name alone, because they are of the place. **One of them is qualified — «di Gallignana».** The cadastral clerk needed to say which Giobatta he meant, and the way he distinguished him was by the village he came from. So in 1820 there is a **Giovanni Battista De Franceschi, identified as a man of Gallignana, holding property at Moncalvo** — the two villages this archive has never been able to join, in one line of one document.

rows.lab: What this is not
rows.text: It is not proof. **It does not say he is our Joannes Baptista**, the farmer of house 5 at Gračišće whom the register catches in 1787 and who would have been in his sixties in 1820; Giovanni Battista is the commonest name in both villages, and a De Franceschi of Gallignana holding land at Moncalvo could be a cousin, a purchaser or a son-in-law as easily as an ancestor. **What it is, is the first object of any kind that puts the two names together** — and it tells this archive exactly which sheet to order. The Catasto franceschino for the Comune di Gallignana, Distretto di Pisino, is at the **Archivio di Stato di Trieste**, and its Moncalvo counterpart with it. Brhan read them. So can we.

rows.lab: And the district it makes them
rows.text: «The most influential family in an area of some ten villages inhabited solidly by Croatian peasants» is a much harder statement than «possidenti». Six proprietor households of one surname in one small village, in an Austrian cadastre made for taxation, is a **local gentry** — which is what the arcaded palazzetto with the shield on its façade was already saying, and what «da modesti possidenti» in Carlo's biography was quietly denying. Both can be true across a century: modest when they arrived, dominant by 1820, and the cadastre is the year the balance shows.

cadastre1820.source_cad: Dean Brhan, «“Stare cum loco et foco”. L'emigrazione verso l'Istria dalla Carnia e dal Friuli», published by the Amici dell'Orologeria Pesarina, Prato Carnico — read in full from the association's own open text, September 2026. Brhan's list is drawn from the Archivio di Stato di Trieste, Catasto franceschino, and his note on the family's origin cites Miroslav Bertoša, «Etos i etnos zavičaja» (Pola–Fiume, 1985).

fond254.heading: The 1610 problem, solved — and it was never a problem
fond254.lead: The family's own archive survives, at the **State Archive in Rijeka**, as fond **HR-DARI-254, «Obitelj De Franceschi iz Gologorice»**, and its catalogue dates run **1610–1934**. That start date has sat awkwardly on this site for a year: every account of the family's arrival says the mid-seventeenth century or about 1700, and here was an archive apparently beginning ninety years before the earliest of them. The archive's own finding aid, read properly in September 2026, dissolves it in one sentence.

rows.lab: The oldest book in the fond is not a family document
rows.text:
«**Sadržajno je raznolika i značajna zbirka obitelji (1610-1874), u kojoj se nalazi najstarija knjiga u fondu, knjiga prihoda župne crkve u Humu (1610-1685), pisana glagoljicom, ujedno i jedina u fondu na hrvatskom jeziku.**»

The oldest book in the fond is the **income book of the parish church at Hum — Colmo — for 1610 to 1685, written in Glagolitic**, and it is the only item in the whole fond in Croatian. It sits in series 3, «**Zbirka obitelji**» — the family's *collection*, the things they gathered — not in series 1, the family's own papers.

rows.lab: So the date belongs to a collector, not to an ancestor
rows.text:
A family archive's earliest date is the date of the **earliest object in it**, and this family produced a historian. The finding aid says as much: «**Nema podataka tko je bio sakupljač gradiva, ali najvjerojatnije je to bio Carlo De Franceschi, a moguće je da je to činio ili nastavio sakupljati njegov sin Camillo**» — no record of who assembled the material, but most probably **Carlo De Franceschi**, and possibly continued by his son **Camillo**.

So 1610 is the year of a Glagolitic parish account book from a village eleven kilometres away, picked up by the man who wrote the history of Istria. **It is evidence about Carlo's library, not about his ancestors' whereabouts.** The four dates this archive has been juggling — 1610, the mid-seventeenth century, 1661, about 1700 — are now three, and 1610 was never one of them.

rows.lab: What the family's own papers actually begin with
rows.text:
The arranged series say it plainly. **1.1 Family papers in the strict sense**: probate 1794–1800, lawsuits between family members 1788–1801, papers on individual members 1791–1934. **1.2 Papers on the family's estates: 1703–1783** — contracts of sale and exchange, land let out, share-farming of livestock. **2. Miscellanea 1804–1926. 3.1 Religious bodies 1610–1805. 3.2 Secular bodies, economy and administration 1709–1874.**

The family's own earliest paper is therefore **1703** — three years after the arrival Carlo himself claimed, and eight years before the date cut over the door of the house.

rows.lab: And a portrait of how they got rich
rows.text:
The content note is the best short description of this family's economics anyone has written: «**Kupoprodajni ugovori, ugovori o permutacijama, knjige kreditiranja i potraživanja svjedoče o intenzivnom bogaćenju obitelji tijekom 18. stoljeća, trgovačkom i financijskom aktivnošću, putem posuđivanja novca i otkupa dugova u gologoričkom kraju, ali i sve do Kastva, Mošćenica, Labina, Kranjske i drugih udaljenih mjesta.**»

Contracts of sale and exchange, and **books of lending and of debts owed**, witness the family's intensive enrichment through the eighteenth century by **trade and finance — lending money and buying up debts** — in the Gologorica country and as far as **Kastav, Mošćenice, Labin and Carniola**.

That is not a farming family that prospered. It is a **money-lending and debt-buying business**, run out of a village, reaching a hundred kilometres. It explains the arcaded palazzetto, it explains six proprietor households by 1820, and it is exactly the Carnian merchant profile the migration literature describes.

rows.lab: And the confusion is institutional, not ours
rows.text:
The last sentence of the provenance note is the one this archive will be quoting for years: «**Zbog nepoznavanja povijesti obitelji do sređivanja 1990. godine gradivo ovog fonda je bilo spojeno u jedan fond s gradivom jedne druge obitelji De Franceshi, onoj iz Šegeta kod Buja.**»

**Through ignorance of the family's history, until the arrangement of 1990, this fond's material was joined into a single fond with that of another De Franceschi family — the one from Šeget near Buje.** Before that there was only a temporary list, «superficial and inaccurate». The fond was separated and arranged by the archivist **Ines Krota**.

So for forty-odd years the Carnian family and the Cretan family were **one archival fond in one building**, because nobody knew they were two families. This site has spent a year arguing that they are separate, against a monograph that calls them two branches of one house. **The archive that holds both of them reached the same conclusion in 1990, and had to physically pull them apart to act on it.**

rows.lab: Where the papers came from, and one that got away
rows.text: The material was taken in in **1948**, out of Pula or Poreč, with the rest of the Istrian holdings that had been prepared for evacuation, and entered in the general inventory at **no. 92, page 142** — never entered in the accessions book at all. In **1950** one bundle was returned to the **Naučna biblioteka in Pula** along with three miscellanea fascicles, said to have come from the Financial Department of the Regional People's Committee for Istria. **That bundle is somewhere in Pula, and this archive does not know what is in it.** The whole fond is 0.70 metres, seven boxes, in Italian, Croatian and Latin — and open to the public.

rows.lab: For comparison, the other family's archive
rows.text: **HR-DARI-382, «Obitelj de Franceschi iz Šegeta»**, runs **1412–1943**: 2.60 metres, **twenty-six boxes and four folders**, archivally arranged. Nearly four times the Gologorica fond and starting two centuries earlier — which is what an estate-owning house with a private library leaves behind, and a reminder that the two families are not comparable in anything but a surname. The 1412 start deserves the same scepticism as 1610 until somebody says what the document is.

rows.lab: And the Glagolitic book may already be in print
rows.text:
One more thing about that Hum income book. In **1999 the State Archive in Pazin published «Glagoljski rukopis iz Huma (1608.–1639.): iz Registro della chiesa parrocchiale di Colmo»**, edited by Dražen Vlahov — a Glagolitic register of the parish church of **Colmo, which is Hum**, covering 1608 to 1639. The family's book runs 1610 to 1685.

Same parish, same script, same kind of book, overlapping decades. **They may be one manuscript**, or two halves of one register that were separated when the family's papers went to Rijeka and the parish's stayed in Istria — or they may be two different books. **The fond description and the printed edition do not cite each other**, so nobody has said. The edition costs thirteen euro and is on the acquisitions list. Until then this is a question, not a claim.

hauptmann1945.heading: The house, 12 August 1945 — an eyewitness, in full
hauptmann1945.lead: An archivist walked into this house three months after the war ended and wrote down what he found. His report has been quoted at second hand on this site for a year. It is printed in full as an appendix to the 2022 Zagreb paper, and it is the last description of the De Franceschi library and archive standing in the building they were made in. **It begins with a rumour about sabres.**

rows.lab: Why he went
rows.text:
«In the village of **Gola Gorica** (12 km from Pazin) the people's militia had, according to one report, **armed itself with historic sabres**. Inspection established, though too late, that the militia had been quartered **in the country house of the De Franceschi family.**»

He adds why the name meant something to him: the family «gave good Istrian historians through two generations. **Carlo (d.) and his son Camillo (aged 70), together with Benussi, have deserved most of the history of Istria.**»

rows.lab: What had happened to the house
rows.text:
**Camillo, the present owner, «was director of the library in Pula, and is now somewhere in Italy».** The house had therefore been sequestered and put under the Administration of National Property for Istria.

In **1943** the partisan hospital from Pazin was moved into it because of the bombing. After the German advance it was no longer kept up — the owners had stopped coming for the summer. After the German capitulation it served as a **guardhouse for the people's militia**, and the former District Committee of Čepić «**carried off four cartloads of various things**».

Hauptmann compares it to the emptied castle of Baroness Hütterot on Sv. Andrija by Rovinj — except that here **not even the thin list of removed items** that Rovinj had was left behind. The Čepić committee listed only what remained, and did that *post festum*.

rows.lab: The library, in his words
rows.text:
«Sorting the chaos in the house, **I reassembled the library**, in which all the scholarly works of the two men are now brought together.»

«The library itself is, for Istrian questions, **exemplary**. I gave up any listing of the books, because one may safely assert that **the library, as regards the historiographical questions of Istria, is complete.**»

He names the runs: *Atti e memorie della Società Istriana di archeologia e storia patria*, the *Archeografo Triestino*, *Memorie storiche Forogiuliesi*, the *Archivio Veneto*. Then great numbers of single issues of the most varied journals, kept for their Istrian content, and newspaper cuttings — their own and other people's. And **an offprint collection sorted by subject into boxes on a register system**, so that specialised literature on archaeology, or on the biographies of Istrians, or on folklore, could be found at once.

The non-scholarly part: «old and new editions of **Petrarch, Dante, Tasso**, in general a great number of books of the most varied content — old editions of **Machiavelli, bibles, the Venetian statutes**.»

rows.lab: The manuscripts, and why he insisted on keeping them
rows.text:
«The manuscripts of Carlo and Camillo are **saved in fair number, though they were scattered everywhere.**» He had too little time to separate published from unpublished — but a glance convinced him they all had to be kept, and his reason is a working historian's:

«It happens, for instance, that in composing a work the writer used **his own notes and those of his forebears**, and of course did not carry the whole of that into the printed work.»

He names Carlo's *Gita a Cosgliaco* and **«a collection of biographies of famous Istrians which Pietro De Franceschi gathered fifty to a hundred years earlier»** — an ancestor-collector this archive has never had a word about. And the Istrian travel accounts: *Gita a Colmo*, *Bogliuno*, *Rovigno*.

rows.lab: «At least from the beginning of the seventeenth century»
rows.text:
«**The noble family De Franceschi has lived, according to the material found, at least from the beginning of the XVII century at Gola Gorica.** Beside the modest manor — if the house may be called that — it possessed some land in the neighbourhood. **An inventory from the beginning of the XVII century is preserved**, which gives a fine insight into those circumstances.»

This archive has cited that sentence at second hand for a year and treated it as a rival date to 1650 and 1700. Read whole, it is **an archivist's inference from a box of papers in a house**, in one afternoon, with a militia billeted in it — not a documented arrival. He is describing the same thing the Rijeka fond describes: **a collecting family whose oldest paper is older than the family's presence.**

rows.lab: What else was in the house — and it is not all theirs
rows.text:
Account books old and new; **lists of dues from the Gola Gorica district, paid to the church or directly to the lordship**, running down into Carlo's and Camillo's own correspondence. That correspondence had once been well ordered; he found it «**all scattered**» and could only roughly put it back.

And then material from around Pazin that had **strayed into the family's ownership through the historiographical enthusiasm of its two representatives**:

· **Protocols of the circulars of the Pićan bishop Aldrago Antonio de Piccardi**, about 1780
· **«Atti di nomine e investiture dai parochi della Contea di Pisino», 1728–1776**
· a copy of the Venetian–Istrian chronicle called **the Barbara**
· a **chronicle of Pula and its district written in 1726 by a Pula archdeacon**
· and «especially **a complete population census of the town of Rovinj, 1650–1736**» — which he calls a rich find
· **the urbarium of the castle of Momiano, 1584/5, in two volumes** — «a small consolation for the destroyed urbarium in Pazin castle»

rows.lab: And the Glagolitic
rows.text:
«The search for treasure written in **Glagolitic** was for the first time crowned with success. It is known that the Italians rooted out Glagolitic in stone and on paper. While some stone inscriptions are still found, **on paper Glagolitic is very rare.**»

«For the church at **Hum (Colmo)** a **parish register from the middle of the XVII century** has now been found, written largely in Glagolitic — and likewise one for the **confraternity of the church of St Roch near Hum**.»

So there was not one Glagolitic Hum book in this house but **at least two**, and the Rijeka fond's «income book of the parish church at Hum, 1610–1685» is a third description of the same small hoard. This is the answer to the question this archive asked yesterday about Vlahov's published *Registro della chiesa parrocchiale di Colmo*: **the family had the Glagolitic books of Hum, more than one of them, and an archivist carried them out of the house in August 1945.**

rows.lab: And a collection of charters from 1201
rows.text:
The last line of the inventory, and the largest claim in it: «**A collection of charters — mostly parchment — rotuli, papal bulls… from the year 1201 onward, for various Istrian towns**, completes the find at Gola Gorica.»

Signed: **Zagreb, 12. VIII. 1945. F. Hauptmann.**

rows.lab: What this changes
rows.text: Three things. **The house was emptied twice** — by four cartloads to Čepić and then by the archivist, and only the second man wrote anything down. **The «seventeenth century» date for the family at Gologorica is Hauptmann's reading of a collection**, not a document, and it should never again be set against 1661 as though the two were rival records. And **the family's own papers are the smaller half of what was in that house**: the bishop's protocols, the Rovinj census, the Momiano urbarium and the Glagolitic books of Hum were other people's records, gathered by two historians, and they are the reason this family's archive begins two centuries before this family does.

hauptmann1945.source_haupt: Ferdinand Hauptmann, «Izvještaj o arhivima. Gola Gorica kod Pazina», Zagreb, 12 August 1945 — printed in full as Appendix 1 to Anita Marin, Martina Jurišić and Alena Matijaca, «Zbirka obitelji De Franceschi u Nacionalnoj i sveučilišnoj knjižnici u Zagrebu», «Libellarium» 13, 2 (2022), pp. 19–21, and published by Markus Leideck in «Arhivski vjesnik» 58 (2015). Translations here are this archive's own.

tomb.heading: The tomb in the churchyard, photographed at last
tomb.lead: David walked into the cemetery at Gologorica on 29 September 2026 and photographed the family monument. It is a walled tomb with a cross above, the arms cut into the pediment, and three inscribed tablets — the historian in the centre in pink marble between fluted pilasters, and a family tablet to either side. Everything below is read off those photographs.

rows.lab: The centre tablet: the historian, in Roman numerals and in Italian
rows.text: «CARLO de FRANCESCHI — STORIOGRAFO DELL'ISTRIA — STRENUO ASSERTORE DELL'ITALIANITÀ DELLA SUA TERRA — MDCCCIX – MDCCCXCIII.» Historiographer of Istria, strenuous asserter of the Italian character of his land, 1809–1893. It is one side of the quarrel this page is about, cut in stone in the village the quarrel was over — and it was cut while his Croatian neighbours were making the opposite case in Naša Sloga. (doc.)

rows.lab: The two side tablets: a wife and three children, all dead before him
rows.text: LEFT — «FAMIGLIA de FRANCESCHI: FAUSTINA fu CARLO, Parenzo 1864 – Trieste 1906. SILVIA de FRANCESCHI fu FRANCESCO, moglie di Camillo, Moncalvo 1872 – Pola 1938. GIULIO fu CARLO, pittore accademico, Fiume 1856 – Moncalvo 1942.» RIGHT — «VIRGINIA fu CARLO, Fiume 1858 – Parenzo 1876. MARIA MICHELI, moglie di Carlo, Pisino 1828 – Parenzo 1880. PIETRO fu CARLO, magistrato, Rovigno 1854 – Moncalvo 1884.» Three of these were new to this archive: Carlo's wife MARIA MICHELI, whose maiden name no page here carried; PIETRO, a magistrate dead at thirty; and SILVIA, a de Franceschi who married the de Franceschi Camillo — the surname on both sides of one marriage, recorded without comment. And the birthplaces are a career: Rovigno 1854, Fiume 1856, Fiume 1858, Parenzo 1864. The family moved with Carlo's posts and the tomb records the route. (doc.)

rows.lab: ⚠ And «Moncalvo» on this tomb is this village
rows.text: Silvia is born at «Moncalvo» in 1872; Giulio dies at «Moncalvo» in 1942; Pietro dies at «Moncalvo» in 1884. Moncalvo is the Italian name of Gologorica — the same bare hill, the other language, and on this page the whole argument. They were born and died at home, and an Italian-language monument says so in Italian. ⚠ There is also a real Moncalvo in Piedmont, and on 29 September 2026 this archive confused the two and used the confusion to disprove a true identification. The correction is on /corrections/, and the lesson is short: a place has as many names as it has had masters, and this village has two that are the argument itself.

rows.lab: The arms, and a serpent that eats its own tail
rows.text: The pediment of each side tablet carries the arms in relief, and they are repeated larger over the centre: a shield bearing a LATIN CROSS with a diagonal device behind it — read from the photographs as a bolt or a branch, and not read further — with a rounded object at the base below a horizontal division, beneath a CORONET of five visible pearls on a jewelled band. A second, older and far more worn version is cut on a stone urn in the same plot, oval, with the same cross and the same charge at the foot. ⚠ And above the centre tablet, set into the pediment of the wall itself, is an OUROBOROS — a serpent biting its own tail, carved as a plain ring. None of this is blazoned here. This archive holds no grant of arms and [item 133](/worklist/) is the open errand to get one: the Austrian nobility archive has «Ausfertigung eines Adelszertifikates und einer Wappenkopie, dato 13.05.1825», a copy of the coat of arms made from an 1825 original. The photographs are a description of what is on the tomb. The blazon is what the paper would give.

rows.lab: Armella's cross, and a broken Slovenian slab
rows.text: A little apart from the tomb, against the churchyard wall, stands a granite cross with a marble plaque: «ARMELLA de FRANCESCHI, morta a 48 anni il 6 maggio 1920, ebbe qui lagrimata sepoltura — il marito GIULIO.» So Armella's husband was Giulio the painter, who outlived her by twenty-two years and is on the tablet a few feet away. And propped against the tomb, broken across the top, is a slab for «FLEGAR FRANJO ✱ 2.3.1872 ✝ 19.10.1940» and a MARIJA above him whose death year went with the break — closing «LAHKA IN BILA ZEMLJA», may the earth be light and white. ⚠ That line is SLOVENIAN. In a churchyard where the argument was whether the village was Croatian or Italian, a third language is lying broken against the wall. A Maria Flegar, 1842–1882, already married into this name; whether these are her people is untested.

tomb.source_tomb: David's photographs of the cemetery at Gologorica, 29 September 2026, read at full resolution. The tomb, Armella's cross, the broken Flegar slab, the arms in two states and the ouroboros.

framemap.heading: What is actually on the two reels, frame by frame
framemap.lead: **This page rests entirely on two microfilms, and until 30 September 2026 nobody had established what was on them.** *The archive held 1,463 page images, had cited **twelve** of them, and had one line in its search register for the whole run. The description it carried — «Gologorica, Gračišće and Lindar» — was wrong in both directions: **Lindar is not on these reels at all**, and a parish that is had never been named.*
framemap.method:
**The Pazin paper inventory is not the authority, and it was wrong twice here.** *Its section headings file both Gračišće books under a GOLOGORICA heading, and it stops the Gračišće births at 1780 when the film says 1840.* **The films carry their own printed title cards**, one before each book, naming the župa, the register and the years. Those are the authority, and they are what this table is built from — found by scanning **every one of the 1,463 frames** for the ink signature of a printed card, then reading each one.

---

**⚠⚠ 9 October 2026 — AND THE TITLE CARDS ARE NOT THE AUTHORITY EITHER. ONE OF THEM IS WRONG ABOUT WHAT ITS BOOK IS.**

*The card at* **M01069199** *reads* «ŽUPA: GOLOGORICA · **MATIČNA KNJIGA UMRLIH 1646-1806** · SIGNATURA: 5.1» — *a death register.* ***[The book it introduces is not a death register](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex).*** *Its own title page, at* **M01069202**, *says:* «Catalogus mortuorum … **ADULTORUM** … ex antiquis et recentioribus paginis **COACTUS A ME** Antonio Ferdinando M[?]ocovrich, Parocho Loci, **Anno Domini 1800**» — **a perpetual obit calendar, compiled in 1800 out of the registers.**

**The whole item is now inventoried frame by frame and every one of the twenty-five is accounted for:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **M01069199** | *the printed title card* |
| **M01069200** | *a resolution test target* |
| **M01069201** | *the volume's own cover —* «**Liber Mortuorum Primus**» |
| **M01069202** | *the title page, and January begins* |
| **M01069202–221** | ***the calendar, twelve months*** |
| **M01069222** | *endpapers, with a list of priests* |
| **M01069223** | *KRAJ / END OF ITEM* |

> ***There is no narrative death register anywhere in this item.***

**Two things follow, and the second is the one that matters.**

**1.** *This table's own rule —* «the films carry their own printed title cards … **those are the authority**» — *is [corrected](/corrections/).* ***A printed card made by a filming project in 1997 is a third-hand description, and here it is wrong in the same way the paper inventory was.*** **The book's own title page is the authority. Read it.**

**2. ⚠ GOLOGORICA'S PRE-1784 DEATH REGISTERS ARE NOT ON THESE REELS.** *This archive has believed since 30 September that it holds* «Umrli 1646–1806». ***It holds a digest of them, made in 1800.*** **[The eleven Defranceschi entries the calendar gave up](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex) cannot be expanded into fuller entries, because there is no fuller entry here to go to** — *which both raises what the calendar is worth and closes [the work-list item that asked where the register sits](/worklist/).*

**⚠ And a second item in this table is mis-described, though more mildly.** *The composite* **M01068953–M01069007** *is filed as* «Rođeni 1770–1781 · Umrli 1770–1789 · Vjenčani 1770–1789». *[Reading it out](/searched/):* **M01068996 is the END of the DEATHS and its last entries are 1768**, *not 1770; the marriages begin at* **M01068997** *under* «Notatio Personarum Matrimonio junctarum a 1ᵐᵃ Julij 1770» *and run forward to Feb 1788; and* **M01069006, the final frame, is OUT OF SEQUENCE and carries 1768–1769 marriages** *in the older full narrative formula.* ***So this item's contents start before 1770 at both ends, and its last frame is not its last date.***

**⭐⭐ And the same item contains a document the table does not mention at all.** *[Its first openings, M01068956–958, are a* **numbered list of every house in Gologorica**](/gologorica-line/#houselist1770) — «Nota delle Case abitate, e disabitate», *1 to about 130, with the head of each household named and the Defranceschi at* **45** *and* **46**. ***Three audits of this table in one day have found two books mis-described and one document missing from it.*** ⚠ *The frame* **ranges** *have been right every time; it is the descriptions that fail.*

**⭐ And the books number themselves.** *[Five covers read](/gologorica-line/#bookseries):* **Bapt. II** *(1764),* **Bapt. III et Mort. II** *(1770),* **Bapt. IV** *(1784),* **Mort. I** *(the 1800 calendar),* **Mort. III** *(1784).* ***The death series is complete; the baptism series runs II, III, IV, so* LIBER BAPTIZATORUM I *is not on these reels*** — *the pre-1764 book, and [the 1679 window the Carnian argument turns on](/carnia/) is inside it.*

**✔ And that item is now swept end to end.** *[Its real structure is* **six** *sections, not three](/gologorica-line/#itemswept): a house list, three blank return-forms, and then baptisms, deaths and marriages — with ***the baptisms and the deaths each split into* MASCULORUM *and* FŒMINARUM** *sequences, announced in their own headings.* ***A year counted out of one of those halves is half a year's count***, *and [this archive published such a count and had to withdraw it](/corrections/).*
rows: **⭐ HOUSE LIST** · Bapt. **M**/**F** · Def. **M**/**F** · Vjenčani — **⚠ see note**
framemap.whatitmeans:
**Three things follow, and none of them was visible before.**

**The household censuses are the bulk of what is here and almost none of it has been read.** *The four Gologorica* status animarum *— **1826, 1862, 1894 and 1921** — are **628 frames, 43% of both reels together**. A* status animarum *lists every soul in every house: the head, his wife, her maiden name, the children, the servants, the ages. **Only 1894 has ever been opened**, and only for [the eleven](/the-eleven/). The other three have never been touched.*

**The Gračišće baptisms run unbroken from 1667 to 1840.** *Two books, 294 frames, joining at 1745/1746 — and the second of them is titled 1746–1840 but **runs off the end of the reel at 1807**, behind a printed card reading «NASTAVLJA SE». **The rest is ZM34K-216, which this family does not hold** — [and it is now the archive's first errand](/errands/). **This is the origin parish of the direct line**, and it covers the 1679 arrival window the [Carnia](/carnia/) argument turns on.*

**And there is a parish here nobody asked for.** *[Cerovlje](/places/cerovlje/) is the next place north on the Pazin–Rijeka road. Its* status animarum *sits in the first 139 frames of reel 214, under an unlabelled row on the paper inventory. **Nothing is claimed from it** — it has not been read — but the archive holds it.*
framemap.honest: **Every frame here has been LOCATED. Almost none has been READ.** *That distinction is the whole point of publishing the table: it turns «1,465 images of something» into a list of books with names, years and sizes, which is what makes the reading plannable. It is not a claim that the reading is done.*

priests.heading: House 1 is the parish house, and it names every hand that wrote these books
priests.lead: **The first household of the 1826 *status animarum* is the plebania, and it was kept up for sixty years.** *Eight priests, each with his birth date and the place he came from, and for two of them the date they died and were buried at Gologorica.* **This archive has been reading these registers without knowing whose handwriting it was looking at.** *It matters: the working rule here is that a hand is only legible against itself, and that rule cannot be applied until the hands have names and dates.* (doc — ZM34K-214, M01069319.) **⚠ 7 October: the third priest's origin, first read here as** «e *Zuckfeld*», *is* «e **Gurkfeld**» — **Krško**. *[Corrected.](/corrections/)*
rows: d. 22 March 1862, aged 58y 2m 15d — *«mortuus et sepultus Gollogoricæ»*
**Gurkfeld** — **Krško**, in Lower Carniola, on the river Krka (*Gurk*)
d. 10 Nov 1885, aged 34y 2m — *«mortuus et sepultus Gollogoricæ»*
priests.note: **Two of the eight came from Vrbnik on Krk and a third from Omišalj** — *so the priests of this inland Istrian village were being supplied from the Kvarner islands, which is a current running the opposite way to the family this archive follows.* **And the book itself was printed at Fiume**, *«presso Antonio Karletzky, Stampatore e Libraio»*, on its cover. *(doc — M01069317.)*

maria1789.heading: A death in 1826 and a baptism in 1789 turn out to be the same woman
maria1789.lead: **This archive held four separate roster rows for her.** *One from David's tree with the birth three years out; one from this pedigree with no dates at all and the wrong mother; one raised at breakfast on 30 September from a death entry, explicitly refusing to identify her; and, three hours later, the baptism that identifies her.*
paras: **The death came first.** *Page 3 of the 1826* status animarum *enters a* **Maria Defranceschi, *civilitas*, died 30 September 1826, aged 37 years 2 months 10 days** — *no parents, no house that survives, the household struck through.* **That was published the same morning with a warning attached**: *«not identified with any Maria already on this roster — this estate holds some thirty Maria Defranceschis and a death date alone will not pick one out».*

**Then a second Maria turned up eight pages later**, *born* **20 July 1780**, *and the two nearly collided: same day, same month, nine years apart.* **They were kept separate**, *and [a work-list item](/worklist/) named the test — walk July 1780 and July 1789 in the baptism books, both of which are on the same reel.*
**The test found her.** *The opening for the summer of 1789 gives, in the parish priest's ruled columns:*

> **«Maria Rosa=/lia Defrances=/chi ex Loco»**, *house* **36**, *baptised by* **a.R.D. Antonius Giacich ex abatia**; *father* **«Joh: Baptis[ta]»**; *mother* **«Catharina JOBLICH»**; *godmother* **«Rosalia Baxa uxor Petri, ex Lindar»**.

**Thirty September 1826 minus thirty-seven years, two months and ten days is the twentieth of July, 1789.** *To the day.* **So the baptism and the death are one woman, and she was thirty-seven.** *The Maria born in 1780 is somebody else and stays unidentified.*

**And the entry corrects her mother.** *This pedigree had her as a daughter of Joannes Baptista and* **Mariana**. *The register says* **Catharina Joblich** — *the same wife who appears three years earlier standing godmother beside him as* «**Cath. ejus uxor nata Jablich ex Buccari**», **born a Jablich of Bakar**. *[Her family now has a page](/married-in/), and [Bakar is on the work list](/worklist/).*

**⚠ Only this child is moved.** *The other five of casa 36 keep Mariana, because no register has been read for them and a man may have two wives. **Reassigning five children on the strength of one sibling would be the same error in the opposite direction**, and this archive has made that error before.*

adoption.heading: Antonius of house 6 was not Leonardus's son — the page says so three times
adoption.lead: **The pedigree on this page was drawn with Antonius (b. 14 April 1814) as the only child of Leonardus and Matthea.** *One opening of the 1826* status animarum *takes him out of that household and puts him in another, and it does so three separate times in the same hand.*
paras: **In the name column** — *«**Antonius Defranceschi filius Usualdi et Apoloniæ**»*.

**In the annotation on the far right** — *«**hunc in filium adoptivum accepit patruus Leonardus, et locatus hic sub N.º 6**»*: **his father's brother Leonardus took him as an adopted son** and settled him here under number six.
**And at the foot of the page**, under a house marked *«non habitata»* — *«**Usualdus … pater Antonii**»*. **His own house at Gologorica stood empty when the census was drawn.**

***Patruus* is specifically the father's brother**, *which is the word that makes Usualdus a brother of Leonardus rather than an unrelated man.* **So the line runs sideways where this archive drew it straight.** *Leonardus and Matthea are now recorded with no children; Antonius sits under a new household, **Usualdus Defranceschi and Apollonia**, both of whom were new here. Every descendant already published under Antonius keeps its place — he did head house 6 — but his ancestry above that point changes.*
**That Leonardus and Matthea were childless is the obvious reason for the adoption, and the register does not say it.** *It is recorded as inference and marked as such.*

**The same opening answers a question about the wives.** *The provenance column —* «Locus ex quo vel ad quem» — *gives, against the marriage of 29 January 1840:* **Antonius «Ex Parochia Lindaris»** *and* **Francisca «Ex Parochia Gallignanæ sub N.º 5»**. **Gračišće house 5 is the direct line's own second generation**, *the farmer Giovanni Battista — so this marriage may join the two lines. **It is not claimed**: the baptism that would prove it is on ZM34K-216, the one reel of this set the family does not hold, and [it is the archive's first errand](/errands/).*

carlohouse.heading: Carlo in the household book, with his mother's birthday
carlohouse.lead: **The archive's [Carlo section](/gologorica-line/) was built from his baptism and from printed biographies.** *House 7 of the 1826* status animarum *has the whole household on one opening, kept up for sixty years — and it confirms what was held, to the day, while adding two dates nobody had.*
paras: **Confirmed exactly:** *«Carolus», born* **17 October 1809**, *dead* **8 January 1893**; *and, in the struck household above him,* **Jacobus Defranceschi**, *civis*, born **21 July 1761**, dead **3 December 1850 aged 88**. **This is verification, not discovery**, *and the archive says so.*

**New: his mother's birthday.** *This archive had Lambertina Peschle as* «about 1786». *The book writes her* **«Lambertina uxor nata Peschle»**, ***born 17 September 1786***, *with* **«Ex Volosca»** *in the provenance column — the town near Opatija that every printed life of Carlo names as his mother's — and her death on* **16 July 1863, aged 76 years 10 months**.
**New: his father's.** *Josephus Defranceschi,* **born 4 March 1765** *where the archive had* «about 1763», *married* **3 February 1807**, *dead* **12 December 1838**.

**⚠ And one thing the page cannot settle about itself.** *It gives Josephus's age at death as* **74 years 9 months**, *which would put his birth in* **March 1764** — *a year before its own birth column.* **The written date is taken and the discrepancy is left visible**, *because a register that disagrees with itself is telling you something about how it was kept.*

**⭐ And the book gives the whole household on one opening, eighty pages later.** *Page 89 of the same census repeats house 7 in full —* **«Dnus Josephus Defranceschi»**, *Civilitas*, *with* **«Lambertina uxor nata Peschle»** *and* **ten children**: Josephus, **Charolus**, Maria Aloisia, Franciscus Xaverius, Clementina, Maria Adelgidis, Maximilianus Antonius, Enrichus Jacobus and **Aloysius**. *The last line is the one that mattered.*

> **«Aloysius … filius natus VOLOSCA»**

**This archive had recorded him as «natus Polonia» — born in Poland — in three files.** *At five times magnification the word is not ambiguous: it is* **Volosca**. *And it is the obvious answer once seen, because his mother is entered* **«Ex Volosca»** *two lines above him.* **She went home to her own town to be delivered.** *«Polonia» and «Volosca» are not similar words; the error was a reading of the initial* **V** *as a* **P**, *made once and repeated without anyone going back to the page.* *[The correction is here](/corrections/); [the Volosca registers have still never been opened](/worklist/).*

**⭐ And on 1 October the baptisms themselves were found.** *Folio 51:* **«Die 19na 8bris 1809 · Carolus Josephus Defranceschi *natus die 17ma hujus, vespere*»** — *born on the 17th in the evening, baptised on the 19th, at house 17, with* **«Dnus Gioanni Curelich, Petinensis»** *of Pićan standing godfather.* *Folio 65:* **«Die 25ta Februarii 1816 · Franciscus Xaverius Joseph Defranceschi *natus die 19na hujus mensis*».* **Both carry the day of death written into the margin by a later hand** — *«† 8/I 1893» and «† 4 Januarii 1893».*

**And between them they explain why this archive's dates kept disagreeing with the census.** *The archive held the* **births**; *the 1826 census in places recorded the* **baptisms**. **Nobody was wrong, and the gap is simply the interval between the two events** — *two days for Carlo, six for his brother.* **⚠ So no date taken from that census can be assumed to be a birth**: *it gave Carlo's birth on one page and his baptism on another. [The correction is here](/corrections/).*

book1826.heading: The 1826 household census, read end to end
book1826.lead: **The first of the thirteen books on these two reels is finished.** *One hundred and nineteen written pages, from the title card at M01069315 to a printed* **«KRAJ — END OF…»** *at M01069435. Before this week the archive had cited thirteen of its frames and read none of it in order.*
paras: **What the book is.** *A* status animarum *is a household census: every soul in every house, with birth, confirmation, marriage, death, the age at death, where a person came from and where they went. This one was* **opened in 1826 and kept up for sixty years**, *so it carries deaths into the 1880s —* **which makes it a far better source than its title year suggests**. *It was printed at* **Fiume, presso Antonio Karletzky**.

**It is arranged by hamlet, not straight through.** *A* **«Pagus»** *heading at the top left of every page names the settlement —* «Gollogoritia» *for most of it, and* **«Gollogorizia Jacotichi»** *for pages 57–60 before it returns.* **That is what explains the «Flegar alias Jacotich»** *this archive corrected a priest's name against: **Jacotichi is a place**, and the families in it are called after it.*

**What it gave this family.** *House 1 is the parish house and names* [**eight priests with their birthplaces**](#) — *the hands that wrote these books. House 6 showed that* **Antonius was Leonardus's adopted nephew, not his son**. *House 7 gave* **Carlo De Franceschi's whole household**, *his mother's birthday, and the line that says* **Aloysius was born at Volosca, not in Poland**. *Elsewhere the book identified* **Maria Rosalia**, *born 20 July 1789 and dead at thirty-seven*, *out of four roster rows that had grown around one woman.*

**And what it gave the wives**, *which is what it was read for:* **Francisca** *out of Gračišće house 5,* **Joanna** *out of Gračišće house 4,* **Clotilda Ortis** *out of Novaki house 2 with her parents named,* **Catharina Joblich** *of Bakar,* **Victoria Calligarich** *in the Peschle household, and about sixty other maiden surnames of the village recorded as they were read.*

**⚠ And one page that belongs to nobody's family.** *Page 114 enters three children* **«ex expositis Tergesti»** — *from the **Trieste foundling hospital*** — *put out to nurse with Gologorica women in 1844 and 1846:* **Angelus Maria Angiussi**, **Adalbertus Almann** *and* **Emilia Olmerling**. *Their surnames belong to the hospital, not to Istria.* **That is how a foreign name arrives in a village without anybody migrating**, *and it is worth knowing before a family is built on one.*

**The honest close.** *Two Defranceschi households sit in this book with dates on them, and perhaps six more entries are bare names struck through as houses changed hands. **The rest of the hundred and nineteen pages are the village** — Udovicich, Rabar, Gasparich, Crismanich, Flegar, Zabran, Runco, Ancich, Selesco. They are recorded as walked, with their surnames, so that nobody reads them again to find out they hold nothing for us.*

enrichus.heading: Enrichus Jacobus, 1830 — and the second set of house numbers
enrichus.lead: **The eighth of Josephus and Lambertina's children had a birth date in this archive and no document behind it.** *It came off the family tree:* **11 March 1830**. *Folio 89 of the Gologorica baptism book now carries the entry that date was taken from, and the register agrees with it to the hour — while correcting the archive on his name, and opening a question about this book that reaches far past one family.*
paras:
> **«Die 28va Martii · ENRICHUS JACOBUS DEFRANCESCHI natus 11ma Martii hora 5ta Mane»**

*Born* **11 March 1830 at five in the morning**, *baptised on the* **28th**, *by* **Franciscus Brussich, parochus**. *Parents:* **«Dnus Josephus Defranceschi, Civilis»** *and* **«Domina Lambertina ejusdem uxor nata Pesle»**. *Godparents* **«Giacomo Giacich»** *and* **«Jos.a Teresa Giacich»**; *midwife* **«Marianna uxor Stanislai Rabar»**. *(doc — Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 — DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-214**, M01069102, folio 89.)*

**This is verification, not discovery, and the archive says so.** *The date was already held. What it did not have was the page, the hour, the priest, the godparents or the midwife — and a date with no document behind it is a date on loan.*

**He is ENRICHUS, not Henricus.** *The register writes him without the H, and so does the* 1826 status animarum *of house 7, which lists him among the ten children as* **«Enrichus Jacobus»**. *Two independent hands, the same form; ours came in off the family tree.* **The id is minted and frozen and is not moved for a spelling** — *a moved id is a dead URL* — *but [his page](/who/henricus-jacobus-defranceschi/) now says which form is the family's and which is ours.*
