**HOW IT WAS READ, SO THE NUMBERS CAN BE CHECKED.** *The column was taken off every frame at moderate magnification in contact sheets, and read where the hand is plain.* **Counts are given as «at least»** *because faint and part-legible cells were* **excluded rather than guessed** — *several read only* «ex Parochia sub N.ᵒ …» *with no parish, and those are not in the table at all.* ***The ranking is robust to that; the exact figures are not.***

**⭐ AND THE COLUMN RECORDS MOVES INSIDE THE VILLAGE — NINE OF THEM.** «**Gollogorizza sub N.ᵒ 2 · 21 · 24 · 32 · 40 · 42 · 49 · 55**». *Each is a household changing house within the parish,* ***with a year***. *That is a dated link between two Gologorica house numbers in one numbering — [exactly what the renumbering work has been short of](/worklist/) — and it came free with the rest of the column.*

house5.heading: ⚠ Reading the Gračišće house 5 page — which this archive had already read, and what checking it turned up
house5.lead: **The page was opened to find Francisca, born 3 February 1819, who came to Gologorica «Ex Parochia Gallignana sub N.ᵒ 5».** ***It had already been transcribed in full on [the direct-line page](/direct-line/), all seven names, a fortnight ago.*** *That is said first because it is the most important thing here.*
paras:
**WHAT THE PAGE SAYS** *(DAPA ZM34K-217, M01072071 —* «Status Animarum, Parochiæ Gallignanæ, Pagus Gallignana»*, house* **5***):*

| | born | |
|---|---|---|
| «**Joan. Bapt. Defranceschi**», *agricola* | **13 Augusti 1787** | *married* **1819**, *died Sept.* **1846** |
| «**Francisca Salomon** uxor» | **17 Martii 1797** | |
| «**Raymundus** eorum filius» | 9 8bris **1823** | |
| «**Antonius** eorum filius» | 20 7bris **1825** | |
| «**Joannes** eorum filius» | 30 Junii **1833** | |
| «**Franciscus** *Liberatus* filius» | 26 Januarii **1840** | |
| «**Leopoldina Maria** eorum ***filia***» | 17 9bris **1829** | |
| «**Regina Theresia** eorum ***filia***» | 19 Junii **1830** *or* **1836** | |

*The book lists* **sons first, then daughters**, *so the dates do not run in order — the same structure as [the Gologorica census](/gologorica-line/).*

**⭐ THE ONE THING READING IT ADDS, AND IT IS WORTH THE HOUR.** ***Francisca is not on this page.*** *The children of this couple begin in* **1823** *and the marriage is* **1819**. *A daughter born 3 February 1819 is not theirs.*

**So «Gallignana house 5» points at the generation ABOVE Giovanni Battista** — *his own parents' household — and that is precisely the generation [this archive holds only from the family chart and not from a register page](/direct-line/).* ***The woman who married into Gologorica in 1840 is the handle on it.***

**⚠⚠ TWO CONTRADICTIONS INSIDE THIS ARCHIVE, FOUND BY SETTING THREE FILES AGAINST ONE IMAGE.**

| | one file says | another says |
|---|---|---|
| *death of Joan. Bapt.* | «**1 September 1846**» *(plate caption)* | «**obiit 14. Sept. 1846**» *(direct line)* |
| *Regina Theresia, born* | **1830** *(direct line)* | **1836** *(roster)* |

***Neither can be settled from the image this archive holds***, *which is a photocopy of a microfilm frame supplied by DAPA in 2021, and at the magnification it will bear the figures are genuinely ambiguous.* **Reel ZM34K-217 is not one of the two this archive owns.** *[Both are raised rather than resolved.](/worklist/)*

**⭐ AND TWO PEOPLE MOVE FROM INFERENCE TO DOCUMENT.** *[Raymundus de Franceschi (1823)](/person/raymundus-de-franceschi-1823/) and [Regina Theresia de Franceschi (1836)](/person/regina-theresia-de-franceschi-1836/) both carry the roster note* «**tree-derived: no register has been read for this person here**». ***This is a register page, and it names them both***, *with their father, their mother and their house. The note is wrong on both rows and is corrected.*

**⚠⚠ AND THE REASON THIS PAGE EXISTS AT ALL IS A FAILURE WORTH PRINTING.** *[Yesterday this archive announced as its own discovery that Joanna came from Gallignana house 4](/gologorica-line/), closed a work-list row on it, and raised two more.* **Joanna was documented here on 30 September** — *her house 4, her marriage of 13 February 1843, her six children, and the sentence* «her marriage is one of two in three years that took a Defranceschi daughter out of Gračišće and into Gologorica — hers from house 4 in 1843, and Francisca's from house 5 in 1840».

***That is the third time in two days that work already done here has been published as new, and the second method note about it was written yesterday.*** *[The correction is on the record.](/corrections/)*

notbaptised.heading: ⭐⭐ The head of the direct line was not baptised at Gračišće — and in ten years of its baptisms the surname never appears
notbaptised.lead: **The earlier house 5** Status Animarum *is on reel* **ZM34K-217**, *which this archive does not hold — that is [an errand, and the hold stands](/worklist/).* ***But the generation above is reachable from the shelf without writing to anybody***: *the Gračišće* **baptism register 1746–1840** *is on reel ZM34K-215, and a baptism names a father.*
paras:
**⚠⚠ HIS BAPTISM IS NOT IN IT.** *[This archive has Joannes Baptista Defranceschi born](/direct-line/)* «**13 Augusti 1787**», *«of Gallignana house 5». The register for that August (M01070195, headed* «Annus 1787»*) holds* ***three*** *entries between 30 July and 2 September:*

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **30 July** | *house 196* | **Josephus**, *father* «Josephus **Fernasar**» |
| **⟨—⟩ August** | *house 179* | **Francisca**, *father* «Georgius Limatich» — ***the whole entry struck through and annotated*** «**rescissa**» |
| **23 August** | *house 96* | **Josephus**, *father* «Mathæus Vojscovich» |

***There is no 13 August, and there is no Defranceschi.*** *The sequence 27 July → 23 August → 2 September is unbroken, so this is a gap in the register's content and not in the reading of it.*

**⭐⭐ AND THE SURNAME IS NOT IN THE BOOK AT ALL IN THAT DECADE.** *The father column was taken off* **twelve consecutive frames**, *M01070190–M01070201 — roughly* **three hundred baptisms, 1783 to 1792**. *The surnames that recur are the ones this family would later marry:* **Salamon** *(Joannes, Maria, Josephus, Barbara),* **Fernasar** *(Josephus, Georgius, Maria, Appolonia),* **Sestan** *(Joannes, Antonius, Joanna),* Picot, Milotich, Miandrusich, Lanza, Brosan, Bursich, Zulle, Poldrugovaz, Vuxa, Jerbula. ***Not one Defranceschi.***

**⭐⭐⭐ PUT THAT BESIDE WHAT THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY KNEW AND IT CHANGES THE SHAPE OF THE LINE.** *[The whole Gračišće baptism book of 1667–1745 has been read leaf by leaf, and the surname occurs in it* **five times** *— a count in 1720, a priest in 1734, and three others](/open-questions/).* **Five in seventy-eight years, then none in ten.**

***So the Defranceschi were not an established Gračišće family in the eighteenth century.*** *«Gallignana house 5», which this archive has treated as where the direct line comes from, looks instead like somewhere the line* **arrived** — *and the arrival is datable: after the baptisms of 1792, and before Joannes Baptista married there in* **1819**.

**⚠ WHAT THIS IS NOT, STATED CAREFULLY, BECAUSE IT IS A NEGATIVE AND NEGATIVES OVERREACH EASILY.**

- *The* **father** *column was read, at contact-sheet magnification. A Defranceschi could stand in the* **mother's** *maiden name or among the* **godparents** *— and [one pair does, in 1808](/gologorica-line/).*
- *The pages carry about twenty-five entries each in a small hand.* «None seen in twelve frames» *is what is claimed;* «none exists» *is not.*
- *The birth date itself comes from a* Status Animarum, *a compilation. If* **13 August 1787** *is wrong, the baptism may sit elsewhere in the book — though the surname's total absence from the decade makes that the lesser problem.*

**AND ONE THING CAME FREE AT THE FOOT OF THE PAGE.** *Under the last entry of 1787 stands the original certificate:* «**Exhib. In Visitatione Spirituali Gallignianæ die 24 Aprilis**», *signed by* «M. Bruñus Francovich … **Cancel. Epis.**» *and* «P. Petr. Martinus Hocovich … **Cancell. Visit.**» — *the episcopal chancellor and the chancellor of the visitation.* ***[This archive knows the 1788 spiritual visitation only through Orbanić's printed edition](/the-library/); here is the parish's own copy of it, signed.***

nastavljase.heading: «NASTAVLJA SE» — the Gračišće baptism book stops in May 1808, as this archive's own errand already said
nastavljase.lead:
**⚠ Said first: [errand 35 already recorded this card and this frame](/corrections/), with the continuation reel, its frame range and a drafted letter.** *What follows is a verification of that, and the sweep around it — which is new.*

*The sweep for the first Defranceschi ran forward from 1783 and stopped at a wall. Frame* **M01070226** *is the last page of register, its entries running on to* «**18 Maij**» *1808. The next frame is not a page.*
paras:
> **M01070227** — *a filmed target, in letters four inches high:*
> «**NASTAVLJA SE**»
> «**TO BE CONTINUED**»

***So the Gračišće baptism register «1746–1840» runs on this film only to May 1808.*** *The remaining ten frames of reel ZM34K-215 are a trailer of cards — a laboratory production card, then title cards for Gologorica's* Status Animarum *of 1862, 1894 and 1921 and for both Gračišće baptism books — and then blank film.*

**⚠⚠ WHICH CORRECTS THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN FRAME MAP.** *[The map of all 1,463 frames](/parish-books/) assigned* **M01070131–M01070236** *to this book. The register pages end at* **M01070226**. *The map was built by scanning every frame for ink coverage, which finds a* **title card** — *and a* «NASTAVLJA SE» *target is not a title card.* *[Corrected, with the trailer frames described rather than left inside a book they are not part of.](/parish-books/)*

**⭐ AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE USEFUL PART.** *The two Defranceschi brides who [came out of Gračišće houses 4 and 5 into Gologorica](/gologorica-line/) were born* **25 June 1818** *and* **3 February 1819**. ***Both fall after the film stops.*** **Their baptisms are not missing from the register; they are on a reel this archive does not have.** *[That is a different problem with a different answer](/worklist/) — and it means the window for the family's arrival at Gračišće can be closed from the shelf only as far as* **1792–1808**, *not 1792–1819.*

**WHAT THE SWEEP ITSELF FOUND, AND ITS TERMS.** *The* Pater *column was read across* **thirty-six consecutive frames, M01070190–M01070226** — *1783 to May 1808, roughly* **nine hundred baptisms**. ***Not one Defranceschi father.*** *The surnames that fill it are the ones this family would marry — Salamon, Fernasar, Sestan — with Picot, Milotich, Miandrusich, Lanza, Brosan, Bursich, Zulle, Poldrugovaz, Vuxa, Jerbula, Dermit, Cincopan, Vlahovich, Carlin, Scubla, Marletta, Berdebich, Zruselich.*

**⚠ AND THE EARLIER HALF CANNOT BE SWEPT THE SAME WAY, WHICH THE FILM ALSO EXPLAINS.** *Before about 1783 this book is not a ruled table at all — it is* **continuous Latin prose**, «Die … ego … baptizavi … filium legitimum … et uxoris ejus …», *with no column a surname can be read down. And the leaves carry the filmers' own label:*

> «**WATER DAMAGE**» · «**OŠTEĆENO OD VLAGE**»

***So 1746 to about 1783 is recorded here as a NAMED GAP, not as a nil.*** *[It needs reading entry by entry at full magnification, and the condition note says some of it may not be readable at all.](/worklist/) **What this archive may not do is call it empty because it was hard to look at.**

fedenascita.heading: ⭐⭐ A certificate loose in the book confirms the diocese — from a second parish, nine years earlier
fedenascita.lead: **Bound in near the front of the Gračišće baptism book, on ruled paper and in a different hand from everything around it, is a loose certificate** — *and its letterhead is the finding.*
paras:
> «**Diocesi di Trieste - Capo d'Istria** *nel* **Litorale austriaco**» · «**Distretto di Pisino**»
>
> «**Fede di Nascita**»
>
> «*Pietro figlio legittimo del defunto* **Martino Krisman** *agricoltore e della defunta* **Maria nata Jerach**, *nato a* **Scopliaco** *(Parrocchia di Gallignana) sub* **N.ᵒ 11** *— li* **28 (ventiotto) Giugno 1836** *(milleottocentotrentasei) — fu battezzato dal Molto Rᵈᵒ Signore* **Don Antonio Scubla Parroco di Gallignana**. *Padrini alla s. Fonte erano:* **Giovanni Runco** *e la di lui Consorte* **Mattea**. *Levatrice:* **Maria Trelesco**.»
>
> «*Dall' Ufficio parrocchiale di* **Gallignana li 25 Marzo 1867**» — *L.S.* — «fᵗᵒ: **Mattia Zimmermann Parroco**»

**⭐⭐ ON 6 OCTOBER THIS ARCHIVE ESTABLISHED THAT GOLOGORICA'S DIOCESE WAS TRIESTE–CAPODISTRIA, [FROM A BISHOP'S SIGNATURE OF 1876](/gologorica-line/).** *Here is the same fact from* ***a different parish, a different kind of document, and nine years earlier*** — *written by the parish priest of Gallignana, on his own office's stationery, in* **1867**, *describing where he was.*

***That is the shape corroboration should have:*** *not a louder version of the first source, but a second one that could have disagreed and does not.*

**AND IT NAMES TWO PARISH PRIESTS OF GALLIGNANA THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE.** «**Don Antonio Scubla**», *baptising in* **1836**, *and* «**Mattia Zimmermann**», *signing in* **1867**. *[The hands in the Gologorica registers are now all named](/gologorica-line/); the Gračišće ones are not, and these are the first two.* **⚠ Scubla is also a Gallignana surname** — *a* «Jacobus Scubla» *fathers a child in the 1787 baptisms — so the priest of 1836 may be a local man, and that is a question, not a claim.*

**⚠ TWO THINGS NOT ESTABLISHED.** *Why an* **1867** *certificate is loose in a book that closes in* **1808** — *a spoiled copy, a working draft, or simply filed where it fell; nothing on the frame says.* *And* «**Scopliaco**», *a hamlet of the parish with its own house numbering,* ***is not on this archive's gazetteer*** *and is [raised rather than guessed at](/worklist/).*

gollagoriciensis.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ «Josephus de Franceschi GOLLAGORICIENSIS» — the register says which village they came from, and it is the other one
gollagoriciensis.lead: **Sweeping the prose half of the Gračišće baptism book frame by frame has found the surname — twice in four years — and both times it is standing at the font, never in the father's place.**
paras:
> **12 March 1747** *(M01070137)* — «**Franciscus Gregorius** filius legitimus **Judicis Ignatij** [Martinich] et **Luciæ** uxoris ejus baptizatus est à me Canᵒ **Vito Drusetich**. *Patrini fuerunt* **Joannes Petrus de Franceschi** *nec non* **Joanna uxor Judicis Joannis Salamon**.»
>
> **2 April 1750** *(M01070142)* — «**Joannes Petrus** filius legitimus **judicis Ignatij Martinich** et **Lucia** jugalium. *Patrini fuerunt* **Josephus de Franceschi *Gollagoriciensis*** *et* **Maria Milotich uxor Gregorij**.»

**⭐⭐⭐ «GOLLAGORICIENSIS» — *of Gologorica*.** *The Gračišće register, writing in 1750, labels a Defranceschi godfather by the village he came from, and that village is* **the other one**.

**⚠ AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY SEEN THAT PATTERN, IN THE BOOK BEFORE THIS ONE.** *[Its note on Count Damian de Franceschis records that the 1667–1745 Gračišće book was read leaf by leaf and the surname occurs five times —](/open-questions/)* «*three times a Defranceschi* **of Gologorica** *standing godparent, in 1733, 1743 and 1744*», *the count being* «the only one of the five who is **not from Gologorica**».

***So the shape was known. What this sweep adds is that it continues unbroken into the next volume*** — *six more appearances, five more epithets, down to 1783.* **[An earlier version of this paragraph called it a reversal of what the archive believed. It was not, and that is published as a correction.](/corrections/)**

**⭐⭐ AND THE SAME HOUSEHOLD ASKED THEM TWICE — THEN NAMED A CHILD AFTER ONE OF THEM.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **5 May 1744** *(folio 160, the* previous *book)* | «D.nus **Joannes Petrus Defranceschi** et Mattia uxor Suppani **Joannis Grach**», *at the baptism of a* **daughter** *of* «**Dominus Ignatius Martinich** et Donna **Lucia**» — *[already in this archive](/direct-line/)* |
| **12 March 1747** | *the same couple's* **son** *— and* «**Joannes Petrus de Franceschi**» *stands again* |
| **2 April 1750** | *the same couple's next son is* ***christened* «Joannes Petrus»** — *and* «**Josephus de Franceschi Gollagoriciensis**» *stands* |

***A village judge asked a Defranceschi to the font three times in six years and then gave the man's name to his own child.*** **That is not a courtesy; it is a standing relationship**, *and it is the earliest tie between this surname and Gračišće that the archive can date.*

**AND THE CO-GODPARENTS ARE THE TWO SURNAMES THAT MATTER.** *In 1744 it is a* «**Grach**» *wife; in 1747 and again in 1750 the other sponsor is* «**Joanna uxor Judicis Joannis Salamon**» *or a Milotich.* **[Grach and Salamon are both married-in surnames of this family](/married-in/)** — *Salamon above all, since [Francisca Salomon married Giovanni Battista Defranceschi in 1819](/maternal/salomon/).* ***Seventy-two years before that marriage, a Defranceschi and a Salamon were standing at the same font.***

**⚠ WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** *That either godfather is an ancestor of this line — neither entry gives a father, an age or a house.* *That* «Joannes Petrus» *and* «Josephus» *are related to each other.* *And the 1750 epithet describes* **one man on one day**: *it is strong evidence about where he lived and it is not, by itself, a statement about the whole surname.* *[The sweep continues.](/worklist/)*

sixgodparents.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ Sixty-two years of Gračišće baptisms: six Defranceschi, every one a godparent, five of them «of Gologorica»
sixgodparents.lead: **The Gračišće baptism register has now been read frame by frame from its first leaf to where the film breaks** — *M01070132 to M01070226,* **1746 to May 1808**, *the prose half one opening at a time at full magnification because [it has no column a surname can be read down and the film labels it* «WATER DAMAGE»](/gologorica-line/).
paras:
**THE SURNAME OCCURS SIX TIMES. NOT ONCE AS A PARENT.**

| | who | standing for |
|---|---|---|
| **12 Mar 1747** | «**Joannes Petrus de Franceschi**» | *Franciscus Gregorius, son of* **Judge Ignatius Martinich** *and Lucia* |
| **2 Apr 1750** | «**Josephus de Franceschi *Gollagoriciensis***» | «**Joannes Petrus**», *son of the same couple* |
| **6 Feb 1752** | «**D.na Elena uxor D.ni Josephi Defranceschi** … *Gollagoritia*» | *Blasius Ignatius, son of the same couple* |
| **16 Feb 1755** | «**Petrus Defranceschi *a Gollagoriza***» | *Maria, daughter of* **Michael Grach** *and Lucia* |
| **13 Apr 1766** | «**Antonius Defranceschi *ex Gollagorizia***» | *Joannes, son of Antonius and Maria Anna* |
| **8 Jun 1783** | «**Joannes Bapta et Helena Defranceschi *Gollogoricienses***» | *Antonius Joannes, son of* **Judge Franciscus Martinich** *and Francisca* |

***Five of the six carry the epithet. The register itself says, over and over, that these people came from the other village.***

**⭐⭐ AND FOUR OF THE SIX ARE FOR THE SAME FAMILY OF VILLAGE JUDGES, ACROSS FORTY YEARS.** *[This archive already held a fifth, from the previous book](/direct-line/):* **5 May 1744**, «D.nus Joannes Petrus Defranceschi et Mattia uxor … Joannis **Grach**», *at the baptism of* **Ignatius Martinich** *and Lucia's* **daughter**.

> *1744 — their daughter.* *1747 — their son.* ***1750 — their next son is christened* «Joannes Petrus».** *1752 — another son.* *1783 — the next generation's son, for* **Judge Franciscus** *Martinich.*

***A family of Gračišće judges asked the Defranceschi of Gologorica to the font five times in forty years, and gave one of them his name back in a child.*** **That is the oldest datable tie between this surname and Gračišće, and it is not a tie of residence.**

**⭐⭐ THE 1783 PAIR ARE ALMOST CERTAINLY MOTHER AND SON, AND THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HAS BOTH OF THEM.** *[«D.nus Joannes Bapta Defranceschi, viduus, son of the late Josephus» died 23 January 1813 aged 60](/gologorica-line/) — born about 1753. [«Domina Helena, widow of the late Josephus Defranceschi» died 26 August 1804 aged 84](/gologorica-line/) — born about 1720.* **Same Josephus.** *In 1783 she would be sixty-three and he thirty.*

**⚠ The entry says only** «Joannes Bapta et Helena Defranceschi Gollogoricienses» — *two people of the surname, of Gologorica. ***The identification is an inference and is labelled one***; what is documented is that a Joannes Baptista and a Helena of this name stood together at a Gračišće font on 8 June 1783.*

**⭐ AND HELENA'S LIFE GETS FIFTY-TWO YEARS LONGER.** *This archive knew her from* **one line of a death register in 1804**. *She is now also* «**D.na Elena uxor D.ni Josephi Defranceschi**», *standing godmother at Gračišće on* **6 February 1752** — *married, styled* Domina, *and travelling to another parish to stand for a judge's child. [Her row carried no dated appearance before her burial.](/person/helena-defranceschi-1725/)*

**⚠⚠ SO THE DIRECT LINE'S «GALLIGNANA HOUSE 5» IS NOT WHERE THIS FAMILY CAME FROM.** *Sixty-two years of baptisms, roughly fifteen hundred children, and* ***not one Defranceschi father***. *[Five occurrences in the whole 1667–1745 book before it](/open-questions/). The eighteenth-century Defranceschi were* **Gologorica people with friends at Gračišće** — *the register says so in five separate hands.*

***[Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, born 13 August 1787 «of Gallignana house 5», is not in this book either](/gologorica-line/)*** — *and the stretch that would show the family arriving is [on the reel the film breaks before](/worklist/).*

**HOW IT WAS READ.** *Fifty-eight prose openings one at a time, each whole opening at about two-thirds scale, plus the thirty-six ruled-table frames already swept by the* Pater *column. The surnames that fill the book are Martinich, Milotich, Druscetich, Salamon, Fernasar, Sestan, Picot, Lanza, Brosan, Bursich, Poldrugovaz, Zulle, Miandrusich, Grach, Baxa, Jerbula, Godenich, Scubla.* **⚠ Six hits in fifteen hundred entries is the kind of count a single tired page could change** — *the frames are named above so the next reader can check any of them.*

visitation1732.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ The Gračišće register certifies its own gaps — a visitor in 1732 found entries missing and ordered them written in
visitation1732.lead: **Between a baptism of 17 July 1732 and one of 12 August, on folio 134, the parish priest's hand stops and another begins.** *It is not an entry.* ***It is a decree, left in the book by the man who had just inspected it, and it says the book is incomplete.***
paras:
> «**Die 18 Lulij 1732 — In Visitatione &c.**
> *Attentis* **ommissionibus repertis in libro hoc Baptizatorum**, *seriò admonentur omnes Ministri huius Sacramenti ut quàmprimùm comodè fieri poterit, imò nulla interposita mora, diligenter adnottentur* **quæque per negligentiam omissa fuère**, *et in posterum observetur formula in Rituali Romano præscripta, sub pœna arbitrii &c. et ita &c.*
> **Fran.cus Augustinus Corsi Vic.us Gen.lis, et Præpositus**»

*«The* **omissions found in this book of the baptised** *having been noted, all ministers of this Sacrament are seriously admonished that — as soon as it may conveniently be done, indeed with no delay interposed — whatever was* **omitted through negligence** *be diligently entered, and that in future the form prescribed in the Roman Ritual be observed, under penalty at discretion.»* — **`doc`**, *[M01070082, folio 134](/plates/)*.

**⭐⭐ WHAT IT DOES TO EVERY NIL THIS ARCHIVE REPORTS FROM THIS BOOK, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF IT.** *This page has spent a fortnight reading the 1667–1745 Gallignana baptism register frame by frame in order to say how many times the surname occurs in it, and [the count it is checking is five](/direct-line/).* ***The decree says a count of what this book contains cannot be a count of what happened.*** *The authority that inspected the register in 1732 recorded, in the register, that baptisms had been celebrated and never written down. A Defranceschi child could have been baptised at Gračišće before July 1732, be absent from these leaves, and the register still be a true register — because its own visitor says so.* **The nil stands as a nil of this book. It is not a nil of these years.**

**⭐⭐ AND HE IS NOT A STRANGER TO THIS PARISH — HE BAPTISES IN IT.** *Four frames on, at* **M01070086, folio 137**, *the same man writes in his own person and gives his style in full:*

> «**Die 3 Februarij 1733.** *Nicolaum filium legitimum* **Judicis Joanis, et Joannæ Uxoris** *jugalium* **Jurich Salamon** *Baptizavi de Licentia Parochi* **Fran.ᶜᵘˢ Augustinus Corsi Vic.ᵘˢ Gen.ˡⁱˢ Petenensis et Præpositus Pisini**. *Patrini fuere* **Jacobus Carlovich**, *et* **Catharina Vidua q.ᵐ Suppani Matthæi Sestan**.»

***Vicar General of Pedena and Provost of Pisino — Pazin.*** **`doc`.** *He inspects the book in July 1732 and is back at the font in February 1733, baptising the son of the village judge under the parish priest's licence.*

**⚠ This archive first read the decree's abbreviated signature as the same office that [baptised Count Damian de Franceschis' son here in 1720](/direct-line/) —** «Marino Iosepho Bellaz **Præposito, nec non Vicario Cathedralis Ecclesiæ Petinensis**» — *and [published that as an inference this morning. It is wrong, and the register itself refuted it](/corrections/): Bellaz is Provost of the* **cathedral of Pedena**, *Corsi is Provost of* **Pazin**. *Two dignitaries of one small diocese, not two holders of one post.* ***What survives is the useful part*** — *two named men of Pedena-diocesan rank, twelve years apart, both at Gallignana, both leaving their hand in this book — and [Corsi's visitation file is now a row of its own](/worklist/).*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE BOOK SHOWS THE ORDER BEING OBEYED, SIX LEAVES LATER — WITH A DEFRANCESCHI INSIDE IT.** *This morning this page reasoned, as* `inf`, *that the volume's famous disorder was the decree at work.* ***It is not an inference any more.*** *At the foot of* **M01070088, folio 138** — *whose own entries run* **January to May 1734** — *comes a run of six baptisms in a smaller, fainter hand, under a one-word heading and a rule, dated* **29 April 1732, 21 September 1732, 16 December 1732, 21 December 1732, 8 January 1733 and 10 January 1733**. *Every one of them is a year or two older than the leaf it sits on, and every one is signed by a canon, not the archpriest who fills the page above.* **These are the late entries. They are written where there was room, at the bottom of a later folio, exactly as a priest obeying the 1732 order would write them.**

**⭐⭐ And the fifth of those six is one of the five Defranceschi occurrences this archive counts in the volume:**

> «*Die 8 Januarij 1733. Josephus legitimus filius* **Marini Cincopan** *et Luciæ uxoris, ego Can.ˢ* **Grach** *baptizavi. Patrini fuerunt* **Judex Gregorius Milcovich** *et* **Joana Uxor Sup.ⁿⁱ Joanis Bapt.ᵃᵉ Defranceschi**»

*[Word for word as this archive published it](/direct-line/) — ✔ verified on the page.* ***But its position is new, and it changes what the entry is evidence of.*** *Joanna's appearance at that font was* **not written down at the time**. *It was recovered afterwards, under the Vicar General's order, by a different priest. [The archive's count of five rests on entries that the register itself classes as recoveries](/method/) — which cuts both ways: it is why this one survives at all, and it is why the ones never recovered are not here to be counted.*

*⚠ **The heading over the block has not been read.** It is one word, faint, in a hand that writes it nowhere else on the leaf, and [this archive's rule is that a hand is only legible against itself](/method/) — there is no second construction to compare it against, so staring harder would only produce a guess with a transcription's authority. [Raised as its own row.](/worklist/)*

**HOW IT WAS FOUND, WHICH IS NOT A CLEVER METHOD BUT A SLOW ONE.** *Frames M01070076 to M01070084 were read for a nil — nine openings, 1726 to 1736, no Defranceschi in any column — and the decree is in the middle of the ninth, in the right-hand page's second block, looking from a distance exactly like another baptism.* **It was read because the rule here is that every frame is read, including the ones that are obviously more of the same.** *[The surnames that fill these leaves](/gologorica-line/) are Drusetich, Salomon, Fernasar, Sestan, Baxa, Poldrugovaz, Martinich, Milotich, Grach, Putigna, Miculin, Scubla, Clay, Bursich, Berdetich — and on 1 October 1727* «**Antonij Fiernaser et eius Uxoris Joannæ**», *which is the Fernasar hand again, in a third construction.*

**⭐⭐ ONE MORE THING FOLIO 138 GIVES, AND IT IS ABOUT THE FAMILY RATHER THAN THE BOOK.** *The first entry of the* **19 March 1734** *leaf is:*

> «*Die 19 Martij 1734.* **Presbiter Philippus de Franceschi** *Baptizavit* **Josephum Antonium** *filium legitimum* **Ignatij Martinich** *et Uxoris* **Luciæ**. *Patrini fuerunt Antonius Derbaltæ et* **Margaritta uxor Francisci Sestan**.»

*✔ The second of the five, verified word for word.* ***And the child is the giveaway.*** *[This archive already holds four Defranceschi appearances for one Gračišće couple](/gologorica-line/) —* **Ignatius Martinich and Lucia** — *in* **1744** *(their daughter),* **1747** *(their son Franciscus Gregorius) and* **1750** *(their son Joannes Petrus), with Helena standing in 1752.* **1734 is ten years earlier than the earliest of them, and it is not a godparent: it is a Defranceschi priest at the altar baptising their son.**

> *The tie to that household now runs* **1734 · 1744 · 1747 · 1750** — *sixteen years, four children, and it opens with a priest of the name rather than a neighbour of it.*

**AND THE SESTAN ARE THE OTHER HALF OF IT.** *Margaritta, wife of* **Franciscus Sestan**, *is godmother here; on [folio 137 the godmother is* «**Catharina Vidua q.ᵐ Suppani Matthæi Sestan**»](/gologorica-line/) — ***the widow of the late headman of Gračišće***. *[The Defranceschi were headmen at Gologorica](/direct-line/); the Sestan were headmen at Gračišće;* **and a century later two Defranceschi daughters of Gračišće houses 4 and 5 marry two Sestan of Gologorica**. *[The two families were each other's opposite numbers over the hill long before they were each other's in-laws.](/households/)* **`inf`** *for the continuity of the families across that gap — the name is common and no descent is traced here — but* **`doc`** *for every entry above.*

judgeshousehold.heading: ⭐⭐ The household the Defranceschi kept coming back to — six children of one Gračišće couple, and the three they were asked for
judgeshousehold.lead: **Reading the 1736–1743 stretch of the Gračišće baptism book frame by frame turns a list of godparent appearances into a family.** *[The archive has long held that four of its Defranceschi occurrences serve «the same family of village judges»](/direct-line/).* ***The sweep can now name the children, and say which ones the Defranceschi were not asked for — which is the more useful half.***
paras:
**IGNATIUS MARTINICH AND LUCIA, OF GALLIGNANA.** *He is* «D.nus» *in 1734 and* «**Judex**» *by 1742 — the village judge. These are their children as the register gives them, each read on its own frame:*

| | child | baptised by | godparents |
|---|---|---|---|
| **19 Mar 1734** | *Josephus Antonius* | ***Presbiter Philippus de Franceschi*** | *Antonius Derbaltæ · Margaritta ux. Francisci* **Sestan** |
| **8 Apr 1740** | *Joanna Petronila* | *Vito Drusetich* | *Suppanus Gregorius* **Millotich** *· Helena his wife* |
| **18 Mar 1742** | *Lucia* | *Can. Mathias Milotich* | *Sup. Gregorius* **Millotich** *· Joanna ux. Judicis Joannis* **Salamon** |
| **5 May 1744** | ***Joanna*** | *Presbiter* **Joannes Grach** | ***D.nus Joannes Petrus Defranceschi*** *· Mattia ux.* **Suppani Joannis Grach** |
| **1747** | *Franciscus Gregorius* | — | ***Joannes Petrus de Franceschi*** |
| **1750** | *Joannes Petrus* | — | ***Josephus de Franceschi Gollagoriciensis*** |

*(The 1734, 1740 and 1742 rows are new to this archive, and the 1744 child's name and godmother were [recovered from a misread word](/corrections/), all in the sweep of 7–9 October; [the last three were already held](/direct-line/).)* **`doc`** *for every row.*

**⭐⭐ WHAT THE NEW ROWS DO, AND IT IS NOT WHAT MORE EVIDENCE USUALLY DOES — IT NARROWS THE CLAIM.** *With only the 1744, 1747 and 1750 entries in hand it was natural to read the Defranceschi as* **this household's godparents**. *They are not.* ***Of six children, the Defranceschi are asked for three; the Millotich are asked for two, and the Millotich are the family that stands when the Defranceschi do not.*** *Gregorius Millotich is* «Suppanus» — *headman of Gračišće — so the judge's children are shared between the local headman's family and a headman's family from over the hill.*

> **That is a better fact than an exclusive friendship would have been.** *It places the Defranceschi inside a* **rota of the parish's office-holding families**, *not in a private attachment to one house — and a rota is the kind of thing a village has reasons for.*

**⭐ AND IT PUSHES THE TIE BACK TEN YEARS, WITH A DIFFERENT KIND OF PERSON AT THE FONT.** *The earliest contact is* **1734**, *and it is not a neighbour standing godparent — it is* «**Presbiter Philippus de Franceschi**» *saying the words over the judge's son. [Verified on the page, with a letter of the father's name corrected](/corrections/).* ***A priest of the surname was available to this parish in 1734***, *sixteen years before* «Josephus de Franceschi **Gollagoriciensis**» *stands at the same family's font in 1750.*

**⭐⭐ THE BISHOP OF PEDENA BAPTISES AT GRAČIŠĆE IN PERSON — TWICE IN SEVEN WEEKS.** *[This archive already holds a bishop at a Gallignana font in 1672](/worklist/), Andreas Daniel von Raunach, standing with his own kin. Here is a second, named:*

> «*Die 28 Aprilis 1743.* **Ill.mus ac R.mus D.nus Josephus Bonifacius Ceccoti Dei gratiâ Ep.us Petenensis** *baptizavit Joannam filiam legitimam Suppani* **Gregorij Sirol** *et Joannæ Uxoris ejus. Compatres fuêre D.nus* **Antonius Rovis** *nec non D.na Margharita Uxor D.ni* **Francisci Sestan** *ambo* **Petenenses**.»

*And again on* **15 June 1743**, *for the daughter of* «D.ni Josephi Godenich et D.næ Franciscæ». **`doc`.** *[The diocese of Pićan is the one this archive established for the parish before 1788](/gologorica-line/); its bishop turns out to have been on the ground here, and [so was his Vicar General in 1732 and 1733](/gologorica-line/).* ***A small poor diocese whose bishops were said never to reside in it is nonetheless at this village font repeatedly.***

**AND THE GRACH ARE THE CONSTANT, WHICH THE SURNAME COUNT HIDES.** *On* **26 June 1743** *Joanna Defranceschi stands for a* **Grach** *child beside the* **Grach** *priest:* «*Baptizavi Joannam filiam legitimam* **Josephi Grach**, *et uxoris ejus Mariæ Annæ. Patrini fuerunt* **R.di D.ni Joannes Grach**, *et* **Joanna uxor Suppani Jo: Baptistæ Defranceschi de Golagoriza**» — *[verified on the page, with the preposition corrected from* «à» *to* «de»](/direct-line/). *In* **1744** *a Defranceschi stands for a Martinich child beside* **Mattia, wife of Joannis Grach**. *Joannes Grach is a deacon in July 1742 and* «R.dus D.nus» *by June 1743; a* «Presbyter Michael Grach» *was baptising here in the 1680s; and [the Grach are judges of the town from 1667](/worklist/).* ***Whatever brought the Defranceschi over the hill, the Grach are on both ends of it.***

**⭐⭐ AND THE LAST ENTRY OF THE FIVE TURNS THE ROTA INTO A SENTENCE.** *[The 5 May 1744 godmother had been read as](/corrections/)* «Mattia uxor **supradicti** Joannis Grach» — *the aforesaid, which pointed back at the priest who had just performed the baptism.* ***The word is*** «**Suppani**». *Set the two Defranceschi entries of these years side by side as the register actually writes them:*

> **26 June 1743** — «*R.di D.ni Joannes Grach, et* **Joanna uxor Suppani Jo: Baptistæ Defranceschi de Golagoriza**»
> **5 May 1744** — «*D.nus* **Joannes Petrus Defranceschi** *et* **Mattia uxor Suppani Joannis Grach**»

***Two headmen's households, one from each village, standing within eleven months at the same font.*** *Gračišće's headman's wife and Gologorica's headman's wife; Gologorica's headman's son and Gračišće's headman's priest-kinsman.* **This is not a family calling on its betters, and it is not a family being patronised. It is two village offices treating each other as equals, in the only document that records such a thing.** **`doc`** *for both entries;* **`inf`** *for reading the pattern as equality of office — but the register gives both men the same word.*

*⚠ **Two men named Joannes Grach must now be kept apart**: the* **Presbiter** *who baptises through 1742–44, and the* **Suppanus** *whose wife is Mattia. [The archive had one person where the register has two](/corrections/), and any future row for either must say which.*

confirmations.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ The sweep is finished — and the confirmation rolls at the back of the book, which the archive had listed and never read, hold no Defranceschi
confirmations.lead: **The Gračišće baptism register of 1667–1745 has now been read frame by frame from its title page to the film's** «**KRAJ · END OF ITEM**» *card —* ***M01069943 to M01070130, one hundred and eighty-eight frames, every one***. *[The five Defranceschi occurrences the archive counted are all verified on the page](/worklist/), and there is no sixth.* **The strongest evidence in the volume turned out to be in the part this archive had catalogued and never opened.**
paras:
**FOLIOS 165 TO 175 ARE NOT BAPTISMS. THEY ARE CONFIRMATION ROLLS, AND THERE ARE TWO OF THEM.**

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **16 [7bris] 1690** | «*confirmati ab Ill.mo et R.mo D.no* **Joanne Marco Rossetti Ep.o Petinense**» | *folios 165–171* |
| **15 Junij 1694** | «*confirmati ab Ill.mo et R.mo D.no D.no* **Petro Antonio Delle de Hohenberg Ep.o Petenensi, Sac.æ Cæs.æ Maiestatis Consiliario**» | *folios 174–175, numbered to* **74** |

*Each line gives a child, the parent, and the sponsor:* «**Gregorius filius Georgij Fernasar, cuius compater fuit D. Grach**». **`doc`.**

**⚠⚠ AND THE HALF OF THIS THAT IS NOT NEW, SAID FIRST.** ***This archive already knew the rolls were there.*** *[The film's own title card, transcribed here on 30 September, reads](/direct-line/)* «**MATIČNA KNJIGA ROĐENIH 1667-1745 · MATIČNA KNJIGA KRIZMANIH 1690-1694**» — *the register of the baptised and* ***the register of the confirmed*** *— and [the frame map on this page has carried* «Rođeni · Krizmani · 1667–1745 · 1690–1694» *ever since](/gologorica-line/).* **What was new on 9 October is not that they exist. It is that somebody read them.** *[The same failure has now happened often enough in this archive to be a habit worth naming](/method/): a thing catalogued is not a thing examined, and the catalogue entry is the easiest place in the world not to look.*

**⭐⭐⭐ WHY READING THEM MATTERED SO MUCH MORE THAN LISTING THEM.** *A baptism register records the children born in a year.* ***A confirmation roll records every child of the parish old enough to be confirmed, gathered on one day, when the bishop came.*** *It is as close to a* **roll-call of the town's households** *as a parish produces, and it does not depend on a scribe remembering to write an entry the week it happened — [which is precisely the failure the 1732 visitor found in the baptism half of this same volume](/gologorica-line/).*

> **Two such roll-calls, four years apart, in the years the family might have been here. Not one Defranceschi child. Not one Defranceschi sponsor.**

*The surnames that fill them are the ones that fill everything else at Gračišće —* **Braissa, Fernasar, Dilizza, Grach, Milotich, Drusetich, Poldrugovaz, Dermit, Salamun, Baxa, Cincopan, Jerbulla, Carlovich, Lupigna, Bertetich, Merletich, Maurovich, Chlaj, Picot, Scuich, Vale, Zotar, Sirol, Lanza, Brosan** — *and the Defranceschi are not among them.*

*⚠ **Stated with its limit.** The 1690 and 1694 rolls are in a small, abbreviated, heavily contracted hand and run to several hundred lines. This is a* **careful reading, not a transcription**, *and a surname could in principle hide in it.* **What is claimed is that the name was looked for, line by line, on every leaf, and not found** — *which is a stronger statement than this archive has ever been able to make about these years, and a weaker one than a transcription would be.*

**⭐⭐ AND IT CLOSES THE ARGUMENT THE 1732 DECREE HAD LEFT OPEN.** *[The visitation of 18 July 1732 recorded that baptisms had been omitted from this register through negligence](/gologorica-line/), which meant a nil from the baptism half could only ever be* «no Defranceschi baptism was **written into this book**» — *never* «no Defranceschi was born here». ***The confirmation rolls do not have that weakness.*** *They were made on a single day, in the bishop's presence, from the children actually standing in the church.*

> *So the sentence this archive can now write is the one it has been working toward for a fortnight:* **through the whole of the surviving seventeenth- and early-eighteenth-century record of Gračišće — two confirmation roll-calls and seventy-eight years of baptisms — the Defranceschi appear five times, every one of them as a visitor, and never once as a household of the parish.**

*Which is [what the family's own chart has always said](/direct-line/), and what [the 1826 census says from the other end](/gologorica-line/): they were* **Gologorica people**, *and they came over the hill [with the generation born at Gologorica casa 31 in 1787](/direct-line/).*

**THE BOOK WAS INSPECTED AGAIN IN 1745, AND THIS TIME THE VISITOR HAD NOTHING TO SAY.** *Drawn across the foot of folio 163, under the last entry:* «**Revisum in Visitatione &c. die 5. Maij 1745**» — *reviewed at the visitation.* **`doc`.** *[Thirteen years after the decree that found the register wanting](/gologorica-line/), and [six leaves after the block of recovered entries that obeyed it](/gologorica-line/), a visitor signs the book off without a complaint.* ***The archive now has the whole arc: the order, the compliance, and the clearance.***

**Four bishops of Pedena are in this one volume**, *which is worth setting down for a diocese whose own canons swore that no bishop had ever resided in it:* **Andreas Daniel von Raunach** *(baptising in person, 1672),* **Joannes Marcus Rossetti** *(confirming, 1690),* **Petrus Antonius Delle de Hohenberg** *(confirming, 1694), and* **Josephus Bonifacius Ceccoti** *(baptising in person twice in seven weeks, 1743) — besides [the Vicar General Corsi in 1732 and 1733](/gologorica-line/).*

**AND THE VERY LAST WRITTEN LEAF IS NOT A REGISTER PAGE.** *Folio 177 carries, in the middle of an otherwise blank sheet, the address panel of a folded letter:*

> «*Al Mol[t]o Rev.do In Christo Padre Pron'e Col.mo Il* **P. Valeriano da Fiume**, *Predicatore e Vicario della [Ve]nerabile Rel[igi]one* **Capucina di Fiume**»

*«To the Most Reverend Father in Christ, my most esteemed patron, Father* **Valeriano of Fiume**, *Preacher and Vicar of the Venerable Capuchin Order* **of Fiume**.»

***A letter-cover to a Capuchin at Fiume, bound into the back of a Gračišće parish register.*** **`doc`** *for the panel; how it got there is not recorded and is not guessed at here.* *⚠ It is* **not** *a document of this family — no Defranceschi is named on it. But [Fiume runs through this archive](/carlo/) — [Kobler's stocks of the surname](/the-library/), [the Fiume evidence of 1626](/fiume-1626/) — and a physical link between this parish's book and a Fiume religious house is worth [a row of its own](/worklist/) rather than a shrug.*

*One stray baptism of* «**1722 die 20 mensis 9bris**» *also sits at the back, after the confirmation rolls, in a deacon's hand — [one more of the misplaced entries this volume is full of](/gologorica-line/).*

patrinisweep.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ The column nobody read: twenty Defranceschi at the Gračišće font, 1791–1808, every one of them «cives»
patrinisweep.lead: **The Gračišće baptism register from 1783 is a ruled table, and this archive read one of its columns.** *[The* **Pater** *column, across thirty-six frames, nine hundred baptisms —* ***not one Defranceschi father***](/errands/). *From that it concluded the family was* «not established at Gračišće in the eighteenth century». ***The nil was right. The conclusion was not, and the archive's own search log had said so in advance.***
paras:
**THE WARNING WAS WRITTEN DOWN AND LEFT UNACTED ON.** *[The search record for that sweep carries this line](/searched/):*

> «*the* **father** *column was read … a Defranceschi could stand as a mother's maiden name or* **a godparent**, *and* **one pair does in 1808**. ***«None seen in twelve frames» is the claim; «none exists» is not.***»

*That is a correctly stated limit, written by the session that did the work.* **It sat there for two days.** *[The* **Patrini** *column of all thirty-seven frames has now been read, row by row.](/searched/)*

**TWENTY-ONE APPEARANCES, NOW DATED ONE BY ONE — AND THEY RUN IN AN UNBROKEN LINE FROM 1791 TO 1808.**

| | date | who stands | conditio | frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **13 Feb 1791** | «**Anna de Franceschi**» *with* «J. Bap. de Tranquillis» | ***Nobiles Pisinenses*** | *200* |
| 2 | 15 Sep 1792 | **Theresia** *w/ Antonius Jvich* | Supanus · **cives** | *203* |
| 3 | 20 Aug 1793 | **Theresia** *w/ Antonius Rovis* | **Cives** | *204* |
| 4 | 30 Aug 1793 | **Theresia** *w/ Antonius Jvich* | **Cives** | *204* |
| 5 | 7 Nov 1794 | **Theresia** *w/ Antonius Selesprch* | **Cives** | *206* |
| 6 | 20 Nov 1794 | «**Joannes**» **+** «**Theresia**» | **Cives** | *206* |
| 7 | **13 May 1796** | «**Joan: Bapta**» **+** «**Vincenca**» | **cives** | *209* |
| 8 | Mar 1797 | **Theresia** *w/ Sanctus Brosan* | **Cives** | *211* |
| 9 | 3 Dec 1797 | «**Joannes**» **+** «**Theresia**» | **Cives** | *211* |
| 10 | 26 Feb 1798 | **Theresia** *w/ Antonius Michnevich* | villicus · **civis** | *212* |
| 11 | 16 Oct 1798 | **Theresia** *w/ Antonius Picot (struck)* | **civis** | *213* |
| 12 | 7 Nov 1799 | «**Antonius**» **+** «**Theresia**» | **Cives** | *215* |
| 13 | 5 Dec 1800 | «**Joannes**» **+** *Lucia* **Martinich** | **Cives** | *216* |
| 14 | 8 May **1802** | **Theresia** *w/ Joannes Salamon* | **Cives** | *218* |
| 15 | 19 Jan **1801** | «**Joannes**» **+** *Maria Putigna* | **Cives** · villica | *217* |
| 16 | 25 Mar **1801** | **Theresia** *w/ Antonius Jvich* | Supanus · **Cives** | *217* |
| 17 | 9 May **1801** | «**Joannes**» **+** «**Theresia**» | **Cives** | *217* |
| 18 | 5 Sep **1801** | «**Antonius**» **+** «**Theresia**» | **Cives** | *217* |
| 19 | 12 Aug 1806 | **Theresia** *w/ Mathdus Slivar* | **Cives** | *223* |
| 20 | 12 Jun 1807 | «**Antonius**» **+** *Fusca Festa* | **civis** · agricola | *225* |
| 21 | **8 Feb 1808** | «**Antonius**» **+** «**Theresia**» | **cives** | *226* |

**`doc`** *for the entries and the frames.* **Four people, not a crowd:** ***Theresia*** *(thirteen times, 1792–1806),* ***Joannes*** *(five, 1794–1802),* ***Antonius*** *(four, 1799–1808), plus* ***Joannes Baptista with Vincenca*** *(1796) and* ***Anna***, *the Pazin noblewoman (1791).*

*⚠ **The years above are the second reading, and the first was wrong.** A fast pass over the date columns put four of these entries in 1802 and one in 1801; re-read against the folio numbers and the mid-page year dividers they are* **1801** *and* **1802** *respectively. [That also dissolves a «disorder» this page flagged yesterday](/corrections/) — M01070217 and M01070218 run 1801 then 1801–02, in folio order, with nothing out of sequence.*

*⚠ **The run has one real gap: 1803, 1804 and 1805.** Frames M01070219–M01070222 were read and carry none. Not explained here.* *⚠ The year headings on M01070217 (1802) and M01070218 (1801) sit in the opposite order to their folio numbers; [this book's disorder is documented](/gologorica-line/), but that pair is worth a second look.*

**⭐⭐ THE CONDITIO COLUMN IS WHERE THE FINDING ACTUALLY IS.** *This register grades every godparent:* **rustici · villici · agricolæ · supani · judices · cives · nobiles**. *The Defranceschi are entered* «**Cives**» *almost every time.* ***Townspeople of Gračišće.*** *Not* «Gollagoriciensis», *not* «ex Gologorica», *not* «Petinenses» — *the epithets this register hands out freely to everyone who comes from elsewhere, and [which it used for the Defranceschi godparents of the previous book five times over](/gologorica-line/).*

> ***In the earlier book they are labelled as coming from somewhere else. In this one they are not labelled at all, because they are of the place.***

**SO THE SENTENCE THIS ARCHIVE SHOULD HAVE WRITTEN IS NARROWER AND FAR MORE INTERESTING.** *[Withdrawn](/corrections/):* «the family was not established at Gračišće in the eighteenth century». ***What the two columns say together:***

> **The Defranceschi were at Gračišće as** *cives* **continuously from at least 1791 to 1808 — and in those eighteen years not one child of the name was baptised in the parish.**

*Present, repeatedly asked to the font, and not breeding there.* **That is not absence; it is a household of adults.** *Which is exactly what [the arrival the archive has been hunting](/errands/) would look like from the inside: people already living in the town before the register has any reason to write their name in the* Pater *column.*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THERE IS A THERESIA DEFRANCESCHI ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE, FROM THE OTHER PARISH.** *[The Gologorica baptism register names her four times, always the same way](/gologorica-line/):* «**Theresia Defranceschi nata Grach**» — *wife of* **Joannes Baptista Defranceschi of casa 31**, *the* «detti Leonardi» *house, entered* **«Cives»**. *She is the mother of* **Franciscus Antonius** *(bapt. 13 April 1785) and of* **Joannes Baptista** *(bapt. 13 August 1787) — [and that second son is this archive's candidate for the head of Gračišće house 5](/direct-line/), the direct line's second generation.*

> *A Defranceschi woman called Theresia, styled* cives, *standing godmother at Gračišće thirteen times between 1791 and 1808 — in exactly the years when the Theresia of Gologorica casa 31 was raising the boy who would head Gračišće house 5.*

**⚠ THIS IS `inf`, AND IT HAS A REAL OBJECTION THAT MUST BE STATED WITH IT.** *[This archive places her Grach at* **Krbune** *— «Cherbune», four kilometres the other way](/married-in/) — on the strength of the* «Archipresbiter Grach of Cherbune» *who stood godfather to her son in 1785.* ***The Grach are also the leading family of Gračišće*** — *[judges from 1667, a priest in the 1680s, a deacon in 1742](/gologorica-line/) — but one surname in two villages is not one family, and this archive has been burned by exactly that reasoning before.*

**WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is cheap:** *the Gračišće entries give her condition but never her maiden name. **One entry reading «Theresia Defranceschi nata Grach» in this book would close it** — the mother column of this very register writes maiden names as a matter of course («Maria olim Zelich»), so the habit exists. [Raised as its own row.](/worklist/)*

**⚠ AND THE CHEAP TEST HAS NOW BEEN RUN. IT FAILS — WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING AS A RESULT, NOT A SILENCE.** *[The plan was to look for one entry reading* «Theresia Defranceschi **nata Grach**»](/worklist/), *on the grounds that this register writes maiden names as routine.* ***It does — but only in the* Mater *column.*** *All twenty-one Patrini entries were re-read against the date column, and the godparent cell gives* **bare names**: «Theresia Defranceschi», «Antonius Defranceschi», *never a* nata *or an* olim. *The column does carry other qualifiers when it wants them —* «Lucia **vidua** Geor: Drusetich», «Maria **filia** Vili Milotich», «Maria **uxor** Martini Jvich» — ***so the omission is the scribe's habit for married women, not damage.***

> **This book will not settle it. The question moves to the Gračišće marriage registers — [MKV 1194 (1671–1835) or 1195 (1785–1850), both at the parish](/parish-books/) — or to the house-5 *Status Animarum*.**

*A negative test is still a test: it closes the cheapest route so the next session does not spend a day on it.*

**ALSO ON THESE LEAVES, AND NOT PREVIOUSLY HELD.** *At the foot of folio 185 (M01070225):* «**Revisus in Visitatione Decanali die 7ᵐᵃ 8bris 1807 — Petrus Anicich, Cæs. Reg. Parochus et Decanus**». **`doc`.** *[This archive already holds the same dean signing the* **Gologorica** *books on 25 June 1808, and Franovich signing them in 1804](/searched/), and reasoned from that that* «a visitation signed off the parish's registers together». ***Here he is doing it in the next parish, nine months earlier*** — *so the 1807–08 decanal round covered both, and a deanery protocol of that round would account for Gračišće and Gologorica in one document.*

*⚠ Not new: the* «Exhib. In Visitatione Spirituali Gallignanæ die 24 Aprilis 1788» *certificate at M01070195 is [already in the search record](/searched/) and is not claimed here.*

**TWO OF THEM ARE PEOPLE THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE, AND BOTH NOW HAVE A PAGE.**

**⭐⭐ [Anna de Franceschi, «Nobilis Pisinensis»](/person/anna-de-franceschi-nobilis-pisinensis-1791/)** — *13 February 1791.* ***A noble Defranceschi of Pazin.*** *[The archive holds exactly one other](/direct-line/):* «**Dominus Comes Damianus de Franceschis**», *whose son was baptised in this same parish on 25 March 1720 by the Provost and Vicar of Pedena Cathedral, and who* ***has never been identified in any source this archive holds***. *Anna stands with a* **de Tranquillis**, *for a child of* **Servulus Martinich** *and* **Francisca de Rapicio of Pazin**, *baptised by* **Nicolaus de Rapicio, parish priest of Pazin**. **A closed circle of Pazin families — Rapicio, Tranquilli, Martinich — with a Defranceschi inside it, seventy-one years after the count.** *⚠ No relationship to Damian is claimed; the two are recorded, not joined.*

**[Vincenca Defranceschi](/person/vincenca-defranceschi-1796/)** — *13 May 1796, beside* «Joan: Bapta Defranceschi», *both* «cives». ***A given name new to this surname in Istria in this archive.*** *⚠ Her Joannes Baptista cannot be [the direct line's man of that name](/direct-line/), who was nine years old in 1796.*

**⚠ AND A THIRD PERSON THIS PAGE BRIEFLY INVENTED.** *Yesterday's fast pass read the godmother of 16 October 1798 as* «**Catharina** Defranceschi» *and built on it — [a «second woman of the name crossing between the parishes»](/corrections/).* ***The word is* «Theresia»**, *read at twenty times magnification against the mother's cell on the same line.* **There is no Catharina at Gračišće, and the reasoning that stood on her is withdrawn.** *[What survives is the rule that was given for not minting her](/method/): the archive already carries a dozen Catharina Defranceschi, and a thirteenth would have been a guess wearing a permanent identifier. **The rule was right; the sighting it was applied to did not exist.***

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE OTHER HALF OF THE FLAGGED LIMIT IS NOW CLOSED TOO — WITH A CLEAN NIL THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIRST ONE.** *[The archive's warning named* **two** *places the surname could hide](/searched/): as a godparent, and* «as a **mother's maiden name**». *The Patrini column gave twenty-one. The* **Parentes** *block — Pater and Mater together — has now been read across the same thirty-seven frames, 1784 to May 1808, at four times the magnification of the original pass.*

> **Not one Defranceschi father. Not one Defranceschi mother. And not one mother entered «olim Defranceschi».**

**`doc`.** *That third clause is the new one, and it does real work.* *This register writes maiden names as a matter of course —* «Maria Salamon **olim** Milotich», «Lucia Milotich **olim** Bergliaffa», «Mathia **olim** Pedignan», «Joanna Bitina **olim** Berbetich» — *so a Defranceschi daughter who married a Gračišće man would appear in that column and be legible.* ***None does.***

**So across twenty-four years the family is at this font twenty-one times and in the parents' columns NOT ONCE, in any of the three ways the register could have put them there.** *⚠ This page first finished that sentence with* «*…whose children were baptised somewhere else, and the somewhere else is* **Gologorica**». ***That was written without checking, and [this archive's own search log refutes it](/corrections/).***

*⚠ The original* Pater *nil [was read «at contact-sheet magnification»](/searched/) and the archive said so. This pass read the same column at 1500px per page-half and agrees with it entirely. **A stated limit that turns out not to have mattered is still worth having stated.***

**⭐⭐⭐ BECAUSE THE SAME HOLE IS IN THE OTHER PARISH, AND THE ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY FOUND IT.** *[The Gologorica baptism book was read folio by folio on 1 October](/searched/), and it says, in as many words:*

> «**No Defranceschi child is baptised between 1788 and 1799 in this book**» *…* «**No Defranceschi baptism between 1799 and 1806**» *—* «*but the family is on almost every page as* **godparents**».

***Set the two registers side by side and they are the same sentence twice.***

| | Gračišće | Gologorica |
|---|---|---|
| *as* **parents** | **none**, 1784–1808 | **none**, 1788–1806 |
| *as* **godparents** | **21 times**, 1791–1808 | *«almost every page»*, 1790–1805 |
| *conditio* | «**Cives**» | «**Civ. gollog**» *(and* «Rust.» *for the Leonardi branch)* |

**So the finding is not that they baptised elsewhere. It is that for roughly fifteen years they did not baptise at all, in either parish, while standing at both fonts constantly.** *The archive's own two houses — [casa 31 and casa 36](/gologorica-line/) — had their children in* **1785–1789**, *and the next cohort arrives* **1803 and after**. **`doc`** *for both nils, which are now read from both books.*

*⚠ **What that means is not settled here, and three readings fit:** a generation finishing its childbearing while the next was not yet married; the men away; or a third parish nobody has opened. [Raised as a row](/worklist/) rather than resolved in a sentence.*

*⭐ One cross-link worth recording and not over-reading:* «**Joh: Bapt: Defranceschi**» *and* «**Antonius Defranceschi**» *stand godparent in* ***both*** *parishes in the same years — Gologorica 1792/1793/1795, Gračišće 1796/1799–1808.* **`inf`** *only: these are the two commonest male names in the family, and one surname in two villages is not one man.*

renumber.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ The renumbering is many-to-one — two old houses became one new house with two families, and the direction was backwards
renumber.lead: **The 1826 census column** «**Nrus. Domus**» *often carries* **two figures**. *[This archive has been building a concordance out of them for three days](/worklist/), and had concluded — reasoning that a census is bound in the order of its own numbering — that* ***the upper figure was the live one***. **Read at twenty times magnification, the upper figure is struck through.**
paras:
**THREE CELLS, AT TWENTY TIMES, WITH THE STRIKE VISIBLE.**

| page | upper | | lower | household |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **19** | **20** *struck* | ⟶ | **27** | *Domus Ecclesiæ* |
| **43** | **35** *struck* | ⟶ | **64** | *Maria, widow of the late Joannes* |
| **44** | **30** *struck* | ⟶ | **64** | *Josephus Ucovich* «Pintar» |

*Each cell is the same shape: a figure with a diagonal stroke through it, a ruled line, and a second figure beneath it left standing.* **`doc`**, *images M01069337, M01069361, M01069362.* ***The struck figure is the superseded number. The one below it is live.***

**⭐⭐⭐ AND PAGES 43 AND 44 ARE THE WHOLE ANSWER.** *They carry the* **same** *lower number —* **64** — *and their* «Nrus. Inquilinorum juxta eorum familias» *figures are* **1** *and* **2**. *Their struck upper numbers are different:* **35** *and* **30**.

> ***Two separately numbered old houses became two tenant families of one new house.***

**So the renumbering is not a shift. It is many-to-one.** *[Which is why three days of looking for a constant difference found none](/worklist/), and why the pairs appear to run in both directions at once —* «36 vetus · 14 novus» *from [the death register](/gologorica-line/) going one way, the census pairs going the other.* **A one-to-one mapping that does not exist cannot be found.**

***The concordance therefore has to be a lookup table keyed by HOUSEHOLD, not a formula and not a number-to-number list*** — *because one new number can answer to two old ones, and the only thing that tells them apart is the family living there.*

**⚠ AND IT CORRECTS THE REASONING, NOT JUST THE ANSWER.** *[The argument for the upper figure being live was that](/worklist/)* «*a census is bound in the order of its own numbering, so the ordering figure was live in 1826*». ***This book is bound in the order of neither.*** *Taking the pages in sequence: uppers run* **20, 29, 12, 22 … 35, 30**; *lowers run* **27, 30, 13, 14 … 64, 64**. *Neither climbs.* **The premise was false, so the conclusion it supported cannot stand even where it happened to be right.**

**What the book IS ordered by** *is [rank, at the front](/gologorica-line/), and then nothing this reading could identify.*

**⚠⚠ THIS SESSION'S OWN FIRST READINGS WERE WRONG TOO, AND THEY ARE WITHDRAWN HERE RATHER THAN PUBLISHED.** *Working at the magnification that fits four pages on a sheet, this walk read the upper figures of pages 43 and 44 as* «28» *and* «36». ***At twenty times they are* 35 *and* 30.** *[Two of today's three published errors came from exactly this — reading at the magnification that was convenient rather than the one the question needed](/corrections/), so the numbers above are the only ones this page will state, and the rest of the column is [left explicitly unharvested](/worklist/).*

**THE FRONT OF THE BOOK, AND THE HALF OF THIS THAT IS NOT NEW SAID FIRST.** *[This archive read every Defranceschi-headed page of this census on 7 October](/searched/) and listed eight of them —* **M01069320, 321, 323, 325, 326, 328, 329, 331** *— with a finding this walk did not improve on:* ***seven of the eight contain no household at all***, «*a name, sometimes a birth date, then nothing or somebody else's family*», *and only the Leonardus page is written out. They are* «**houses, named by whoever answered for them**».

**⭐ What this walk adds is two more pages and a total.** *Page* **14** *is* «**Jacobus Defranceschi**» *and page* **15** *is* «**Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi**» *(M01069332, M01069333) — neither on that list.* ***So the count is ten, not eight: pages 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15 of a fifteen-page* «civilitas» *section.***

> *The parish's census opens with its gentry, and* **two thirds of that section is one surname.**

*⚠ The* «**X**» *most of them carry where a house number should be is* ***not*** *interpreted here. [The established reading — a house named by whoever answered — already accounts for it](/searched/), and a second inference laid on top would add nothing but confidence.* *[Page 8 gives* «**Anna Mater nata Bembo**»*, the name this archive already holds from the 1731 Parenzo marriage.](/gologorica-line/)*

twelveyears.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ Twelve years with no child — the gap is in the family, not in the registers
twelveyears.lead: **[Yesterday this page established that the Defranceschi baptise no children at Gračišće or Gologorica for roughly fifteen years while standing at both fonts constantly](/gologorica-line/)** — *and left three readings open: a generational gap, the men away, or a third parish nobody had opened.* ***A third source, already in the house, now closes two of the three.***
paras:
**THE 1826 STATUS ANIMARUM OF GOLOGORICA, READ FOR ONE COLUMN.** *[Ten of its first fifteen pages are Defranceschi](/gologorica-line/); the* «Nativitatis» *block was read across every one of them:*

| born | who | page |
|---|---|---|
| **21 July 1764** | *Jacobus Defranceschi* | *5, 14* |
| **30 January 1766** | *Leonardus Defranceschi* | *10* |
| **17 April 1768** | *Petrus Defranceschi* | *7, 8* |
| **20 February 1772** | *Mathea, Leonardus's wife* | *10* |
| **5 July 1779** | *Anna Mater* «**nata Bembo**» | *8* |
| **20 July 1789** | *[Maria Rosalia](/person/maria-rosalia-defranceschi-1789/)* | *11* |
| ***— nothing —*** | | |
| **4 October 1803** | *[Hermenegildus](/person/hermenegildus-defranceschi-1803/)* | *8* |
| **14 April 1814** | *Antonius,* «filius Ubaldi et Apoloniæ» | *10* |
| **28 February 1815** | *Franciscus Xaverius* | *15* |

**`doc`** *— DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *frames M01069320, 321, 323, 325, 326, 328, 329, 331, 332, 333.*

**⭐⭐ SO THREE INDEPENDENT SOURCES NOW SAY THE SAME THING.**

| | says |
|---|---|
| *Gračišće baptisms, Pater* **and** *Mater* | **no Defranceschi parent, 1784–1808** |
| *Gologorica baptisms* | **no Defranceschi baptism, 1788–1806** |
| *the 1826 census* | **nobody born between 1789 and 1803** |

***None of them is the same record, and none of them was read for this question.*** *[The first two were read for a surname count](/searched/); this one was read for a house-number concordance.*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE CENSUS KILLS THE READING THIS PAGE THOUGHT MOST LIKELY TO SURVIVE.** *[The third of the three explanations was* «a third parish nobody has opened»](/worklist/) — *children born somewhere else and baptised there.*

> ***A child born elsewhere in 1792 would be thirty-four years old in 1826, and in this census. A child born in 1802 would be twenty-four.*** **Neither is there. Nobody of that age is there at all.**

*For that reading to hold, every child of those twelve years would have had to be born away* ***and never come home*** — *while their parents stood godparent in two parishes throughout.* **`inf`**, *but the inference is narrow and the census is the right book to make it from.*

**WHAT IS LEFT IS THE PLAINEST READING, AND IT HAS A DATE ON IT.** *The last Defranceschi child born at Gologorica before the silence is* **[Maria Antonia](/person/maria-antonia-defranceschi-1791/)**, *and [this archive already holds her death](/gologorica-line/):*

> «*Idem · [domus]* **36** *·* **16 Julij** *[1791] ·* ***MARIA ANTONIA DEFRANCESCHI*** *· mens[ium]* **6** *·* **Vermes**»

***Born 1791, dead at six months in July of the same year*** — *and then nothing until Hermenegildus in October 1803.* **Twelve years.** *[Her sister Maria Rosalia, born 20 July 1789, is the last one before her who lived](/person/maria-rosalia-defranceschi-1789/) — and the census has her struck through, because she died in 1826, the year it was taken.*

*⚠ **The limit of a census, stated.** A* Status Animarum *lists the living and resident. A child born in 1795 who died young, or a daughter who married into another parish before 1826, would not appear in it — so this* **corroborates** *the other two books rather than proving anything alone.* ***What it does do is remove the one explanation the other two could not touch***, *because an absent child who came back would be in it, and an absent child who never came back cannot explain parents who never left.*

*⚠ Two readings survive and are not chosen between here:* **a generation that simply did not reproduce** *— the 1764–1772 cohort finishing, the next not yet married — or* **something that stopped them**, *which would want the* [1817 famine](/gologorica-line/) *and [the 1789 smallpox](/gologorica-line/) kind of evidence for the right decade. [The row stays open on that.](/worklist/)*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY ON THIS PAGE, WRITTEN FIVE DAYS BEFORE THE QUESTION WAS ASKED.** *⚠ Nothing below is a discovery. [Every fact in it was published here on 6 October under the heading* «**House 36, in eighteen months**»](/gologorica-line/) — *and what had not been done was to notice what it answers.*

| when | who | age | cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| **16 July 1791** | *Maria Antonia Defranceschi* | ***six months*** | *vermes* |
| **26 April 1792** | *Sancta Defranceschi,* **cœlebs** | **58** | ***febris putrida*** |
| **21 May 1792** | *Catharina Defranceschi,* **nata Jablich ex Buccari** | **26** | *apoplexia* |

***All three at house 36, inside ten months.*** *And the sentence that matters was already written under them:* «**He did not remarry. He died a widower twenty-one years later, in January 1813, at sixty.**»

> ***The wife who would have borne the children of 1792 to 1802 died in May 1792, aged twenty-six, and her husband never took another.***

**That is reading 2, and the register supplies it** — *not* «something stopped them» *in the abstract, but* ***a putrid fever in the house in April and a young woman dead of apoplexy four weeks later***. **`doc`** *for all three deaths;* **`inf`** *that they are why the house fell silent, though a widower who does not remarry is about as short an inference as this archive makes.*

**⚠ IT ACCOUNTS FOR ONE HOUSE, NOT FOR THE FAMILY, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS.** *[There were two Defranceschi houses at Gologorica, told apart by their wives](/gologorica-line/):* **house 36**, *Joannes Baptista and* **Catharina née Jablich**, *and* **casa 31**, *another Joannes Baptista and* **Theresia née Grach**.

*House 36 is now explained.* ***Casa 31 is not.*** *Its last children are [Franciscus Antonius in 1785 and Joannes Baptista in 1787](/gologorica-line/), and* ***Theresia has no dates in this archive at all*** — *no birth, no death, no marriage.* **A second woman's record would finish this, and it is the same woman [the Gračišće godparent series needs](/worklist/).**

*⚠ One loose end recorded rather than smoothed: Catharina dies at* **house 36** *in 1792 and her husband dies at* **house 17** *in 1813. [This archive established today that the renumbering is many-to-one](/gologorica-line/), so two numbers for one household across twenty-one years is expected rather than alarming — but it is an assumption, and it is the archive's own link between the two rows.*

marriage1774.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ 9 June 1774 — the marriage register nobody had opened names the archpriest, the bride's father, and a weaver
marriage1774.lead: **This archive has known since 7 October that an «Archipresbiter Grach» of «Cherbune» stood godfather at a Gologorica font in 1785** — *the mother's own kin, a churchman, and [named by office and surname only](/married-in/). The plan for finding his forename was a diocesan clergy list at Poreč-Pula, which means a letter, which means [the standing hold](/errands/).* ***He is named in a book that has been in this house the whole time, eleven years earlier, in the act of marrying the couple himself.***
paras: **THE BOOK.** *The [frame map](/gologorica-line/#framemap) files* **M01068953–M01069007** *as Gologorica* «Rođeni · Umrli · Vjenčani», *1770–1781 and 1770–1789 and 1770–1789 — three registers bound as one, fifty-five frames, no signatura on the paper inventory.* **The archive's own audit rates it 3.6% read.** *The marriages run from about* **M01068998** *to* **M01069006**, *and nothing in [the search register](/searched/) had ever been in them.*
**THE ENTRY**, *right-hand page of M01068999, under the heading* «Die 9 Junij», *between a* «1774» *divider on the facing page and a* «1775» *divider four entries below:*

> «45ᵃ ***Joannes Baptista Defranceschi q.ᵐ Leonardi filius***, *professionis suæ* ***Textor***, *copulatus est cum Virgine* ***Theresia, filia Antonij Grah ex Parochia Cherbune***, *à Rev.ᵐᵒ D.ⁿᵒ* ***Archipresbytero et Parocho Cherbunensi Joanne Grah***, *in facie Ecclesiæ coram testibus ibidem notatis.*»

*(**doc** — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068999.)*
## ⭐ The archpriest has a name, and the errand can be struck

**«Archipresbytero et Parocho Cherbunensi JOANNE GRAH.»** *Archpriest* **and** *parish priest of Krbune, in the ablative of agent — he did not witness this marriage, he performed it.* ***He is the same man who stands at the font for Theresia's son eleven years later***, *and [the married-in page's line «no forename is given» is now wrong](/married-in/) and has been corrected.*

**What it costs to know this: nothing.** *[Worklist 168 set the order of work as Krbune's film, then Gračišće and Cerovlje, then a diocesan clergy list for the archpriest](/worklist/) — and flagged that he stands* **eighteen years before Krbune's surviving film begins**, *so the film could not hold him.* **That was right. The conclusion drawn from it — that a diocesan list was therefore the route — was not**, *because the parish he served kept sending its priest four kilometres to Gologorica, and* ***Gologorica's own books are on the family's hard drive.***
## ⭐⭐ «detti Leonardi» is a patronymic, and here it is in Latin

**The Gologorica death book's index files a girl of house 31 under** «Defranceschi Joanes Bapta ***detti Leonardi*** · N.º 12», *and [this page has been treating that as a byname](/gologorica-line/) — a clerk's way of telling two households apart.* ***The marriage says what it actually is.***
> «Joannes Baptista Defranceschi ***q.ᵐ Leonardi filius***» — *son of the late Leonardus.*

**And the archive holds a Leonardus Defranceschi of Gologorica who died in 1773** — *[the year before this marriage](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-1697/).* **«q.ᵐ» means he was already dead when his son married**, *which is exactly where that record puts him.* ⚠ *The identification is* **inf**, *not* **doc**: *the entry names a dead Leonardus and does not date his death, and more than one Leonardus lived in this parish.*

**⚠⚠ AND BY THE END OF THE SAME DAY THAT CAUTION HAD A NAME.** *[The obit calendar buries a* **Leonardo Defranceschi on 2 November 1751**](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-the-elder-gologorica/), *and on 13 November 1755 [a* **Matteo** «figlio **q.** Leonardo Defranceschi»](/person/matteo-defranceschi-d1755/) — *a second entry confirming that Leonardo was dead and had sons.* ***A man marrying in 1774 whose father died in 1751 is a man of twenty-three or more, so* «q.ᵐ Leonardi» *fits him exactly as well.*** **The archive now has two candidate fathers — one with a day and a year off a register index, one with a year off a family tree — and it is not choosing between them.**

**⭐ And nine months earlier, on the facing page, the OTHER one.** *The same scribe, the same volume, 15 September 1773 — a witness at the marriage of Josephus Udovicich:*

> «...et ***Joanne Baptista Defranceschi filio D.ni Josephi***, omnes Religionis Catholicæ»

***Son of Lord Josephus*** — *which is [the man whose death entry of 1813 calls him* «defuncti Josephi filius», *widower of Catharina née Jablich](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-1752/), born 1752 and so twenty-one that September.*

**So one book, in nine months, writes both Joannes Baptista Defranceschi of Gologorica, each with his father's name attached.** *This archive has been telling them apart [by their wives](/married-in/) and by their house numbers.* ***It can now tell them apart the way the parish did.***

| | the groom of 1774 | the witness of 1773 |
|---|---|---|
| **as written** | «q.ᵐ Leonardi filius» | «filio D.ni Josephi» |
| **house** | casa **31**, index N.º **12** | house **36**, later **17** |
| **wife** | **Theresia née Grach** of Krbune | **Catharina née Jablich** of Bakar |
| **trade given** | ***Textor*** | *none in this entry* |
## ⭐⭐ A weaver — and the word was checked against the hand that wrote it

**«professionis suæ TEXTOR».** *The column is a trade column and it is normally dull: the marriage above this one and the marriage below it both read* «professionis suæ ***Agricola***», *and so do most of the others on the opening.* ***The Defranceschi groom is the only man on the page who is not a farmer.***

**The reading that had to be excluded is «Tector», a plasterer or roofer — one letter apart.** *[The rule here is that a hand is only legible against itself](/method/), so the word was not stared at; it was set beside the same scribe writing* «textore» *in entry 62, nineteen days later, and beside his* «Agricola» *twice, all at one magnification. [The plate is below.](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774)* *His* «c» *is a plain open hook; the third letter of* «Textor» *carries a crossing stroke and a loop.* **(doc.)**

**⭐ Why a weaver is not a small detail in this archive.** *[The Carnian argument rests on the 1679 return of the headmen of Mione](/carnia/), which names* «Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo» *among men listed as* **weavers** *— and the whole case that the Gologorica family came from Carnia has run on names, dates and a village, with the trade sitting in the Carnian half of the story and nothing on the Istrian side to answer it.* ***Ninety-five years later, in Istria, a Defranceschi groom gives his trade as weaver in a parish of farmers.***

⚠ **This is not proof of the descent and is not offered as one.** *A trade is not a pedigree; Istria had weavers who never saw Carnia, and ninety-five years is three generations.* **What it is: the first time the Istrian records have said anything at all about what these men did**, *and what they said matches.* *(**doc** for the trade; the connection to Mione stays* **inf**.*)*
## What else the entry gives, and one thing it does not

- **Theresia is «Virgine»** — *a maiden, so this is her first marriage, and [her roster row, which carried no note and no dates at all, now carries a date](/person/theresia-defranceschi-nee-grach-gologorica/).*
- **Her father is ANTONIUS GRAH, of the parish of Krbune** — *new to this archive, and [added to the Grach page](/married-in/).*
- **The marriage was at Gologorica**, *the groom's parish, but celebrated by the* **bride's** *priest — who came the four kilometres to do it.*
- ⚠ **No witnesses are named.** *The entry closes* «coram testibus ibidem notatis» *— before the witnesses noted there — and then notes none, which is this scribe's habit in some entries and not in others; entry 62 on the same page names two.*
- ⚠ **The marginal numbers are not understood.** *This opening carries* **25 · 110 · 62 · 102 · 50 · 6 · 82 · 27 · 115 · 45 · 62 · 34 · 65** *in the margin, in no order and with repeats. They are* **not** *read as house numbers here and nothing is inferred from the 45. [Raised on the work list.](/worklist/)*

**⭐ And the register that was dismissed four hours ago as stopping too early.** *[Worklist 216 named the Gologorica marriages 1770–1789 and set them aside](/worklist/) —* «on the reel the family holds but **stop too early**» *— because the twelve-year gap needs marriages of 1795–1815 and this book ends in 1789.* ***That was true about the question being asked and false about the book***, *which was holding the answer to a different question the archive had already decided needed a letter to a diocesan archive.* **[A note has gone to the method page.](/method/)**

parochus1782.heading: ⭐⭐ The priest of this surname was in this parish from 1768 — and here he is writing his own name
parochus1782.lead: **[Reading on through the marriage register past the 1774 entry](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774) runs into the years when a Defranceschi was parish priest of this village** — *and because a marriage entry says* «per me», ***the officiant is also the scribe, so these pages are in his hand.***
paras: **What this archive already held about him, and it is not little.** *[His burial of 29 March 1798](/person/joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica/):* «admodum R.ᵈᵘˢ D.ⁿᵘˢ **MATH.
