DE FRANCESCHI, ex Parocho GALLEGNA[nensi]** · *annorum* **62** · *Paralisia*» — *formerly parish priest of Gračišće, dead at sixty-two.* *And [the* Sepeliens *column of the death register heading* **1786**](/gologorica-line/), «[Defran]**ceschi, P[aro]chus Loci**», *which showed he had held* **this** *cure too.* **The row already carries him as Joannes Mathias Franceschi.**

**So the forename is not a discovery here, and this page is not going to pretend it is.** ***What the marriage register adds is a document for it.*** *The 1798 burial gives only* «MATH.»; *the death column gives no forename at all.* *On* **12 January 1785** *he writes, in the first person, breaking the name across a line:*
> «*...ex hac Parochia ambo* **per me Parocum Joannē | Mathiam Franceschi** *in facie Ecclesiæ, præmissis denunciationibus...*»

⚠ **«Mathiam» is written out; «Joannē» is an abbreviation under a macron**, *and [the rule here is not to read anything off an abbreviation without a second construction](/method/).* ***This page went up saying no second construction had been found. It was on the next frame.***

> **29 February 1788** — «*habita est, nulloque legitimo impedimento detecto.* ***Ego JOANNES MATTHIAS de FRANCESCHI, Parocus hujus loci***, *Joannem viduum Bubich ex Parochia Cerougliensi...*»

**The whole name in one line, in his own hand, nothing abbreviated.** *And on the same frame, under* **1786**: «**Ego Joannes de Franceschi, Parochus hujus Loci**». ***So the forename is* `doc` *and no longer an expansion*** — *and the archive's row, written three days ago off a burial that gives only* «MATH.», *was right.*
## ⭐⭐ And he is four years earlier in this cure than the archive had him

| | |
|---|---|
| *what the archive held* | «[Defran]ceschi, P[aro]chus Loci» at the head of **1786** in the death register |
| *the marriage register* | «**per me Parochum Franceschi** in facie Ecclesiæ» — **12 November 1782** |

**And a third self-naming, 22 November 1785, with the particle this time:** «*nulloque legitimo impedimento detecto.* **Ego idem Parochus de Franceschi hujus loci**, *Stanislaum filium defuncti Josephi Rabbar...*» — ***I, the same parish priest de Franceschi of this place.***

**⭐ He writes his own surname both ways in one book**, «Franceschi» *in 1782 and 1785 and* «de Franceschi» *in November 1785.* *[This archive has watched the particle come and go with the hand before — at Svetvinčenat the spelling changed when the archpriest changed](/searched/).* ***Here it changes inside one man's own hand***, *which is worth knowing before anybody treats* «Franceschi» *and* «Defranceschi» *as two families.*

**⚠ ⚠ THIS PARAGRAPH SAID «CONTINUOUSLY» AND IT IS WITHDRAWN** — *within the hour, by two more frames of the same book.* *[It argued that because he is parish priest from November 1782 to November 1785, Gallignana must fall before 1782 or after 1785.](/corrections/)* **M01069004 has, three weeks after one of those entries:** «*1 February 1785 ...* **per Parochum Josephum Deprato** *in facie Ecclesiæ*». ***A DEPRATO, styled* «Parochum», *inside the span.*** *[This page's own standing warning is that at Gologorica a* «De—» *surname may be Defranceschi, Deprato or Defranich](/gologorica-line/), and [the death register shows these two alternating in one column](/gologorica-line/) — ***the inference was made anyway, from the Defranceschi entries alone, because those were the ones being looked for.*** **[Method row.](/method/)** *What stands: he is parish priest* **on the three dates where he signs**. *What is gone: the word* «continuously», *and the bracket built on it.* **«One man or two» is exactly where it was** — *the Gračišće registers, [on the reel that is the first errand](/errands/).*

**And between the two of them a curate works.** *«per me* **Joannem Florcich**, *Capellanus,* **cum licentia Parochi**» *(27 January 1784) and* «cum facultate Parochi hujus loci» *(24 November 1783) — so the parish had a chaplain under the Defranceschi priest, and [the archive's table of hands](/gologorica-line/) gains two names instead of one.*
## ⭐⭐ The marginal numbers are house numbers — and the book says so itself

**[A work-list row was opened for these this morning](/worklist/)** *because the 1774 opening carries* **25 · 110 · 62 · 102 · 50 · 6 · 82 · 27 · 115 · 45 · 62 · 34 · 65** *in the margin, out of order and with repeats, and the row said plainly that* **115 is too large for a house** *and that nothing should be inferred until it was settled.* ***Reading forty frames further on settles it, and the objection was wrong.***
**The left page of the 1782 opening carries the column heading, written once:** «**Num. Domus**».

**And the entries of this hand write the number twice — in the margin, and again inside the prose as the groom's own house:**

| margin | in the entry | date |
|---|---|---|
| **13** | «annorum 21 **Sub N.º 13**» | 24 Nov 1783 |
| **108** | «annorum 24 **sub N.º 108**» | 27 Jan 1784 |
| **70** | «annorum 47 **sub N.º 70**» | 9 Feb 1784 |
| **41** | «annorum 32 **sul N.º 41**» | 12 Jan 1785 |
| **9** | «annorum 65 **sub N.º 9**» | 30 Jan 1785 |
| **12** | «**N.º 12** copulatus est» | 30 Jan 1785 |

**⭐ Six matches, and the one that answers the objection is 108.** ***Houses in this parish are numbered past a hundred***, *and the entries confirm it from the other side — a bride* «ex Salignana **sub N.º 109**». *So* **115 and 110 and 102 on the 1774 opening are ordinary house numbers**, *not evidence that the column counts something else.*

⚠ **The heading and all six matches are in the later hand.** *The entries of the 1770s have the same column in the same place with no heading above it and no in-text number to check against, so strictly this is proved for 1782 onward and* **carried back by the position of the column alone**. *It is enough to stop treating the figures as a mystery; it is not enough to attach* **house 45** *to [the Defranceschi groom of 1774](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774), and that is not done here — [casa 31 and index N.º 12 were joined only because two independent books said so](/gologorica-line/).*

⚠ **One observation against reading the numbering as continuous:** *on 30 January 1785 the groom at* «**N.º 12**» *is a* **Bubich**. *[The death book's index files the casa 31 Defranceschi household under* «detti Leonardi · **N.º 12**»](/person/mariana-defranceschi-d1786/) — *so the index's* **N.º 12** *and the marriage book's* **N.º 12** *are not the same number.* ***Two numbering systems with the same figures in them is precisely how a household gets attached to the wrong door***, *and it is recorded here before anybody does it.*
## And one of ours standing in the church of Sancta Anastasia
> **9 February 1784** — «...*in Ecclesia* **Sanctæ Anastasiæ** *coram testibus Supano Martino Zabran, et* **Domino Jacobo de Franceschi**, *ambo ex hac Parochia*»

**[The archive holds one Jacobus de Franceschi at Gologorica](/person/jacobus-de-franceschi-1761/)** — *born* **21 July 1762** *by the 1826 census, dead* **8 December 1850** *at eighty-eight, of house 7, entered* «civis» *where the men around him are* «agla». **On this date he would be twenty-one.** *(**doc** for the witnessing; **inf** that he is that man.)*

⚠ **A twenty-one-year-old styled «Dominus» is the thing to watch here.** *It is not impossible in the* civilitas *branch, which the registers do style so — but an older Jacobus otherwise unrecorded would fit the title better, and this archive has only the one.* **Nothing is merged and no date is moved.** *What is recorded is that [his row's earliest dated appearance moves from 1826 to 1784](/person/jacobus-de-franceschi-1761/), forty-two years, if the identification holds.*
## ⭐ Later the same day — he is earlier still, and the handover has a bracket

**Reading back one frame (M01069002, 1779–1782) moves the first sighting from 12 November to 11 July 1782:** «*Matheus viduus filius defuncti Stanislai Gasparich dicti Silai ... copulatus est cum Vidua Hellena defuncti Joannis Ancich* **per me Parochum Franceschi** *in facie Ecclesiæ*».

**And his predecessor is on the same frame, still in office in the autumn of 1780:** «per me **Marcum Bancich Parochum huius Loci**» — *the same man who married [the Defranceschi groom of 1774](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774) six years earlier.*

| | |
|---|---|
| *autumn **1780*** | **Marcus Bancich**, *Parochus huius Loci* |
| *19 Nov **1781*** | **Antonius Carnihar**, *Presbyter, «de licentia Parochi»* — **does not name the incumbent** |
| *11 July **1782*** | **Franceschi**, *Parochus* |

***So the cure passes from Bancich to a Defranceschi between late 1780 and July 1782***, ⚠ *with the caveat the correction above imposes: in this parish* «Parochus» *is a style two* «De—» *men wear within weeks of each other, and a handover is not a tenancy.*
## And on 9 November 1782, two of the name standing as witnesses

> «*Josephus filius Supani Antonij Flegar* **ex Novaco**, *professione rusticus, ætatis* **20** *annorum,* **ex Domo N.º 19**, *copulatus est cum* **Mariana filia Leonardi Deprato**, *annorum* **22** *... per* **Parochum Franceschi** *in facie Ecclesiæ, coram testibus nimirum* ***Antonio Defranceschi***, *et Dominico Bachialab ex Novaco, et* ***Margare[t]ha de Franceschi*** *ex hac Parochia.*»

**⚠ Women witness routinely in this book** — *[the 1774 entries name* «Ellena Flegar filia defuncti Thomæ» *and* «Maria filia Supani Mathæi Flegar» *among the* testes *— so nothing is made of her sex here. What is worth something is her row.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **[Antonius Defranceschi](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1742/)**, *1742–1802, house 29* | *everything this archive had of him was [his death entry of 1802](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1742/).* ***Twenty years earlier, and he is forty.*** |
| **[Margarita Defranceschi](/person/margarita-defranceschi-1747/)**, *1747–1783* | *her row was a name and two years off a family tree and* ***no document at all***. *She is thirty-five here and dead fourteen months later.* |

⚠ *Both identifications are* **inf** *— the entry gives* «ex hac Parochia» *and no ages or houses. They are the only two of those names this archive places at Gologorica in that decade, and nothing else is claimed.*

**⚠⚠ And the bride is the thing to carry away from this entry.** «**Mariana filia LEONARDI DEPRATO**», *aged twenty-two, so born about 1760.* ***There was a Leonardus DEPRATO raising children in this village at exactly the time this archive has a Leonardus DEFRANCESCHI and a branch called* «detti Leonardi».** *It does not touch [the 1774 groom](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774), whose own surname is written out in full — but it does mean that* **«a Leonardus of Gologorica» is not one man and may not even be one family**, *and the* «De—» *warning now reaches the forenames as well as the surnames.*
# ⭐⭐⭐ And the last frame of the item puts him here in 1768, as a CURATE

**The marriage item's final frame, M01069006, is out of sequence** — *the marriages proper begin at M01068997 under the heading* «**Notatio Personarum Matrimonio junctarum a 1ᵐᵃ Julij 1770**» *and run forward frame by frame to 1788; this last frame carries* **1768 and 1769**, *in the older, fuller narrative formula.* ***Its first entry is his.***

> «*Præmissis Denunciationibus tribus continuis diebus festivis … nulloque legitimo impedimento detecto.* ***Ego JOANNES MATTHIAS DE FRANCESCHI, COOPERATOR hujus loci***, *viduum* **Michaelem Gadda q.ᵐ Andrea ex CHERBUNE**, *sub N.º —, rusticum, ætatis suæ* **40** *annorum, et* **Catharinam, celibem filiam Joannis Gadda dicti Picin**, *rusticam, ætatis suæ* **26** *annor., ex hac Parochia…*»

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069006, the last frame of the item before KRAJ.)*

**⭐ A FIFTH attestation of the full name, and the earliest.** *After* «per me Parocum Joannē Mathiam Franceschi» *(1785),* «Ego Joannes de Franceschi» *(1786),* «Ego Joannes Matthias de Franceschi» *(1788) and* «Rev.ᵈᵒ Sig.ʳ Gio: Mattia Defranceschi» *(the obit calendar).* ***Five books, one man, one name.***
**⭐⭐ And it is not the same office.** «**COOPERATOR**» *— curate, the assistant, not the incumbent.* ***So his career in this parish now has a shape instead of a single point:***

| | |
|---|---|
| **Nov 1768** | «**Cooperator** hujus loci» |
| *by* **11 July 1782** | «**Parochum** Franceschi» |
| **29 Feb 1788** | «**Parocus** hujus loci» |
| **29 March 1797/8** | *buried,* «**ex Parocho Gallegnanensi**», *aged 66 or 62* |

**⚠ And it narrows the «one man or two» question again, in the useful direction.** *[If he is curate at Gologorica in 1768–69 and its parish priest from 1782 to 1788](/person/joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica/), **the Gallignana cure has to fall between them — roughly 1769×1782.** *That is a real window where there was none.* ⚠ *It is still not proof of one man, and [the correction of this afternoon stands](/corrections/): in this village* «Parochus» *was a style two* «De—» *men wore within three weeks of each other.*

**⭐ And a Krbune man marrying in.** *The groom is* «**Michael Gadda, son of the late Andreas, ex Cherbune**», *a widower of forty.* ***Not a Grah*** — *but [more of the Krbune traffic this archive keeps finding in Gologorica's own books](/gologorica-line/#jablichnil), and a reminder that the two parishes exchanged people constantly.*

jablichnil.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ The marriage this walk went looking for is not in this book — and the archive has been holding it on another page for a week
jablichnil.lead: **The Gologorica marriage register was opened to find one thing:** *[the marriage of* **Catharina née Jablich of Buccari** *to the Joannes Baptista of house 36](/person/catharina-defranceschi-jablich-gologorica/).* ***It is not there.*** *And the nil is worth more than the search was.*
paras: **THE NIL, IN ITS EXACT TERMS**, *because [a nil that does not name what was tried is an assertion about a list nobody kept](/method/):*

| frame | years | how it was read |
|---|---|---|
| **M01068999** | Sept 1773 – Sept 1775 | *entry by entry, both halves* |
| **M01069002** | 1779 – Nov 1782 | *officiant line of every entry; the four carrying the surname read in full* |
| **M01069003** | Nov 1782 – Jan 1785 | *entry by entry, both halves* |
| **M01069004** | Feb 1785 – 1786 | *scanned for the surname; officiant lines read* |
| **M01069005** | 1786 – Feb 1788 | *officiant line of every entry* |

***No Defranceschi bride or groom on any of them except the 1774 entry.*** ⚠ *Only two of the five were read entry by entry; the others were scanned for a long and distinctive surname, which is reliable but is not a walk, and [is logged as `walked: false`](/searched/).*

**⚠ And the unread frames cannot hold her.** *M01068996–98 and M01069000–01 run 1770–1779 and M01069006 runs 1788–89.* ***She was born about 1766*** *— twenty-six when she died on 21 May 1792 — so she is a child in the first group, and [her first known baby died at eleven days in March 1786](/person/catharina-defranceschi-d1786/), so she is long married before the last.* **The window is 1779–1786 and it has been looked at.**
## ⭐⭐ So where would she marry? In her own parish — and the archive got there a week ago by another road

**[Worklist 166 set the job out on 30 September](/worklist/)**, *in these words:* «**Look for Jablich, not only for the surname.** *A marriage of a Jablich daughter to a Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, before 1786, is a specific entry in a specific decade — far more findable than a surname sweep.*»

**It also set, as step one,** «*establish whether the Bakar registers are filmed at all, and by whom*». ***They are, and this archive holds the waypoints.*** *[The Kvarner parish-book table](/parish-books/) lists seven Bakar films, among them:*
> **Marriages (Vjenčani) 1739–1857** · FamilySearch waypoint **`9R28-82Z`**
## ⭐⭐⭐ And step two is already done, on a page about a different question
**[The Bakar household, published from the FamilySearch indexes](/crikvenica-house/)**, *carries this sentence:*

> «*His son* «**Joanem Bap. Defranceschi**» *marries* «**Catharinam Akacich**»*, with an Antonius Akacich named beside her.* ***A separate entry has a* «Joannem Defranceschi» *marrying* «Catharinam SABLICH»** *— either the same man remarried, or a brother.*»

**«Catharinam Sablich». «Catharina née Jablich ex Buccari».** ***One letter, and the archive has been reading them as two unrelated problems in two different stories*** — *the Bakar one as a question about which Bakar man married twice, the Gologorica one as a wife with no marriage.*

**⭐ And the age arithmetic puts the two Bakar Catharinas apart, which is what lets this stand up at all.** *[The Bakar household's own Catharina was born 1734 and died 7 April 1819 at eighty-five](/crikvenica-house/), and her children are baptised there in* **1773** *and* **1776**. ***Our Catharina was seven years old in 1773.*** *She cannot be the Akačić wife —* **so the Sablich marriage is the other one, and it is unclaimed.**
## ⚠ What is NOT claimed

- **The index says «Joannem», not «Joannes Baptista».** *The Akačić entry two lines above it does say* «Joanem Bap.», *so the indexer distinguishes them, and that cuts against the join as much as the spelling cuts for it.*
- **No date has been quoted for the Sablich entry anywhere in this archive.** *Without one it cannot be placed in the 1779–1786 window at all.*
- **It is an index entry.** ***No register has been read.*** *[The spellings are the indexer's](/crikvenica-house/).*
- **«Sablich» and «Jablich» are a one-letter difference in two different hands read by two different people**, *and [this archive has spent the day being wrong about single letters](/corrections/).*

**⭐ THE TEST, AND IT IS CHEAP AND IT IS NOT A LETTER.** *The volume is filmed and the archive holds its waypoint.* ***Open* `9R28-82Z` *— Bakar marriages 1739–1857 — find the Sablich entry, read the page, and take the date, the groom's patronymic and the bride's father.*** *If the groom is* «Joannes Baptista filius...» *and the date falls in the early 1780s, [a wife this archive has had for a week without a wedding](/person/catharina-defranceschi-jablich-gologorica/) has one — and [the «Bakar to Gologorica» arrow David drew on his own map by hand](/mymap/) has a document under it.*

bakar1783.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ 10 November 1783, at Bakar, in her father's house — the wedding this archive has been missing for a week
bakar1783.lead: **[An hour ago this page said the nil pointed at the Bakar register and named the test](/gologorica-line/#jablichnil)** — *open the film, find the entry, take the date, the groom's patronymic and the bride's father.* ***The film was opened and it gives all three.***
paras:
> «**Die 10 9bris** *pro domo* **D. Sebastiani Sablich**, *Nuptiis in facie Ecclesiæ contractis inter* ***D.ⁿᵘᵐ Joannem Bap.[tistam] [De]franceschi ex GOLLOGORIZZA*** *et* ***D. Catharinam Sablich***, *tradidit D. Parochus Buccarensis* **Jacobus Polian**, *præsentibus Senatore D.* **Josepho Walis** *et D.* **Josepho Smich**»

*(**doc** — FamilySearch,* «Croatia, Delnice Deanery Catholic Church Books, 1571–1926»: ***Bakar, Religious Marriage Registers 1739–1808, film 005494714, item 1, image 172 of 226, page 161***. *Index entry* `1:1:6Z2F-LSSQ`; *image* `3:1:3QSQ-G99X-RX3F`. *Read 9 October 2026.)*
## What it settles

**⭐ «EX GOLLOGORIZZA» IS IN THE ENTRY.** *This is not a join made by matching a name against a name. The Bakar scribe wrote the groom's village into his own register*, *and it is the same spelling [the Svetvinčenat archpriest used for an Antonio of this family two years later](/person/antonio-de-franceschi-q-leonardo-of-gologorica-m-1785-svetvincenat/).*

**⭐ And it answers the objection this page raised against itself an hour ago.** *The published caution was:* «*the index says* **«Joannem»**, *not* **«Joannes Baptista»** *— the entry two lines above it does say* «Joanem Bap.», *so the indexer distinguishes them, and that cuts against the join.*» ***The register says* «Joannem Bap.». *The indexer dropped it.*** *The objection was right to make and it is now spent.*

**⭐ The nil and the entry fit to the month.** *[M01069003 was read entry by entry and covers November 1782 to January 1785](/gologorica-line/#jablichnil).* ***10 November 1783 falls inside it, and there is no Defranceschi marriage on it.*** *He was not at Gologorica that day because he was at Bakar.*

**⭐ Her father is named, and the wedding was in his house.** «*pro domo* **D. Sebastiani Sablich**». ***A generation this archive did not have***, *and a detail that places the marriage socially: it was held at the bride's family house, not simply in the parish church.*

**⭐ And it is a marriage into Bakar's governing class.** *Both parties are* «Dominus» / «Domina», *and one of the witnesses is a* **Senator of Bakar**, *D. Josephus Walis.* *[The Gologorica Defranceschi are entered* «Cives Gollogoricenses» *at the font three years later](/person/catharina-defranceschi-jablich-gologorica/);* **this is the marriage that connects the two.**
**⭐ And David drew the line before the archive found it.** *[His own map carries a hand-drawn movement](/mymap/) labelled* «**Bakar to Gologorica**». ***It now has a document under it, and a date.***
## ✔ And it raises her surname — which was settled the same evening, from inside the entry

| | spells her | |
|---|---|---|
| **Gologorica**, baptisms, 3 Oct 1786 | «Cath. ejus uxor nata **JABLICH** ex Buccari» | *one Istrian scribe, 130 km from her home* |
| **Bakar**, marriages, 10 Nov 1783 | «D. Catharinam **SABLICH**», «D. Sebastiani **SABLICH**» | ***her own parish, her own father, twice in one entry*** |

***The home parish ought to win*** — *but [a long* **ſ** *and a* **J** *are one of the classic confusions in this hand](/method/), and this archive had spent the day being wrong about single letters in both directions. **So the page first said neither spelling was declared correct, and named the test: find the Bakar scribe writing an unambiguous S and an unambiguous J on the same leaf.**
**✔ THE IMAGE WAS DOWNLOADED AND THE TEST RUN. IT DID NOT NEED THE REST OF THE LEAF.**
> *Line 1* «*in domo D.* **Sabastiani Sablich**» · *line 3* «*et D.* **Catharinam Sablich**» · *line 4* «*Parochus Buccarensis* **Jacobus** Polian» · *line 5* «*et D.* **Josepho** Smich»

**The scribe's J — in «Jacobus» and «Josepho», three lines below — rises high and drops a long descender below the baseline, hooking left.** *The initial of* «Sablich» *rises and returns to the baseline and* ***has no descender at all***.

**✔✔ And the clincher is inside the name itself.** *The bride's father is* «**Sabastiani Sablich**», *and the two words begin with the* ***identical letterform***. ***Whatever opens* «Sabastiani» *can only be an S.*** **So it is SABLICH**, *settled from the entry's own letters rather than by staring — [which is the rule this archive works by](/method/). [Plate below.](/gologorica-line/#bakar1783)*

⚠ **What that does NOT make the Gologorica entry.** *[That register writes her* «nata **JABLICH** ex Buccari»](/person/catharina-defranceschi-jablich-gologorica/) *and may well have written exactly that.* ***The discrepancy is between two scribes a hundred and thirty kilometres apart, not between two readings of one page*** — *an Istrian priest setting down a Kvarner name he had heard spoken.* **The family's name is Sablich; what Gologorica called her is Jablich; both are now facts rather than alternatives.** ⚠ *[Her person id stays frozen at the Jablich form — a moved id is a dead URL.](/method/)*

**The test, and it is the same rule as always:** *[find the Bakar scribe writing an unambiguous* **S** *and an unambiguous* **J** *elsewhere on page 161 and compare at one magnification](/method/).* *Until then she is* **Catharina née Sablich / Jablich**, *and [the person id stays frozen](/method/) because a moved id is a dead URL.*
## ⚠ And two sentences on the Bakar page are now wrong

**[The Bakar household](/crikvenica-house/)** *reads this entry as a local puzzle:* «*A separate entry has a* «Joannem Defranceschi» *marrying* «Catharinam Sablich» — ***either the same man remarried, or a brother***.»

***He is neither.*** *He is not a Bakar Defranceschi at all — the register calls him* «**ex Gollogorizza**». **[Corrected.](/corrections/)** *The Bakar household loses a supposed second marriage and keeps its own* **Akačić** *one; [the age arithmetic that first separated the two Catharinas](/gologorica-line/#jablichnil) was pointing at this all along.*

calendarindex.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ A perpetual calendar of this parish's dead — never opened, and it gave up eleven Defranceschi in a day
calendarindex.lead: **[Worklist 218 listed the Gologorica deaths of 1646–1806 as the last and least of four items](/worklist/)** — *twenty-five frames, never opened, worth a look for a Grah.* ***What is actually in it is a finding aid this archive did not know existed, and it is pointed straight at the oldest generation the roster has.***
paras: **IT IS NOT A REGISTER YOU READ FORWARD. It is a calendar.** *Each opening carries two months; down the left of each page run the* **days of the month**; *against each day are the people who died on that day,* ***in any year***, *and the year stands in a ruled column at the right.*

> **30.** · **Pietro Defranceschi** — *170—*
>    Luca Zabran — *1750*
>    Bortolo Dobradon — *1752*
>    Giuseppe figlio di q. Matteo Flegar Lucotich N.º 109 — *1782*
>    [—] Zabran Tulla N.º 86, d'anni 50 — *1788*

*(30 September, in a single column — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069217.)*

**It is an obit calendar**, *the book a priest reads from to know whose anniversary falls today and whose mass to say.* ***Which is why it is the one place in this parish where a death of 1701 and a death of 1788 sit on the same line of ruling*** — *and why it is worth more to this archive than the register it indexes.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **where** | DAPA **ZM34K-214**, inside the item [the frame map files as](/gologorica-line/#framemap) «Gologorica · Umrli · 1646–1806», **M01069199–M01069223** |
| **verified on** | **M01069204** *(Jan–Feb)* · **M01069212** *(Jun–Jul)* · **M01069214** *(Jul–Aug)* · **M01069217** *(Sep–Oct)* · **M01069218** *(Oct)* |
| **so it runs** | *the full twelve months, within roughly* **M01069202–M01069221** |
| **language** | **Italian**, not Latin — «figlia di q.», «moglie di», «d'anni» |
| **it does not stop in 1806** | *entries on the same pages carry* **1817, 1819, 1857, 1887** — ***it was kept up for at least eighty years after the register it belongs to closed*** |
## ⭐⭐ Why this matters more than a Grah search
**The archive's oldest Gologorica people are tree people.** *Six of them carry a death year, the place* «Gologorica, Istra», *the source* `myheritage`, ***and a note of nothing at all***:

| | died | behind it |
|---|---|---|
| **[Pietro Defranceschi](/person/pietro-defranceschi-d1701/)** | **1701** | *a family tree* |
| **[Gian Battista Defranceschi](/person/gian-giovanni-ivan-battista-defranceschi-1673/)** | **1743** | *a family tree* |
| **[Leonardus Defranceschi](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-1697/)** | **1773** | *a family tree* |
| **[Gisanna Defranceschi](/person/gisanna-defranceschi-1684/)** | **1774** | *a family tree* |
| **[Pietro Defranceschi](/person/pietro-defranceschi-1695/)** | **1781** | *a family tree* |
| **[Josephus Defranceschi](/person/josephus-defranceschi-1722/)** | **1782** | *a family tree* |

***All six die before 1784, which is where [the death register this archive HAS walked](/searched/) begins.*** **That is why none of them has ever been documented: the book that would do it is the one nobody opened.** *And [Margarita, dead 1783](/person/margarita-defranceschi-1747/), is a seventh — she got her first document today, but it was a marriage she witnessed, not her death.*

**⭐⭐ And the one that matters most is Leonardus.** *[This morning's marriage entry calls the groom](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774)* «**Joannes Baptista Defranceschi q.ᵐ Leonardi filius**» — *son of the late Leonardus — and the archive's identification of that father with the Leonardus who died in* **1773** *rests on* ***the tree's year and nothing else***, *and was published as* **inf** *for exactly that reason.* **A death entry for him in this calendar would make it doc.**
## ⚠ The one reading taken so far, and what is wrong with it

«**Pietro Defranceschi**» *under* **30 September** *is the first Defranceschi found in this index, and [the archive holds a Pietro whose only property is the year 1701](/person/pietro-defranceschi-d1701/).* **So the day is new and the decade agrees.**

⚠ **But the year digit is not legible and is NOT being read off the tree.** *At eight times, the figure is* «**170**» *followed by a faint upright with a dot — beside the same scribe's unmistakable* **1750**, **1752**, **1782** *and* **1788** *in the four lines below it.* ***The decade 1700–1709 is certain; the final digit is not.*** *[The tree says 1701 and that is consistent with it, which is not the same as confirmed by it](/method/) — and this archive spent today being wrong about single characters in both directions.*
**So: a Pietro Defranceschi died at Gologorica on 30 September in the first decade of the eighteenth century.** *That is what the book says and all it says.*

**⭐ What it costs to do properly:** *nineteen openings, read down two columns each, for one surname —* ***and it would hand this archive the death days of a generation it has never documented at all.*** **[Specified on the work list.](/worklist/)**
# ⭐⭐⭐ And then the sweep reached March

> **29.** · Gregorio Zabran — *1752* · Matteo Udovich Juricich — *1758* · ***Rev.ᵈᵒ Sig.ʳ Gio: Mattia Defranceschi, Paroco del luogo, d'anni 66*** — ***1797***

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069207, the obit calendar under 29 March.)*

**[This archive has held his burial since 6 October](/person/joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica/)**, *from the other death book:* «Idem · [domus] **63** · **29 Martij** [1798] · admodum R.ᵈᵘˢ D.ⁿᵘˢ **MATH. DE FRANCESCHI, ex Parocho GALLEGNA[nensi]** · annorum **62** · *Paralisia*». **The day is the same. Three other things are not.**

**⭐ 1. It is a FOURTH attestation of the forename, and the first in Italian.** «**Gio: Mattia**». *[Today the register gave](/gologorica-line/#parochus1782)* «Joannē Mathiam» *(1785),* «Ego Joannes de Franceschi» *(1786) and* «Ego Joannes Matthias de Franceschi» *(1788).* ***Four books, one man, one name — and [the roster row that guessed it from* «MATH.» *alone was right](/person/joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica/).***

**⭐⭐ 2. It calls him PAROCO DEL LUOGO — parish priest of THIS place.** *The 1798 register styles him* «**ex** Parocho **Gallegnanensi**», *of Gračišće.* ***So one book buries him as Gologorica's priest and the other as Gračišće's former one, on the same day.*** **[That is the strongest thing yet said about the open «one man or two» question](/person/joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica/)** — *not proof, because a calendar kept by his successor may simply be recording the man they knew, but two parishes in two entries for one burial is what you would expect of a man who had held both.* ⚠ *[And today's correction stands: in this village* «Parochus» *is a style two* «De—» *men wore within weeks of each other.](/corrections/)*
**⚠⚠ 3. THE YEAR AND THE AGE DISAGREE, AND THIS ARCHIVE IS NOT CHOOSING.**

| | the obit calendar | the death register |
|---|---|---|
| **day** | **29 March** | **29 March** |
| **year** | **1797**, *written against the name in the ruled column* | **[1798]**, ***supplied in brackets from the page heading — the entry itself carries only* «29 Martij»** |
| **age** | *d'anni* **66** | *annorum* **62** |
| **so born** | *about* **1731** | *about* **1736** |
| **style** | «Paroco del luogo» | «ex Parocho Gallegnanensi» |
| **cause / house** | *none given* | *Paralisia, house* **63** |

***The calendar's year is explicit where the register's is editorial*** — *which is a reason to take it seriously and not a reason to flip the row.* **A perpetual calendar is written up after the fact, sometimes long after, and a year copied into it can slip by one as easily as a page heading can be misapplied.** ⚠ *Both figures are recorded on his row and [neither date is changed](/method/); what has changed is that the archive now knows the 1798 was never written on the entry.*

**⚠ And the age is the harder of the two**, *because* **both** *are explicit:* «d'anni 66» *against* «annorum 62». ***Four years is not a slip of the pen in the way a year-digit is***, *and it moves his birth across the span 1731–1736. Nothing in this archive dates him independently.*

**And the sweep that found him is six openings of nineteen.** *[M01069203, 204, 205, 207, 212, 214, 217, 218 — January to October, in parts.](/searched/)* ⚠ *One thing checked and* ***not*** *claimed on the way: a* «Moglie di q. Giovanni—» *under 20 February that resolved at magnification into* **Zadetich**, *not Defranceschi.* **[Still nil on the Grah, across every opening read.](/worklist/)**
# ⭐⭐ And November gave a father and a son the archive did not have

> **2.** · ***Leonardo Defranceschi*** — ***1751***

> **13.** · Pietro Sepcich — *1647* · ***Matteo figlio q. Leonardo Defranceschi*** — ***1755***

*(M01069219.)*

**[«Leonardus Defranceschi the elder» has sat in this roster with no dates, no source and no note of any kind](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-the-elder-gologorica/)** — *a placeholder minted to hold a Leonardus who was not the one the family tree dates 1697–1773.* ***He now has a death day.*** *And eleven days later in the calendar, four years later in time,* «**Matteo figlio q. Leonardo Defranceschi**» — ***[a son, new to this archive](/person/matteo-defranceschi-d1755/), whose own* «q.» *confirms from a second entry that the father was already dead.***
**⚠⚠ AND IT WEAKENS THIS MORNING'S WORK, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT BURIED ON A PERSON PAGE.**

*[The marriage of 9 June 1774 calls its groom](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774)* «**q.ᵐ Leonardi filius**». *This page published that, this morning, against* **the Leonardus who died in 1773** *— flagged* **inf**, *because [that year comes off a family tree and nothing else](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-1697/).*
> ***A man marrying in 1774 whose father died in 1751 is a man of twenty-three or more.*** *The word* «q.ᵐ» *fits the 1751 Leonardo exactly as well —* **and he is the one with a document.**

**So the archive has two candidate fathers and is choosing neither.** *No parent is attached to the groom, the morning's sentence is left standing with the objection under it, and [the rule that a correction is a claim and must be verified as hard as the thing it corrects](/method/) is why this is published as a weakening rather than a swap.*

⚠ **And the reading itself needed the magnification.** *At page scale the year under 2 November looked like* «177—», *which would have made it the 1773 Leonardus and the morning's identification* **doc**. *At eight times it is* **1751**. ***That is the sixth first impression today that did not survive being enlarged***, *and the first one that would have produced a false confirmation rather than a false discovery.*
# ⭐⭐⭐ And April gave a death, a father, a house — and the control that makes the rest of it usable

> **20.** · Lorenzo Cirich — *1701* · Mattio Muca Possin — *1705* · ***Margarita figlia q. Sig.ʳ Giuseppe Defranceschi, N.º 36*** — ***1783***

> **26.** · Santina moglie q. Andrea Gabaro — *1728* · ***Santina Defranceschi, cœlibe, N.º 36, d'anni 58*** — ***1792***

*(M01069209.)*
## ⭐⭐ The second one is the control, and it is the more important

**[Sancta's burial is already in this archive](/person/sancta-defranceschi-d1792/)**, *from the other death register:* «[domus] **36** · **26 aprilis** [1792] · SANCTA DEFRANCESCHI, **CŒLEBS** · annorum **58** · febris putrida».

***The calendar matches it in every particular — day, year, age, status, house — from a different book, in a different language.*** **A finding aid compiled after the fact has to be tested on a case you can check, before its uncheckable cases are believed.** *This one passes, and that is what licenses the rest of this page: [the* **1797** *for the priest against the register's bracketed* **[1798]**](/person/joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica/), *and the* **1751** *for [Leonardo](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-the-elder-gologorica/), neither of which can be checked against anything else.*
## ⭐ And Margarita, who this morning had nothing
**[Her row was a name, two tree years and no document of any kind.](/person/margarita-defranceschi-1747/)** *This afternoon it gained a marriage she witnessed in 1782. Now it has her death.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **died** | **20 April 1783** ⚠ *[the register says the* **22nd**](/corrections/) |
| **father** | «**q. Sig.ʳ Giuseppe Defranceschi**» — *already dead.* **inf**: *[the Josephus who died in 1782](/person/josephus-defranceschi-1722/), whose entire row was the single word* «Dominus», *and who now has a daughter* |
| **house** | **36** — *the same door as [Joannes Baptista and Catharina](/person/catharina-defranceschi-jablich-gologorica/) and [Sancta](/person/sancta-defranceschi-d1792/)* |
| **⭐ «figlia»** | ***she was BORN a Defranceschi*** — *[which this page listed as unsettled four hours ago](/gologorica-line/#parochus1782)* |

**⚠ And it corrects a sentence published this afternoon.** *Her row said she was* «dead within fourteen months» *of the witnessing.* ***It was five months and eleven days*** — *the fourteen was the distance to the end of a bare tree year with no month in it.* **[Corrected](/corrections/), with [a method row](/method/): a tree year is an interval, and subtracting a real date from it silently turns it into a point.**

**⭐ The book now stands at thirteen openings read of about nineteen** — *January to December with gaps at M01069200–202, 210, 211, 213, 215 and 216.* **In those thirteen it has given this archive six Defranceschi entries**, *four of them for people who had no document at all.* ⚠ *And still* **nil on the Grah**.
# ⭐⭐⭐ The harvest, after sixteen openings of nineteen

| died | the entry | frame |
|---|---|---|
| **30 Aug 1709** | «Vittoria **figlia q.** Gio: Battà Defranceschi» | M01069215 |
| **20 May 1720** | «Lucia **moglie di q.** Gio: Batta Defranceschi» | M01069210 |
| **11 Sep 174—** | «Gio: Battà Defranceschi … **d'an: 70**» | M01069216 |
| **2 Nov 1751** | «**Leonardo** Defranceschi» | M01069219 |
| **13 Nov 1755** | «**Matteo figlio q. Leonardo** Defranceschi» | M01069219 |
| **30 Sep 170—** | «**Pietro** Defranceschi» | M01069217 |
| **8 Sep 1781** | «**Sig.ʳ Giovanni Pietro** Defranceschi, **N.º 36**, d'anni **86½**» | M01069216 |
| **20 Apr 1783** | «**Margarita figlia q. Sig.ʳ Giuseppe** Defranceschi, **N.º 36**» | M01069209 |
| **26 Apr 1792** | «Santina Defranceschi, **cœlibe**, N.º 36, d'anni 58» · ***control*** | M01069209 |
| **29 Mar 1797** | «**Rev.ᵈᵒ Sig.ʳ Gio: Mattia** Defranceschi, **Paroco del luogo**, d'anni 66» | M01069207 |
| **17 Sep 1802** | «Antonio Defranceschi, N.º 29, **q. Leonardo**, d'anni 60» · ***control*** | M01069216 |
| **26 Aug 1804** | «**Signora Ellena Ved.ª q. Gius.ᵉ** Defranceschi, d'anni 84» · ***control*** | M01069215 |
## ⭐⭐ Three of those are controls, and they are why the other nine can be used

**[Sancta 1792](/person/sancta-defranceschi-d1792/), [Antonio 1802](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1742/) and [Hellena 1804](/person/helena-defranceschi-1725/) are deaths this archive already holds from the other register.** ***The calendar matches all three in every particular — day, year, age, status, house — from a different book in a different language.*** *A finding aid compiled after the fact must be tested on cases you can check before its uncheckable ones are believed.* **Three for three.**

**⭐ And two of the controls give something the Latin register did not:** *Antonio is* «**q. Leonardo**», *a son of a late Leonardo — [which the burial entry never says and which complicates what this archive had read from the death index](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1742/).*
## ⭐⭐ What it does to the oldest end of the roster

| | before today | now |
|---|---|---|
| **[Gian Battista](/person/gian-giovanni-ivan-battista-defranceschi-1673/)** *1673–1743* | *a tree row, note empty* | *died* **11 September**, ***aged 70*** — *the age confirms both tree years* |
| **[Pietro](/person/pietro-defranceschi-1695/)** *1695–1781* | *a tree row, note empty* | «**Sig.ʳ Giovanni Pietro**», *died* **8 September 1781**, ***aged 86½***, *house* **36** |
| **[Margarita](/person/margarita-defranceschi-1747/)** *d. 1783* | *a tree year* | *died* **22 April** *(the calendar said the 20th)*, *father* **q. Sig.ʳ Giuseppe**, *house* **36** |
| **[Josephus](/person/josephus-defranceschi-1722/)** *1722–1782* | *the single word* «Dominus» | ***a daughter*** |
| **[Leonardus the elder](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-the-elder-gologorica/)** | *a name, no dates* | *died* **2 November 1751**, *and ***a son*** |

**⭐⭐ AND IT JOINS TWO ROWS THAT HAVE NEVER MET.** *[The archive holds a* **Joannes Petrus Defranceschi** *who stands godparent at Gračišće in 1744, 1747 and 1750 and whose row says in terms* «no parents, age or house are attached to him on any of the three entries»](/person/joannes-petrus-defranceschi-gologorica/).* ***«Sig.ʳ Giovanni Pietro Defranceschi, N.º 36, d'anni 86½» is Joannes Petrus.*** *He was* **49, 52 and 55** *at those three fonts.* ⚠ **inf**, *and the rows are not merged — the join rests on a distinctive double forename, one parish and an age that fits.*
## ⭐ And a household a generation older than anything here

> **30 August 1709** · «Vittoria **figlia q.** Gio: Battà Defranceschi»
> **20 May 1720** · «Lucia **moglie di q.** Gio: Batta Defranceschi»

***A daughter and a wife, eleven years apart, each calling the same man dead.*** **So [a Giovanni Battista Defranceschi was dead at Gologorica before August 1709](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-of-gologorica-d-by-1709/)** — *and he is* **not** *[the Gio: Battà who died in the 1740s aged seventy](/person/gian-giovanni-ivan-battista-defranceschi-1673/), who was alive throughout.* ***Two Giovanni Battista Defranceschi at Gologorica, a generation apart*** — *which is [this village's standing warning](/gologorica-line/) arriving now inside the archive's own surname instead of beside it.*
## ⚠ And one row-level problem the sweep exposed

*[Hellena, widow of the late Josephus, died 26 August 1804 aged 84](/person/helena-defranceschi-1725/) — two registers now say so.* ***The archive wrote that up on a row carrying* 1725–1809, *while a second row carrying exactly* 1720–1804 *sits beside it with no note at all.*** **[Flagged on both, merged on neither](/person/ellena-defranceschi-1720/)** — *identity here is by record.*
**⚠ Sixteen openings of about nineteen; M01069200–202 are unread.** *And across every one of them,* **still not a single Grah.**
# ⚠⚠ And then the title page, which was three openings further back the whole time

> «**Catalogus mortuorum in Parochia Gollogoritiæ ADULTORUM, ab anno Christianæ 1646 usque ad nostra tempora, ex antiquis et recentioribus paginis COACTUS A ME ANTONIO FERDINANDO M[?]OCOVRICH, PAROCHO LOCI, Anno Domini 1800.**»

*— «Catalogue of the dead* **adults** *of the parish of Gologorica, from the year 1646 down to our own times,* **gathered by me**, *Antonio Ferdinando M[?]ocovrich, parish priest of this place,* **out of the old and the more recent pages**, *in the year 1800.»* ⚠ *The compiler's surname is read* «Mocovrich» *and the initial letter is not certain.* *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01069202, the title page.)*
**Two things in one sentence, and the first is a correction of this page.**
## ⚠ 1. «Three controls, three passes» proved much less than it said

***The calendar was compiled in 1800 out of the registers.*** *So for everything before 1800 it is a* **copy of the very book the controls compared it to**. **Sancta, Antonio and Hellena agreeing is not three sources agreeing — it is one source and two copies of it.**

*What the controls do show is that* **Antonio Ferdinando copied accurately**, *which is worth having: it is why the nine entries that* **cannot** *be checked — 1709, 1720, the 1740s, 1751, 1755, 1781, 1783 — can be used at all, since the registers they came out of are not in this archive's hands.* ***But the claim as published was too strong and [is corrected](/corrections/).***

**⚠ It also shrinks the argument for the priest's 1797.** *[This page said the calendar's year is* «explicit where the register's* **[1798]** *was editorial»](/person/joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica/).* **Both are readings of one register** — *one by a modern archive off a page heading, one by his own successor in 1800 off the entry, with the memory of the man to help him and a hundred and fifty years of copying to hinder him.* ***Neither figure moves.***
## ⭐⭐ 2. «ADULTORUM» — and this one changes how every nil here should be read

***The catalogue is of adults only.*** **So the sixteen-opening nil on the Grah is a nil for adult Grah**, *and a family that buried only children at Gologorica would not appear in this book at all.* *The same qualification applies to the absence of [Josephus 1782 and Gisanna 1774](/worklist/) from the openings read, and to any future nil taken here.*

**⭐ And it tells the reader what the book is for.** *A parish priest in 1800 sat down with* «the old and the more recent pages» *and rebuilt a hundred and fifty-four years of his parish's dead as a calendar of anniversaries.* ***What he made is, for the years before 1784, the only surviving digest of registers this archive cannot otherwise reach*** — *and that, not independence, is its value.*

houselist1770.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ A numbered list of every house in the village, dated by its own strikings to 1 July 1770 — and the Defranceschi are at 45 and 46
houselist1770.lead: **[This archive has spent weeks on Gologorica's house numbers](/worklist/)** — *casa 31, index N.º 12, house 36, house 17, house 29, [a renumbering that turned out to be many-to-one](/gologorica-line/#renumber), and [a warning published this afternoon that two systems carry the same figures](/worklist/).* ***The list the numbers came from has been on the reel the whole time, inside a frame range labelled* «Rođeni 1770–1781».***
paras:
> «**Nota delle Case abitate, e disabitate nel Territorio, e nel nostro Luoco di Gollogorizza**»

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068956–M01068958.)*

**It runs from 1 to about 130**, *one line per house, in Italian:* **a number, then the head of the household by surname and forename**, *often with a patronymic or a byname —* «Zabran Matthias q.ᵐ Lucæ», «Udovicich alias Juffinich Matthias» — *and against the empty ones the single word* «**Disabitata**».

**Each line carries a second, smaller figure, and it is not a second house number.** *It skips every* «Disabitata». ***It is an ordinal counting the INHABITED houses only*** — *so house* **45** *is the* **35th** *inhabited house and house* **46** *is the* **36th**. ⚠ *That matters, because a* **36** *written beside a Defranceschi is exactly the kind of figure this archive would otherwise have read as a house number — [and it has two of those already](/worklist/).*
## ⭐⭐ And two of the lines are ours

> **45** ⁽³⁵⁾ · Defranceschi — ~~**Leonardus**~~ **Antonius**
> **46** ⁽³⁶⁾ · Defranceschi — ~~**Joannes [Baptista]**~~ **Josephus**

***The first name in each line is struck through and the successor written over it.*** **So this is not a snapshot — it was kept up**, *and it records a handover in both houses:* **Leonardus → Antonius** *at 45, and* **Joannes Baptista → Josephus** *at 46.*

**⭐ And the first of those is a succession this archive reached by a different road today.** *[The obit calendar gives* «**Antonio Defranceschi, N.º 29, q. Leonardo**, d'anni 60 — 1802»](/person/antonius-defranceschi-1742/) — ***Antonius, son of the late Leonardo.*** *Here is the same pair as father and successor in a house.* ⚠ *Different number — 29 there, 45 here — which is [the renumbering problem](/gologorica-line/#renumber), not a contradiction.*

⚠ **And it touches the 1774 marriage, carefully.** *[That groom is* «Joannes Baptista Defranceschi **q.ᵐ Leonardi filius**»](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774). *If house 45 is the Leonardus house and Antonius is the son who followed him there, **the 1774 groom and Antonius are both sons of a late Leonardus*** — *which makes them brothers, or makes* «Leonardus» *commoner here than one household.* **Nothing is attached: [the archive already holds two candidate Leonardi](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-the-elder-gologorica/) and this list names neither's dates.**
## ⭐⭐ What the item actually is, and the frame map does not say
**The whole composite — M01068953–M01069007 — is one administrative project with a single start date.**

| frames | what |
|---|---|
| **M01068956–958** | ***the house list***, 1–130, inhabited and uninhabited |
| **M01068958–959** | *three blank printed return-forms* — «Formolare … dei **Battezzati**», «… dei **Copulati**», «… dei **Morti**» — *ruled* «Delle Case · Maschi · Femine» |
| **M01068959–** | «**Notatio Baptizatorum Masculorum a 1ᵐᵒ Julij 1770 in Parochia Gollogorizziæ**», *with a column headed* «**Ex Domo sub Numero**» |
| **M01068997–** | «**Notatio Personarum Matrimonio junctarum a 1ᵐᵃ Julij 1770**» |

***Both registers begin on the same day: 1 July 1770.*** **And both are keyed to the house numbers in the list at the front.** ⚠ *A reader may recognise the shape of the Habsburg house-numbering and conscription returns of 1770–71; this page notes the resemblance and claims nothing from it, because [the list carries no date of its own](/worklist/) and the identification would need the decree, not a likeness.*
## ⚠ What is NOT known, and it is the thing that matters
**The list carries no year in its heading** — *and it did not need one.* ***It is dated by the one thing about it that first looked like a complication: the strikings.***
## ✔ THE TEST, AND IT PASSED ON THE FIRST TRY

*[The baptisms that begin behind this list on 1 July 1770 carry their own column](/searched/),* «**Ex Domo sub Numero**». **So the list can be tested against the register it sits in front of.** *Two entries, taken from the register's first page:*

| the baptism says | the list says | |
|---|---|---|
| «Michael **Joannis Udovicich**» · *Ex Domo* **5** | **5** · «Udovicich alias Juffinich Matthias» | *same surname* ✓ |
| «Josephus **Joannis Udovicich**» · *Ex Domo* **128** | **128** · «~~Udovicich~~ **Joannes Giacotich**» | ***the STRUCK name is the register's family*** ✓✓ |

**✔✔ The second row is the proof, and it is better than a plain match.** *At house 128 the list's original entry was* **Udovicich** *— struck, and* **Giacotich** *written over it.* ***The baptism register, in 1770, puts a Udovicich at 128.*** **So the list was written in the register's own numbering and updated afterwards** — *which is exactly what a document begun with the register and kept up for years would look like.*
> ***The list is the numbering of 1 July 1770.***

⚠ *The house-5 row is the weaker of the two: same surname, different forename —* «Matthias» *in the list,* «Joannis» *as the baptised child's father. Brothers in one house, or a head recorded at a different moment. **It agrees; it does not prove.** The 128 row does.*
## ⭐⭐ So what this fixes, and what it does not

**✔ FIXED.** ***In the numbering of 1 July 1770 the Defranceschi are at houses 45 and 46***, *and every house number in [the baptisms of 1770–1781](/gologorica-line/) and [the marriages of the same item](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774) can be read against a named household.*

⚠ **NOT fixed, and this is the part to keep hold of.** *It says nothing yet about* «**domus 36**» *in the death register of 1784–1880, «**casa 31**» in the baptisms of 1785, «**N.º 12**» in the death index, «**house 17**» in 1813 or «**N.º 29**» in 1802.* ***Those are later numberings and [the renumbering between them is many-to-one](/gologorica-line/#renumber).*** **What the archive has now is a dated baseline at one end of the problem, where before it had numbers and no document.**

**But it is the first document in this archive that states the numbering rather than using it**, *and [the registers it sits in front of carry the same numbers in a ruled column](/gologorica-line/).* **[The work it opens is on the list.](/worklist/)**
# ✔✔ And the sweep's FIRST hit landed on the predicted house

*[Worklist 220 set the job](/worklist/): sweep the* «**Ex Domo sub Numero**» *column of the 1770–1781 baptisms for* **45** *and* **46**. *The register turns out to be only eight frames —* **M01068959–M01068966** — *and it was swept.*

> **45** · «***Joannes Petrus Defranceschi, filius legitimus Joannis Bapt[istæ] Defranceschi et ejus uxoris Theresiæ***, *baptizatus est a me* **Marco Bancich, Parocho hujus Loci**; *patrini fuerunt* **Rev.ᵈᵒ D. Mathias Baxa, Canonicus Titularis Cathedralis Eccl. Petinensis**, *et* **Marianna filia Domini Josephi Defranceschi**» — **2 July 1780**

*(doc — M01068965.)*
**✔ The house number is 45, which is what the list said it would be.** *That is the list's dating confirmed a second time, from the other direction.*
**⭐⭐ And the entry is three findings at once.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **[Joannes Petrus](/person/joannes-petrus-defranceschi-1780/)** | ***a son of [the weaver's marriage of 1774](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774)***, *new to this archive, six years into the marriage and the eldest of their children it holds* |
| **[Marianna](/person/marianna-defranceschi-fl-1780/)** | «filia Domini Josephi Defranceschi» — ***a second daughter for [the man whose whole row was the word* «Dominus» *this morning](/person/josephus-defranceschi-1722/)***, *joining [Margarita](/person/margarita-defranceschi-1747/)* |
| **Mathias Baxa** | *a* **titular canon of Pedena cathedral** *standing godfather in a village of a hundred and thirty houses* |

**⚠ And house 45 in 1780 against casa 31 in 1785.** *[The same couple's later children are entered at* «casa 31»](/person/franciscus-antonius-defranceschi-1785/). ***One household, two numbers, five years apart.*** **That is [the renumbering](/gologorica-line/#renumber) caught in the act between two documents for the first time** — *and it is recorded as a question. Noticing it is not solving it.*
## ⭐⭐ ⚠ And the register's last entry names a Defranceschi canon of Pedena
> «*Michael Gasparich … baptizatus est* ***a Rev.ᵐᵒ D. MATHIA DEFRANCESCHI, CANONICO TITULARI Ecclesiæ CATHEDRALIS PETENENSIS***» — **17 September**, *1781 by position* · *(M01068966)*

**[The archive has wanted a named handle on the Pedena cathedral chapter since the Count Damian entry of 1720](/worklist/)**, *and [worklist 212 is an errand drafted to go looking for one](/worklist/).* ***Here is one, and it carries this surname.***

**⚠⚠ The objection, and it is serious.** *Fourteen months earlier the same register gives the same title to a different man:* «Rev.ᵈᵒ D. **Mathias BAXA**, Canonicus Titularis Cathedralis Eccl. Petinensis». ***Two men, both Mathias, both styled titular canon of Pedena, in one small parish inside fourteen months.*** *Both words were magnified and they are not the same word —* «Baxa» *is short,* «Defranceschi» *is long with the usual shape —* **so this is not a misreading of one entry.** *Either the chapter had two of that forename, or one entry has the title on the wrong surname.*

⚠ **And whether the canon is [the Gologorica priest](/person/joannes-mathias-franceschi-gologorica/) is *inf*.** *The chronology fits exactly — curate 1768, canon 1781, parish priest 1782 — but neither his obit-calendar line nor his burial mentions a canonry, and [this village has more than one* «De—» *family and repeats its forenames](/corrections/).* **No second row is minted: minting one would assert a second man as confidently as merging would assert a single one.**

bookseries.heading: ⭐⭐ The parish numbered its own registers, and the covers say which book is missing
bookseries.lead: **[The cover of the 1784 baptism book turned out to carry a Roman numeral](/gologorica-line/#french1812)** — «**IV.** LIBER BAPTISATORUM». *That is a cheap thing to test, because a parish that numbers its books tells you, free, whether you are holding all of them.* ***Five covers were opened.***
paras:
| the cover says | the book | frames |
|---|---|---|
| «LIBER BAPTIZATORUM **II.ᵈᵘˢ** … **1764**» | *baptisms* **II** | M01068915–952 |
| «Liber Baptizatorum **III.ᵗⁱᵘˢ** et Mortuorum **II.ᵈᵘˢ**» | *baptisms* **III** *and deaths* **II**, *from* **1 July 1770** | M01068953–1007 |
| «**IV.** LIBER BAPTISATORUM … **ab anno 1784**» | *baptisms* **IV** | M01069008–181 |
| «**Liber Mortuorum Primus**» | *[the obit calendar](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex), compiled* **1800**, *covering from* **1646** | M01069199–223 |
| «Liber Mortuorum **III.ᵗⁱᵘˢ** in Parochia Gollogorizæ ab anno 17[84]» | *deaths* **III** | M01069224–314 |
**✔ The death series is complete on these reels: I, II, III.**
**⚠⚠ The baptism series is not. It runs II, III, IV.** ***Liber Baptizatorum I is not here.***

**That is the book of this parish's baptisms before 1764** — *and [the window the whole Carnian argument turns on, the 1679 return of the Mione headmen naming* «Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo»](/carnia/), *is inside it.* **[This archive already knew Gologorica's early registers were not in its hands](/undigitised/); what it did not have was the parish's own name for the one it is missing.** *A book you can ask for by its number is a different request from* «whatever you have from before 1764».
## ⭐ And one reading, offered as a reading

***«Liber Mortuorum PRIMUS» is the catalogue Mocovich compiled in 1800.*** *A book written in 1800 is shelved as the parish's* **first** *death register — while the deaths of 1770–89 are* **II** *and those from 1784 are* **III**.

**So the numbering is not by when a book was written. It is by what period it covers** — *and the parish gave the earliest slot to a digest rather than to a register.* ***The obvious reading is that the real first death book was already gone by 1800, and [Mocovich's catalogue, compiled* «ex antiquis et recentioribus paginis»](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex), *was shelved in its place.*** ⚠ **That is an inference from a numeral and a date, and nothing on the cover says it.** *But it would explain why a parish priest sat down in 1800 and rebuilt a hundred and fifty-four years of his dead out of older pages: not as an index, as a replacement.*

⚠ **And the frame map does not carry any of this.** *[Three audits yesterday found two books mis-described and one document missing from that table](/corrections/); this is a fourth thing it does not say.* **The frame ranges have been right every time.** *What the table lacks is what the books call themselves* — *and [the books' own title pages have now been wrong-footed the film's printed cards twice](/corrections/).*

zupanwife.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ The župan's widow, dead at ninety and buried inside the church — and the arithmetic of the direct line does not survive her
zupanwife.lead: **[The death register of 1770–1789 was opened](/gologorica-line/#bookseries) to test the house numbering** — *it is the only book that spans the change from [house 45 in 1780](/person/joannes-petrus-defranceschi-1780/) to [casa 31 in 1785](/person/franciscus-antonius-defranceschi-1785/).* ***What it gave instead was the grave of the best-documented woman in this archive's eighteenth century.***
paras:
> **46** · «***Joanna Defranceschi annorum nonaginta circiter, vidua defuncti Supani Joannis Defranceschi***, *munita Sacramentis … per me Parochum hujus Loci* **Marcum Bancich**, *et a me eodem* ***sepulta est 21 in Arca ejusdem existente in hac Parochiali Ecclesia***.»

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068988,* «Liber Mortuorum II», **20 April 1774**.)*

**⚠ THE ŽUPAN IS NOT NEW, AND THIS PAGE IS NOT CLAIMING HIM.** *[He has been on the direct-line page since the Gračišće sweep](/direct-line/) —* «**Ioana Uxor Sup.ⁿⁱ Ioanis Bap.ᵗᵃe Defranceschi**» *standing godmother on 8 January 1733, and* «**Joanna uxor Sup.ⁿⁱ Jo: Baptistæ Defranceschi de Golagoriza**» *again in 1743.* ***What is new is that the same woman now has a death, an age, a house and a tomb.***

| | |
|---|---|
| **died** | **20 April 1774**, *buried the* **21st** |
| **age** | «nonaginta **circiter**» — *about ninety, so born about* **1684** |
| **house** | **46** — *[the second Defranceschi house on the 1770 list](/gologorica-line/#houselist1770), whose struck first head is a* «Joannes» *replaced by* «Josephus» |
| **grave** | «**in Arca ejusdem existente in hac Parochiali Ecclesia**» — ***in the household's own chest-tomb, inside the church*** |

**⭐ And it documents [a row that was a name and two tree years](/person/gisanna-defranceschi-1684/).** «**Gisanna** Defranceschi, 1684–1774», *source* `myheritage`, *note empty.* ***Both years are confirmed by a single entry, and* «Gisanna» *turns out to be* «Joanna».*** *[One of the six people this archive could only date from a family tree yesterday morning.](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex)*

**⭐⭐ A tomb inside the church is the social fact here.** *[Everyone else on these pages is* «in hoc Parochiali Cœmeterio»](/gologorica-line/) — *in the churchyard.* ***This household had an* arca *under the floor of the parish church, and the register says it was theirs.*** *That is what a župan's family looked like from the outside, and it sits beside [the conditio column at Gračišće entering these people* «Cives»](/gologorica-line/) *rather than* «rustici».
# ⚠⚠ And then the arithmetic

**[The Zagreb librarians' account of the family archive makes the župan's son* **Gian Pietro**, *the Belgian lord's tax-collector](/direct-line/).** *And [yesterday this archive identified that man](/person/pietro-defranceschi-1695/) as* «**Sig.ʳ Giovanni Pietro Defranceschi, N.º 36, d'anni 86½**», *dead* **8 September 1781** — *born about* **March 1695**.
> ***A woman born about 1684 cannot be the mother of a man born about 1695. She would have been eleven.***

**Three things could be true, and this page chooses none of them:**

1. *The* «**circiter**» *is doing heavy work and her age is loose by a decade —* ⚠ *but even at eighty she is born 1694, which does not help.*
2. **She is a later wife**, *and Gian Pietro is the župan's son by an earlier marriage.* ***This is the reading that costs nothing and explains everything***, *and it is still a reading.*
3. *The* «**86½**» *of 1781 belongs to a different Giovanni Pietro, and [yesterday's join of the Gračišće godparent to the tree row](/person/joannes-petrus-defranceschi-gologorica/) — which was published as* **inf** *— is wrong.*

**⚠ No parentage is attached to anybody on the strength of this.** ***What is recorded is that the archive's best-attested eighteenth-century household has a join in it that does not add up***, *and that the entry which exposes it is the first one ever read from this book.* **[A household reconstructed from three sources can still be arithmetically impossible, and nobody notices until a fourth source gives somebody an age.](/method/)**

margaretta1783.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ The archpriest of Krbune came back to bury her — and the register unmakes three things this archive published yesterday
margaretta1783.lead: **[The same death book that gave up the župan's widow](/gologorica-line/#zupanwife) runs on to 1783** — *which is where [Margaretta Defranceschi, whose row was a name and two tree years until yesterday](/person/margarita-defranceschi-1747/), should be.* ***She is, and almost nothing this archive said about her survives the entry.***
paras:
> «**Die 22. Aprilis anno 1783.** ***Margaretta Ancilla annorum 22, mensium 9, filia Josephi et Hellenæ jugalium de Franceschi***, *provisa Sacramentis omnibus in sua infirmitate a me Parocho; obdormivit in Domino, cujus corpus die* **25** *ejusdem mensis sepultum est* ***in Arca Parentuum*** *per R.ᵐᵘˢ* ***Archipresbiterum et Parochum CHERBUNÆ D.ⁿᵘˢ Joanes Gràch***.»

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068991,* «Liber Mortuorum II», **22 April 1783**.)*
# ⭐⭐ First, the man who buried her
**«*per* R.ᵐᵘˢ Archipresbiterum et Parochum CHERBUNÆ D.ⁿᵘˢ Joanes Gràch»** — ***the archpriest and parish priest of Krbune.***

*[Yesterday this archive found him for the first time, marrying a Defranceschi to a Grah of Krbune at Gologorica on 9 June 1774](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774), and [it already had him standing godfather at a Gologorica font on 13 April 1785](/person/franciscus-antonius-defranceschi-1785/).* ***Here he is a third time, in 1783, burying a Defranceschi daughter.***

| | |
|---|---|
| **9 June 1774** | *marries* [Joannes Baptista to Theresia Grah](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774) |
| **25 April 1783** | ***buries Margaretta Defranceschi*** |
| **13 April 1785** | *stands godfather to* [Franciscus Antonius](/person/franciscus-antonius-defranceschi-1785/) |

***Three rites in eleven years, all at Gologorica, all for this family, by the archpriest of a parish four kilometres away.*** **That is not a man passing through.** *[The Grach of Krbune married into this household in 1774](/married-in/); the archpriest is their kinsman; and he kept coming.* ⚠ *What it is not: evidence about where the Grach lived. [Krbune's own register, 1803–1870, has no Grah in it at all](/searched/).*
# ⚠ And then what it does to yesterday's work

| | published yesterday | the register |
|---|---|---|
| **died** | **20 April** *(the obit calendar)* | ***22 April***, *buried the* **25th** |
| **age** | *about* **35**, *from [the tree's 1747](/person/margarita-defranceschi-1747/)* | ***22 years 9 months*** → *born about* **July 1760** |
| **her mother** | **inf** | ***doc*** — «filia Josephi **et Hellenæ** jugalium» |
| **her grave** | — | ***in Arca Parentuum*** — *her parents' tomb, inside the church* |

**⚠⚠ THE CALENDAR IS TWO DAYS OUT, AND THAT IS NOW A MEASURED THING.** *[It was published yesterday as passing three controls, then corrected to* «it is a copy, so the controls prove less»](/corrections/).* ***This is the first case where the copy can be checked against the book it copied, and it is wrong.*** **Not a reason to stop using it** — *[for 1646–1770 it is the only route there is](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex)* — *but every date out of it now carries a tolerance, and where the register survives the register wins.* **[Corrected in every file that asserted the 20th.](/corrections/)**

**⚠ The tree is thirteen years out on her birth**, *and that is worth more than the date:* ***[five of the six people this archive could only date from that tree](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex) have now been checked against a register, and this is the first one the tree got badly wrong.***

⚠ **«Ancilla» is left as the register writes it.** *The word is* **maidservant**, *which sits oddly on a daughter of a* «Dominus»; *it is capitalised like a name.* **This archive does not know which it is and has not let either reading into her row.**

⚠ **And the register does not call her father dead.** «filia **Josephi** et Hellenæ **jugalium**» — *no* «quondam» — *where [the 1800 calendar writes* «figlia **q.** Sig.ʳ Giuseppe»](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex) *and [the tree kills him in 1782](/person/josephus-defranceschi-1722/).* ***A scribe in April 1783 would normally mark a dead father.*** **Flagged, not resolved** — *an omitted* «q.» *is a thinner thing than a date, and [this archive has no document for his death at all](/person/josephus-defranceschi-1722/).*

sterilis1783.heading: ⭐⭐ «1783. Sterilis et fames» — the priest headed the year, and the 1773 that should hold Leonardus holds nobody
sterilis1783.lead: **[«Liber Mortuorum II» was opened for the house numbers](/gologorica-line/#zupanwife) and has been read forward.** *Three things came out of the years between 1773 and 1783, and the first is two words.*
paras:
> «**1783. Sterilis et fames.**»

*—* «**Barren, and famine.**» *(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068991, the year-heading in the parish priest's hand.)*

***He did not write a year. He wrote a verdict on one.*** *[This archive already holds the famine of 1815 and the hunger of 1817 from the later death book](/gologorica-line/); **1783 is new**, and it is the first of them written as a heading rather than inferred from a column of causes.*

**⭐ And it is the year [Margaretta Defranceschi died at twenty-two](/gologorica-line/#margaretta1783)** — *on 22 April,* «provisa Sacramentis omnibus in sua infirmitate». ***The register does not say she starved and this page does not either.*** *It says what year she died in, and the priest wrote what kind of year it was.*
## ⚠⚠ And 1773, which should hold Leonardus, holds nobody

**[The family tree gives Leonardus Defranceschi a death in 1773](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-1697/)**, *and [the marriage of 9 June 1774 says the groom's father Leonardus was already dead](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774). So this register — kept by the same parish priest, Marcus Bancich, through both years — is where he should be.*

**The 1773 deaths, read in full:** *7 March (Helena, 2) · 12 March (Maria, c. 50) · 4 May (Mathia, the judge's wife) · 3 July (Lucia, 9) · 1 August (Maria, c. 40) · 12 September (Antonia Radde, 8) · 13 October (Oliva Flegar, c. 30) · 27 November (Matthia Stosich, c. 60).*
> ***Eight deaths. Not one of them a Defranceschi.***

**⚠ So the tree's 1773 has no support in the parish's own death register**, *and [the obit calendar — the other death book — gives a Leonardo Defranceschi dying on 2 November* **1751**, *not 1773](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-the-elder-gologorica/).*

***That makes the 1751 Leonardo the stronger candidate for the father of the 1774 groom***, *where [yesterday the two stood level](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774).* ⚠ **It does not make him certain.** *A man can die outside his parish; a register can drop an entry; and* **eight deaths in a year is a low count for a village of a hundred and thirty houses**, *which is itself a reason to distrust the book's completeness before distrusting the tree.* **No parent is attached, and the 1773 reading is weakened rather than withdrawn.**
## ⭐ And the Defranceschi priest is four months earlier again

*[Yesterday his earliest sighting as* **Parochus** *was 11 July 1782](/gologorica-line/#parochus1782).* **This book has him signing the deaths from 13 March 1782** — «*provisa Sacramentis …* **per me Parochum Franceschi**» — *and again on 22 March as* «**per me Parochum Mathia Franceschi**», *in May as* «**Parochum Franceschi**», *and on 20 September signing off* «*per me Parochum hujusdem Loci* **M. Franceschi**».

***Six, seven and eight attestations of the name, in one book, in one year.*** **His tenure now starts 13 March 1782** — ⚠ *[with the standing caveat that a Deprato wears the same style three weeks from one of his entries](/corrections/).*

**⭐ One more thing the book gives free: this parish's burial topography.** *The entries distinguish* «**in hoc Parochiali Cœmeterio**» *from* «**in Crypta Infantium**» *— a children's crypt — from* «**in tumulo apud Ecclesiam Parochialem**», «**ante Portam Majoris**», *and* «**in Arca**». ***Five different places to be buried in one small parish, and which one you got says something about who you were.*** *[The Defranceschi are in the Arca.](/gologorica-line/#zupanwife)* *And the church is named:* «**Ecclesiam S. Petri et Pauli**».

textorexcarnia.heading: ⭐⭐⭐ «TEXTOR EX CARNIA» — the parish register says it, in 1773, of a named man
textorexcarnia.lead: **Everything this archive has argued about Carnia has rested on documents from somewhere else** — *[the 1679 return of the Mione headmen](/carnia/), [the Svetvinčenat marriages of Carnians](/lines/), [the Zagreb librarians' account](/direct-line/), [Carlo's letter to Kobler](/carlos-letter/).* ***No Gologorica register had ever used the word.*** **This one does, in the death entry of the man whose son married in 1774.**
paras:
> «**45** · ***Die 14 Martij obijt*** · ***Leonardus Defranceschi annorum septuaginta sex***, *provisus Sacramento Pœnitentiæ per me* **Marcum Bancich Parochum**, *sepultus vero est* **15** *in* ***Arca D.ⁿⁱ Petri Defranceschi*** *in hoc Parrochiali Ecclesia existente, per me eundem Parrochum.* **( : *professionis suæ* TEXTOR EX CARNIA : )**»

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068977,* «Liber Mortuorum II», *the* **male** *sequence, 14 March 1773. The last six words magnified to nine times before transcription.)*
# ⭐⭐⭐ What it says

| | |
|---|---|
| **who** | **Leonardus Defranceschi**, *of* **house 45** — *[the Defranceschi house on the 1770 list](/gologorica-line/#houselist1770)* |
| **when** | *died* **14 March 1773**, *buried the* **15th** |
| **age** | **seventy-six** → *born about* **1697** |
| **trade** | «***professionis suæ TEXTOR***» — *a weaver* |
| **origin** | «***EX CARNIA***» |
| **grave** | «*in* ***Arca D.ⁿⁱ Petri Defranceschi*** *in hoc Parrochiali Ecclesia existente*» — *in Dominus Petrus Defranceschi's tomb, inside the church* |

**✔ The family tree's [`1697–1773`](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-1697/) is confirmed in both years by one entry** — *an age of seventy-six in March 1773 puts his birth in 1696 or 1697, and the tree says 1697.*
# ⭐⭐ And it makes the 1774 marriage *doc*

*[Nine June 1774:* «**Joannes Baptista Defranceschi q.ᵐ Leonardi filius**, *professionis suæ* **Textor**»](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774). *This archive published that identification as* **inf** *because the father's death rested on a family tree, and [yesterday evening it was weakened further](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex) when a second Leonardo turned up dying in 1751.*
> ***The groom's father died at house 45 on 14 March 1773, fifteen months before the wedding. The son married out of that house. The identification is doc.***

**⭐⭐ AND FATHER AND SON ARE BOTH WEAVERS.** «Textor» *in the father's burial of 1773;* «Textor» *in the son's marriage of 1774.* ***[Yesterday this page argued that one weaver in a parish of* Agricolae *was worth noticing](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774). Two, in one house, across two generations, is a trade descent.***
# ⚠ What «ex Carnia» does and does not prove

**It proves that the man who died at Gologorica house 45 on 14 March 1773 was a weaver and came from Carnia, and that the parish knew it and wrote it down.** ***That is the first time a Gologorica register has placed any Defranceschi outside Istria.***

⚠ **It does not, by itself, reach Mione.** *[The 1679 return names* «Zuane De Franceschi con un suo fiolo» *among the Mione weavers](/carnia/); Carnia is a region with many villages and many weavers, and ninety-four years separate the two documents.* **No join to that household is made here.**

**⭐ But it sits inside a pattern the archive already had, and tightens it:** *[Leonardus's other son Antonio married at Svetvinčenat in 1785](/person/antonio-de-franceschi-q-leonardo-of-gologorica-m-1785-svetvincenat/) —* «**Antonio q. Leonardo de Franceschi da Gollogorizza**» — *to* «**Maria figlia q. Giacomo Corva da MUINA Diocesi d'Udine**». ***A weaver from Carnia dies at Gologorica in 1773, and twelve years later his son goes back to Carnia for a wife.***
# ⚠⚠ And it corrects this archive, twice, inside an hour

**1. «The 1773 register holds nobody» was wrong, and the reason matters.** *[That was published an hour ago](/corrections/) from eight deaths read in full.* ***They were eight* **women**. ***This register, like the baptisms in the same volume, is split by sex*** — «Notatio Baptizatorum **Masculorum**» *and* «**Fœminarum**», *and the deaths follow the same division.* **Leonardus is in the male sequence, forty frames earlier.** *[Corrected.](/corrections/)*

**2. «The 1751 Leonardo is the stronger candidate» is withdrawn.** *He remains [a documented Leonardo Defranceschi](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-the-elder-gologorica/) and nothing about his own entry changes.* ***But the 1774 groom's father is the man of 1773, at the right house, of the right trade, at the right remove.***
# ⭐⭐ And whose tomb it was
*The weaver was buried* «**in Arca D.ⁿⁱ Petri Defranceschi** in hoc Parrochiali Ecclesia existente». **Eight years later the same book buries its owner.**

> «**36.** · ***Die 8 Septembris obijt*** · ***Dominus Joannes Petrus Defranceschi annorum 86, mensium 4***, *provisus in sua infirmitate Sacramentis Pœnitentiæ, Eucharistiæ et Extremæ Unctionis per me* **Marcum Bancich Parochum hujus Loci**; *sepultus est* **9** *in* ***propria Arca ejusdem***, *per D.ⁿᵘᵐ* **Carolum Covas, Canonicum**»

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068980,* «Liber Mortuorum II», *male sequence,* **8 September 1781**.)*
> ***«In propria Arca ejusdem» — in his own tomb. The one Leonardus the weaver had been laid in eight years before.***

**So [the Leonardus of house 45](/person/leonardus-defranceschi-1697/) and [the Dominus Joannes Petrus of house 36](/person/pietro-defranceschi-1695/) share a grave inside the parish church** — *which makes them one kin group across two houses, in a village where [everyone else on these pages goes into the churchyard](/gologorica-line/#sterilis1783).* ⚠ **The register does not say how they were related, and this page does not guess.**

⚠ **And it measures the obit calendar again.** *The calendar gives his age as* «**d'anni 86½**»; *the register says* «**annorum 86, mensium 4**». ***Two months.*** *[After the two days on Margaretta, that is the second checkable discrepancy in the 1800 copy](/corrections/) — **small, consistent, and now quantified: it is reliable to within days-to-months, not to the day.**
# ✔ And the scribe proves the split himself

*[This page corrected itself an hour ago for counting a year's deaths out of half a register](/corrections/) — the volume separates men from women, and the eight 1773 deaths read were eight women.* ***The proof that it does so turns out to be in the book, in the scribe's own hand.***

> «**36** · *Die* **22. Aprilis** *anno quo supra obijt in D.no* ~~*Margaretta*~~ *Ancilla annorum* **22, mensium 9**, *filia* **Josephi et Hellenæ jugalium de Franceschi** … *cujus corpus die* **25** *sepultum est* ***In Arca Parentuum*** *per R.ᵐᵘˢ D.ⁿᵘᵐ Archipresbiterum et Parochum Cherbunæ* **Joannem Grach**» — ***the whole entry struck through with a diagonal.***

*(doc — DAPA* **ZM34K-214**, *M01068982, the* **male** *sequence — cancelled; [the surviving entry is in the female sequence at M01068991](/gologorica-line/#margaretta1783).)*

**He wrote Margaretta into the men's sequence, saw what he had done, struck the entry through, and wrote her again among the women.** ***A cancelled duplicate is better evidence of the division than any heading***, *because it is the rule being enforced rather than announced.*

**⭐ And the cancelled copy carries something the surviving one does not: her house.** «**36**» — *[which is where her mother Hellena died in 1804](/person/helena-defranceschi-1725/), and what [the 1800 obit calendar says](/gologorica-line/#calendarindex).* ***Three sources, one door.***
## ⚠ And it bears on her father's death year
**Both writings of the entry — the struck one and the surviving one — call her** «*filia* **Josephi et Hellenæ JUGALIUM** *de Franceschi*». ***Neither says* «quondam».***
